docs.title: 11.12.4.1. The descriptors
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Business Logic/MetierService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Implementation of the business layer.
//
// The management of doctors and clients follows three management rules:
//
//    1. A person (doctor or client) and their user account will
//       TOUJOURS as a set: they are created, modified, and deleted together, within
//       the same TRANSACTION—either everything succeeds, or nothing is written;
//    2. The login is unique throughout the application, and two doctors (or
//       two clients) cannot have the same first and last names;
//    3. Deletion:
//       - A MÉDECIN with appointments cannot be deleted (their
//         patients would lose their appointments without being notified): you must
//         cancel them first. Its time slots disappear along with it;
//       - a CLIENT, on the other hand, disappears along with TOUS its appointments (past and
//         future) — regardless of whether the deletion is initiated by the ADMIN or the patient
//         himself.
//
// And two rules for scheduling appointments, regardless of the role of
// the person making the reservation (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient themselves):
//    4. No appointments in the past;
//    5. A patient may have only one upcoming appointment at a time.
//
// Doctors and clients follow exactly the same rules: the common code
// is written UNE times (generic private methods XxxPersonneAsync<T>), and
// is configured by a small "descriptor" that specifies what kind of person we are
// dealing with.
// =========================================================================

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using MySqlConnector;
using RdvMedecins.Data;
using RdvMedecins.Domain;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Repositories;

namespace RdvMedecins.Metier;

public class MetierService : IMetier
{
     // number of bcrypt salt rounds—the same as in the script SQL ($2b$10$...)
    private const int ToursBcrypt = 10;

     // everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client for management rules.
     // "where T : Person, new()": T is a Person, and we can write new T().
    private record DescripteurPersonne<T>(
        PersonneRepository<T> Dao,
        Role Role, // DOCTOR or USER
        string CleIntrouvable, // message if the person does not exist
        string CleExisteDeja, // message if the same first and last names already exist
         // optional: if present, the deletion is REFUSÉE as long as the
         // person has appointments (CompterRv > 0), with the message CleAvecRv
        Func<int, Task<int>>? CompterRv = null,
        string? CleAvecRv = null,
         // optional: what to delete for the person (the rows that
         // refer to it via a foreign key)
        Func<int, Task>? AvantSuppression = null) where T : Personne, new();

    private readonly RdvMedecinsDbContext db;
    private readonly MedecinRepository medecinRepository;
    private readonly ClientRepository clientRepository;
    private readonly CreneauRepository creneauRepository;
    private readonly RvRepository rvRepository;
    private readonly UserRepository userRepository;
    private readonly DescripteurPersonne<Medecin> medecinDescripteur;
    private readonly DescripteurPersonne<Client> clientDescripteur;

     // all dependencies are provided by dependency injection
     // from ASP.NET Core (see Program.cs). DbContext is not used here to open
     // transactions—the requests themselves remain in the DAO layer.
    public MetierService(
        RdvMedecinsDbContext db,
        MedecinRepository medecinRepository,
        ClientRepository clientRepository,
        CreneauRepository creneauRepository,
        RvRepository rvRepository,
        UserRepository userRepository)
    {
        this.db = db;
        this.medecinRepository = medecinRepository;
        this.clientRepository = clientRepository;
        this.creneauRepository = creneauRepository;
        this.rvRepository = rvRepository;
        this.userRepository = userRepository;

        medecinDescripteur = new DescripteurPersonne<Medecin>(
            medecinRepository,
            Role.DOCTOR,
            "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND",
            "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS",
            CompterRv: rvRepository.CountByMedecinAsync,
            CleAvecRv: "ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS",
             // A walk-in clinic may still have available time slots:
             // they no longer make sense without it, so they are deleted along with it (otherwise
             // the foreign key creneaux.id_medecin would prevent the deletion)
            AvantSuppression: creneauRepository.DeleteByMedecinAsync);

        clientDescripteur = new DescripteurPersonne<Client>(
            clientRepository,
            Role.USER,
            "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND",
            "ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS",
             // no CompterRv: deleting a client is never denied;
             // their appointments (past and future) are deleted along with them (otherwise
             // the foreign key rv.id_client would prevent deletion)
            AvantSuppression: rvRepository.DeleteByClientAsync);
    }
  • lines 6–29: The header comment summarizes the five business rules applied by the class;
  • line 34: the [MySQL] driver (see Chapter 9): the class uses its [MySqlException] exception to detect violations of uniqueness constraints;
  • line 42: the class implements the interface; it must provide all of its methods;
  • line 45: the cost of [bcrypt] (see Example 25), which is the same as that of the passwords in the SQL script (prefix [$2b$10$]);
  • lines 49–60: everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client in terms of business rules: their DAO, their account role ([DOCTOR] or [USER]), their error messages, and what happens when they are deleted. Since doctors and clients follow the same rules, the code for these rules is written only once, in generic methods (parameterized by a [T] type) that accept a descriptor. The constraint [where T : Personne, new()] requires that [T] inherit from [Personne] (we could read [Nom], [Prenom], [User]...) and have a parameterless constructor (we could write [new T()]). [Func<int, Task<int>>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns a [Task<int>]; [Func<int, Task>] is the type of an asynchronous function that returns nothing. These parameters have a default value ([= null]): they are optional;
  • lines 62–69: the class fields: the [DbContext], the five DAO, and the two descriptors. [readonly] prevents them from being modified after the constructor;
  • lines 74–87: all dependencies are provided by dependency injection. The [DbContext] is used here only to open transactions: the requests remain in the DAO layer. As in Example 28, DAO and the business layer receive the same [DbContext] during a query, and thus the same connection and the same transaction;
  • Lines 89–99: the doctor descriptor. The named arguments ([CompterRv:], [CleAvecRv:]...) refer to a parameter by name, which allows optional parameters to be skipped (the client descriptor, further down, thus omits [CompterRv] and [CleAvecRv]). [rvRepository.CountByMedecinAsync] is not called here: the method itself is passed, and it will be called later (a method can thus serve as a value of type [Func]). Deleting a doctor will be denied as long as they have appointments; their time slots, however, will be deleted before the doctor is deleted;
  • Lines 101–109: The client descriptor. No [CompterRv]: Deleting a client is never denied, and its appointments (past and future) are deleted before the client itself; otherwise, the foreign key [rv.id_client] would prevent the deletion.

     // same algorithm as the server JSON (and as the original Spring project)
    public async Task<AgendaMedecinJour?> GetAgendaMedecinJourAsync(int idMedecin, DateOnly jour)
    {
        var medecin = await GetMedecinByIdAsync(idMedecin);
        if (medecin is null)
        {
            return null;
        }
        var creneauxHoraires = await GetAllCreneauxAsync(idMedecin);
        var reservations = await GetRvMedecinJourAsync(idMedecin, jour);
         // slot number -> appointment scheduled for this slot
        var hReservations = reservations.ToDictionary(resa => resa.IdCreneau);
        var creneauxMedecinJour = creneauxHoraires
            .Select(creneau => new CreneauMedecinJour(creneau, hReservations.GetValueOrDefault(creneau.Id)))
            .ToList();
        return new AgendaMedecinJour(medecin, jour, creneauxMedecinJour);
    }
  • lines 5–22: The read operations simply delegate to the DAO layer. The [=> expression] syntax (an expression body) replaces a [{ return expression; }] block. These methods are not [async]: they directly return the [Task] from the DAO, without waiting for it;
  • lines 24–25: a patient’s upcoming appointments: the business layer provides the current date to DAO;
  • lines 28–42: calculation of a doctor’s schedule for a given day, using the same algorithm as the [NestJS] version. An unknown doctor yields [null]; otherwise, the doctor’s time slots and appointments for the day are read;
  • line 38: [ToDictionary] stores the appointments in a dictionary where the key is the slot ID (equivalent to [Map] in the [NestJS] version). The dictionary eliminates the need to scan the list of appointments for each time slot;
  • lines 39–41: Each time slot is associated with its appointment, or with [null] ([GetValueOrDefault] returns the default value, [null], when the key is missing). [Select] transforms each item in a list (see [LINQ], Chapter 9). The result is a [AgendaMedecinJour] object in the [Domain] folder, which the calendar view will display.

docs.title: 11.12.4.3. Scheduling an appointment
docs.text:
// =======================================================================
     // appointment
    // =======================================================================

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // scheduling an appointment, within a transaction:
        // 1. no past appointments;
        // 2. on VERROUILLE the patient’s record (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): if the
           // same patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs,
           // double-click...), the second transaction waits for the
           // first one—and then sees the appointment it just created;
        // 3. only one upcoming appointment per patient;
        // 4. Finally, the insertion. If the time slot has just been booked by a AUTRE
           // patient, it is the constraint SQL unq1_rv (day, id_creneau) that
           // prevents the insertion—translated to MetierException by TransactionAsync.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public Task<Rv> AjouterRvAsync(DateOnly jour, Creneau creneau, Client client) =>
        TransactionAsync(async () =>
        {
            var aujourdhui = Dates.Aujourdhui();
            if (jour < aujourdhui)
            {
                throw new MetierException("ERRORS.PAST_DATE");
            }
            if (await clientRepository.VerrouillerAsync(client.Id) is null)
            {
                throw new MetierException("ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND");
            }
            if (await rvRepository.CountAVenirByClientAsync(client.Id, aujourdhui) > 0)
            {
                throw new MetierException("ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT");
            }
             // we specify the foreign keys: there is no need for Creneau and Client to link the objects
             // "Creneau" and "Client" themselves to write the line [rv]
            var rv = new Rv { Jour = jour, IdCreneau = creneau.Id, IdClient = client.Id };
            return await rvRepository.SaveAsync(rv);
        });

    public Task SupprimerRvAsync(Rv rv) => rvRepository.DeleteByIdAsync(rv.Id);
  • lines 17–18: The entire booking takes place within a single transaction: the method passes an asynchronous anonymous function, [async () => { ... }], to [TransactionAsync] (see below), which performs the task;
  • lines 20–23: no appointments in the past. The rule is verified here regardless of the role of the person making the reservation (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient), even if the web layer has already hidden the “Book” buttons for past dates: a request can be created manually;
  • lines 25–27: the patient’s record is locked: [VerrouillerAsync] executes [SELECT * FROM clients WHERE id = ... FOR UPDATE] (see [Repositories/PersonneRepository.cs]). This is a pessimistic lock: it is acquired before processing begins, assuming a potential conflict, and remains in place until the end of the transaction. Without it, two reservations for the same patient sent at the exact same time (two tabs, a double-click) could both pass the following test before either one has written its appointment to the database. With this lock, the second transaction waits for the first to finish, then sees the appointment it created. A patient who cannot be found (deleted in the meantime) is rejected;
  • lines 29–31: only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • lines 35–36: the insertion. Only the foreign keys [IdCreneau] and [IdClient] are specified: there is no need to link the objects [Creneau] and [Client] to write the row [rv]. If another patient has just booked the same time slot, the lock did not prevent it (the lock applies to the patient’s row): it is the database’s [unq1_rv (jour, id_creneau)] uniqueness constraint that rejects the insertion, and [TransactionAsync] translates the error into [MetierException] with the key [ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED];
  • Line 39: Cancellation of an appointment: a simple [DELETE], with no specific rules.

docs.text:
// =======================================================================
     // doctors and clients—public methods delegate to
     // shared private methods, with the correct descriptor
    // =======================================================================

    public Task<Medecin> AjouterMedecinAsync(DonneesPersonne donnees) => AjouterPersonneAsync(medecinDescripteur, donnees);

    public Task<Medecin> ModifierMedecinAsync(int id, DonneesPersonne donnees) =>
        ModifierPersonneAsync(medecinDescripteur, id, donnees);

    public Task SupprimerMedecinAsync(int id) => SupprimerPersonneAsync(medecinDescripteur, id);

    public Task<Client> AjouterClientAsync(DonneesPersonne donnees) => AjouterPersonneAsync(clientDescripteur, donnees);

    public Task<Client> ModifierClientAsync(int id, DonneesPersonne donnees) =>
        ModifierPersonneAsync(clientDescripteur, id, donnees);

     // the client, their account ET all their appointments (ADMIN, or the patient
     // themselves via “Manage My Account”: same method, same rule)
    public Task SupprimerClientAsync(int id) => SupprimerPersonneAsync(clientDescripteur, id);

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // creation: the user account first (the person references it),
     // then the person—all within the UNE transaction.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private Task<T> AjouterPersonneAsync<T>(DescripteurPersonne<T> d, DonneesPersonne donnees) where T : Personne, new()
    {
        var nom = donnees.Nom.Trim().ToUpperInvariant();
        var prenom = donnees.Prenom.Trim();
         // rules for the dbrdvmedecins2 database: login = name in lowercase,
         // password = login—unless the user has entered others
        var login = (string.IsNullOrEmpty(donnees.Login) ? nom : donnees.Login).ToLowerInvariant();
        var password = string.IsNullOrEmpty(donnees.Password) ? login : donnees.Password;

        return TransactionAsync(async () =>
        {
            await VerifierPersonneUniqueAsync(d, prenom, nom, null);
            await VerifierLoginLibreAsync(login);

            var user = new User
            {
                Login = login,
                Password = BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.HashPassword(password, ToursBcrypt),
                Nom = $"{prenom} {nom}",
                Role = d.Role,
            };
            await userRepository.SaveAsync(user);

            var personne = new T { Titre = donnees.Titre, Nom = nom, Prenom = prenom, User = user };
            return await d.Dao.SaveAsync(personne);
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Change: the user ET must update their account (the displayed name "first name NOM"
     // must follow; the login and password only change if they have been
     // entered).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private Task<T> ModifierPersonneAsync<T>(DescripteurPersonne<T> d, int id, DonneesPersonne donnees)
        where T : Personne, new() =>
        TransactionAsync(async () =>
        {
            var personne = await d.Dao.FindByIdAsync(id) ?? throw new MetierException(d.CleIntrouvable);

             // optimistic lock: if the version in the database is no longer the same as the
             // form, someone has modified this record in the meantime—the system refuses
             // rather than silently overwriting their changes.
             // (If a concurrent modification occurs during this read, it is
             // the "WHERE version = ..." clause in UPDATE that detects it.)
            if (donnees.Version is not null && donnees.Version != personne.Version)
            {
                throw new MetierException("ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE");
            }

             // simply modifies the objects: the DbContext, which follows them,
             // will send the necessary UPDATE to the next SaveChangesAsync
            personne.Titre = donnees.Titre;
            personne.Nom = donnees.Nom.Trim().ToUpperInvariant();
            personne.Prenom = donnees.Prenom.Trim();
            await VerifierPersonneUniqueAsync(d, personne.Prenom, personne.Nom, id);

            var user = personne.User;
            user.Nom = $"{personne.Prenom} {personne.Nom}";
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(donnees.Login) && donnees.Login.ToLowerInvariant() != user.Login)
            {
                var login = donnees.Login.ToLowerInvariant();
                await VerifierLoginLibreAsync(login);
                user.Login = login;
            }
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(donnees.Password))
            {
                user.Password = BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.HashPassword(donnees.Password, ToursBcrypt);
            }
            await userRepository.SaveAsync(user);
            return await d.Dao.SaveAsync(personne);
        });

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // deletion, in the UNE transaction, in the order dictated by the keys
     // foreign keys:
        // 1. possible rejection if there are remaining appointments (with a doctor);
        // 2. information identifying the person (a doctor’s time slots,
           // for a client);
        // 3. the person (who references their account);
        // 4. their account.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private Task SupprimerPersonneAsync<T>(DescripteurPersonne<T> d, int id) where T : Personne, new() =>
        TransactionAsync(async () =>
        {
            var personne = await d.Dao.FindByIdAsync(id) ?? throw new MetierException(d.CleIntrouvable);
            if (d.CompterRv is not null && await d.CompterRv(id) > 0)
            {
                throw new MetierException(d.CleAvecRv ?? "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM");
            }
            if (d.AvantSuppression is not null)
            {
                await d.AvantSuppression(id);
            }
            await d.Dao.DeleteByIdAsync(id);
            await userRepository.DeleteByIdAsync(personne.IdUser);
            return true; // TransactionAsync is waiting for a result: we don’t need it here
        });

     // rejects first and last names already used by a AUTRE person of the same type
     // (idCourant: the person being edited, who obviously has the
     // right to keep their own first and last names; null for a new record)
    private static async Task VerifierPersonneUniqueAsync<T>(DescripteurPersonne<T> d, string prenom, string nom, int? idCourant)
        where T : Personne, new()
    {
        var homonyme = await d.Dao.FindByPrenomNomAsync(prenom, nom);
        if (homonyme is not null && homonyme.Id != idCourant)
        {
            throw new MetierException(d.CleExisteDeja);
        }
    }

    private async Task VerifierLoginLibreAsync(string login)
    {
        if (await userRepository.FindByLoginAsync(login) is not null)
        {
            throw new MetierException("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN");
        }
    }
  • Lines 6–20: The six public methods delegate to the three private generic methods, using the correct descriptor. The compiler infers [T] from the descriptor: [Medecin] for [medecinDescripteur], [Client] for [clientDescripteur];
  • Lines 26–50: Creating a person and their account;
  • lines 28–33: data preparation, outside of a transaction. [Trim] removes leading and trailing spaces from the string; the name is capitalized. By default, the login is the same as the name and is always in lowercase; by default, the password is the same as the login: these are the account rules for the SQL script;
  • lines 37–38: within the transaction, the two uniqueness rules: no duplicate names, and a free choice of login. These are checked before writing to the database to provide a clear message (see Example 28);
  • lines 40–47: The user account is created first, since the person references it (foreign key). The password is never stored in plain text: [BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.HashPassword] calculates its hash (see Example 25). [$"{prenom} {nom}"] is an interpolated string: the displayed name of the account;
  • Lines 49–50: Then, based on the constraint [new()], the person uses [new T] to generate either [Medecin] or [Client]. If this second write operation fails, the transaction also rolls back the first one: an account can never exist without a person;
  • lines 59–95: modifying the person and their account in a single transaction;
  • line 63: a person not found is a [MetierException], with the descriptor key. [?? throw] was seen in Example 28;
  • lines 70–72: the optimistic lock (see Example 28): the form has carried over the version of the record read to its display; if the version in the database is different, someone has modified the record in the meantime, and the system rejects the update rather than silently overwriting their work. Unlike the pessimistic lock used for reservations, nothing is blocked: we assume that conflicts are rare, and we simply detect them. If the concurrent modification occurs after this read, it is the condition [WHERE version = ...] of [UPDATE] that will detect it (see [TraduireErreurBase], below);
  • Lines 77–80: The read object is simply modified: the subsequent [DbContext] will send the necessary [UPDATE] to the next [SaveChangesAsync]. The name check transmits the person’s identifier: they are, of course, entitled to keep their own first and last names;
  • lines 82–88: the account follows the person (navigation property [User], loaded by DAO): their displayed name is recalculated. The login changes only if it has been entered and differs from the current one; in that case, it must be available;
  • lines 90–92: The password changes only if it has been entered; it is then hashed;
  • lines 94–95: saving the account and the person. Our [DbContext] increments the version number of each modified entity (see [Data/RdvMedecinsDbContext.cs]);
  • lines 107–121: deletion, within a single transaction, in the order dictated by the foreign keys;
  • lines 111–113: potential rejection: a doctor with scheduled appointments cannot be deleted (their patients would lose their appointments without being notified). [d.CompterRv(id)] calls the function stored in the descriptor;
  • lines 115–117: deletion of what references the person: a doctor’s time slots, a client’s appointments;
  • lines 119–120: the person, then their account, which the person was referencing;

docs.title: 11.12.4.5. Transactions and uniqueness constraints
docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // executes [travail] in a transaction:
        // BeginTransactionAsync -> START TRANSACTION;
        // Commit           Async -> COMMIT, if everything went well;
        // if an exception is thrown (including MetierException), we do not validate
        // : "await using" closes the transaction upon exiting the block, and a
        // transaction closed without COMMIT is rolled back (ROLLBACK).
    //
     // The "free login" and "unique first name + last name" checks are performed AVANT
     // the entry, to provide a clear message. However, two ADMIN entries could
     // register the same login (or the same doctor) at the same time: in this
     // rare case, a uniqueness constraint SQL rejects the second
     // write operation—we then translate this error SQL into the same MetierException.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private async Task<R> TransactionAsync<R>(Func<Task<R>> travail)
    {
        await using var transaction = await db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync();
        try
        {
            var resultat = await travail();
            await transaction.CommitAsync();
            return resultat;
        }
        catch (Exception e)
        {
             // If the operation fails, the DbContext “forgets” everything that came after it: an
             // entity that remained in the "Added" state would otherwise be sent back to the database to the
             // next SaveChangesAsync in the same query
            db.ChangeTracker.Clear();
            if (TraduireErreurBase(e) is { } erreurMetier)
            {
                throw erreurMetier;
            }
            throw; // "throw;" rethrows the original exception, with its call stack intact
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Database errors -> MetierException
    //
     // - DbUpdateConcurrencyException: the UPDATE "WHERE id = ... AND version = ..."
        // did not modify any rows (optimistic lock, see AbstractEntity);
     // - DbUpdateException, the cause of which (InnerException) is the error MySQL
        // ER_DUP_ENTRY (No. 1062): a constraint UNIQUE rejected the write operation. Its
        // message cites the constraint's ID: NOM:
          // Duplicate entry 'marie-pelissier' for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'
        // (MySQL prefixes the name with the table name, MariaDB does not). This is why
        // this reason that the script SQL NOMME has all these constraints.
     // Any other error is a true anomaly: null is returned (untranslated).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private static readonly Dictionary<string, string> MessagesContraintes = new()
    {
        ["unq_users_login"] = "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN",
        ["unq_medecins_prenom_nom"] = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS",
        ["unq_clients_prenom_nom"] = "ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS",
        ["unq1_rv"] = "ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED",
    };

    private static MetierException? TraduireErreurBase(Exception e)
    {
         // Pay attention to the order: DbUpdateConcurrencyException inherits from DbUpdateException
        if (e is DbUpdateConcurrencyException)
        {
            return new MetierException("ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE");
        }
         // "pattern matching": Is it a DbUpdateException
         // whoseInnerException is a MySqlException with the code DuplicateKeyEntry?
        if (e is DbUpdateException { InnerException: MySqlException { ErrorCode: MySqlErrorCode.DuplicateKeyEntry } erreurSql })
        {
             // "... for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'" -> "unq_medecins_prenom_nom"
            var correspondance = Regex.Match(erreurSql.Message, @"for key '(?:[^'.]*\.)?([^']+)'");
            if (correspondance.Success && MessagesContraintes.TryGetValue(correspondance.Groups[1].Value, out var cle))
            {
                return new MetierException(cle);
            }
        }
        return null;
    }
}
  • line 15: all multi-step entries go through this generic method: [R] is the type of the result of the operation ([Rv], [Medecin], [Client], [bool]), and [Func<Task<R>>] is the type of a parameterless asynchronous function that returns a [R]. This is the [TransactionAsync] method from Example 28, expanded;
  • line 17: [BeginTransactionAsync] opens a transaction ([START TRANSACTION]). [await using var] declares a variable that will be automatically closed upon exiting the block that contains it, regardless of what happens (normal termination or exception); the version [await] allows for asynchronous closure. A transaction that is closed without having been committed is rolled back ([ROLLBACK]);
  • Lines 20–22: The task is executed; if it succeeds, [CommitAsync] commits the transaction ([COMMIT]). If an exception is thrown—including [MetierException]—[CommitAsync] is never reached: everything that has been written is rolled back;
  • line 24: Example 28 caught two specific types of exceptions; here, we catch all exceptions to clean up before restarting them;
  • line 29: the cleanup. The database has rolled back everything, but the [DbContext] is still tracking entities that no longer correspond to anything: for example, the doctor whose insertion failed remains in the [Added] state. Since the [DbContext] persists throughout the entire query, it would be sent back to the database with the next [SaveChangesAsync] for that query. [ChangeTracker.Clear()] causes the [DbContext] to forget all the entities it was tracking;
  • lines 30–32: if the error is a known database error, the corresponding [MetierException] is raised instead. [is { } erreurMetier] is a pattern filter: it checks that the value is not [null] and stores it in the variable [erreurMetier];
  • line 34: otherwise, the original exception is rethrown as-is. [throw;] alone, within a [catch], keeps its call stack intact (the one that indicates where the error occurred), whereas [throw e;] would reset it. A [MetierException] raised by the job is thus passed back, unchanged, to the controller; any other error is an anomaly, which will generate a 500 error page;
  • lines 51–56: for each named uniqueness constraint in the SQL script, its translation key. This is why the script SQL names all its constraints. [new()] without a type name is allowed when the type is already specified on the left; [["cle"] = valeur] populates the dictionary;
  • lines 59–77: translation of a database error into [MetierException], or [null] if the error is not recognized;
  • lines 62–64: [UPDATE ... WHERE id = ... AND version = ...] did not modify any lines: EF Core raises a [DbUpdateConcurrencyException] (optimistic lock; see Example 28). This test comes first because [DbUpdateConcurrencyException] inherits from [DbUpdateException]: if placed later, the following test would have intercepted it;
  • line 68: a uniqueness constraint violation. The error [MySQL] (code [DuplicateKeyEntry], No. 1062) occurs nested within a [DbUpdateException], in its property [InnerException]. Pattern filtering checks everything in a single expression, on two levels: [e] is a [DbUpdateException], whose [InnerException] is a [MySqlException], which is a [ErrorCode] that equals [DuplicateKeyEntry]; this [MySqlException] is contained within [erreurSql]. The [NestJS] version also tested the [ER_DUP_ENTRY] code of a [QueryFailedError];
  • line 71: the error message lists the constraint name, for example, [Duplicate entry 'marie-pelissier' for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom']. The regular expression extracts it: [(?:[^'.]*\.)?] skips the optional prefix [medecins.] (written by [MySQL] 8, not by [MariaDB]), and the group [([^']+)] captures the name up to the apostrophe. The [@] at the beginning of the string makes it a verbatim string, where [\] is not an escape character;
  • Lines 72–74: If the name was found and is listed in the dictionary, [TryGetValue] stores the translation key in [cle], and the error becomes [MetierException]. Any other error, including a violation of a constraint not present in the dictionary, is left untranslated: this is a true anomaly.

docs.title: 11.13. Authentication
docs.text: The [Auth] file includes, in a more comprehensive form, examples 25 through 27: the JWT token in a cookie, roles, CAPTCHA, and attempt limits. It also includes a “pass” for creating a customer account. The [AuthController] controller, discussed at the end of this section, brings these components together for the login page.

docs.title: 11.13.1. Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What the token JWT contains, and how to parse it.
//
// In ASP.NET Core, the request user is a ClaimsPrincipal
// (the User property of a controller; see HttpContext.User elsewhere): a list of
// "claims," type/value pairs—exactly the
// fields of the JWT token once verified. The authentication middleware
// populates the CHAQUE request (see Program.cs, UseAuthentication).
//
// The claims in our tokens (see AuthService.CreerJeton):
//    su  b: the user account ID (convention JWT: "subject")
//    login: the login
//    na  me: the display name ("Marie PELISSIER"), for the navigation bar
//    rol e: ADMIN, DOCTOR, or USER
// =========================================================================

using System.Security.Claims;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public static class ClaimsJwt
{
    public const string Sub = "sub";
    public const string Login = "login";
    public const string Nom = "nom";
    public const string Role = "role";
}

//: the logged-in user, in a typed format
public record UtilisateurConnecte(int UserId, string Login, string Nom, Role Role);

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An “extension method”: it is called as if it were part of
// ClaimsPrincipal (User.Utilisateur()), even though it is defined here.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public static class ClaimsPrincipalExtensions
{
     // the logged-in user, or null if the request is not authenticated
    public static UtilisateurConnecte? Utilisateur(this ClaimsPrincipal principal)
    {
        if (principal.Identity?.IsAuthenticated != true
            || !int.TryParse(principal.FindFirstValue(ClaimsJwt.Sub), out var userId)
            || !Enum.TryParse<Role>(principal.FindFirstValue(ClaimsJwt.Role), out var role))
        {
            return null;
        }
        return new UtilisateurConnecte(
            userId,
            principal.FindFirstValue(ClaimsJwt.Login) ?? "",
            principal.FindFirstValue(ClaimsJwt.Nom) ?? "",
            role);
    }
}
  • lines 24–29: the names of the token claims, grouped into constants: a typo in [ClaimsJwt.Nom] is flagged by the compiler, whereas an error in the string ["nom"] would only be discovered at runtime;
  • line 33: the user logged in using a typed form: an integer identifier, a role of type [Role] (the enumeration ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER from the [Entities] folder), instead of the list of string pairs that constitute the claims. This is equivalent to the [req.user] object created by the [Passport] strategy of the [NestJS] project;
  • lines 39–42: an extension method (see Example 06) on ***[ClaimsPrincipal], the type of the ***[User] property of controllers and views (see Example 25). The pages simply write [User.Utilisateur()];
  • lines 44–48: the method returns [null] if the request is not authenticated, or if the claims are not as expected. [Identity?.IsAuthenticated] is equal to [null] if [Identity] is missing: the [!= true] comparison treats this case as “unauthenticated.” [int.TryParse] and [Enum.TryParse<Role>] attempt a conversion and return [false] if the conversion fails, rather than throwing an exception; the result is stored in the variable declared by [out var];
  • lines 50–54: [FindFirstValue] returns the value of the first claim of the requested type, or [null]; the operator [??] then replaces it with an empty string.

docs.title: 11.13.2. Auth/AuthService.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/AuthService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The authentication logic:
//    - ValiderUtilisateurAsync(): verifies a username/password pair;
//    - DeposerJeton(          ) : generates the JWT token for a validated user
//                                 and stores it in a cookie;
//    - EffacerJeton(          ) : Deletes this cookie (logout).
//
// Where does the JWT token go?
// With the Angular client, it was the client’s code JavaScript that stored the
// token and added it itself to every request (the "Authorization:
// Bearer ..."). A browser that displays ordinary pages HTML does not
// how to do this: for it to automatically include the token in every request,
// it must be stored in a COOKIE. The settings in this cookie affect
// security:
//    - HttpOnly: the JavaScript on the page cannot read the cookie (an
//      injected script would therefore not be able to steal the token);
//    - SameSite=Lax: the browser does not send the cookie with a PAS value originating
//      from another site. Since all actions that modify data are
//      part of POST, a malicious page on another site cannot reserve or
//      delete anything by impersonating the user
//      (known as a CSRF attack);
//    - Secure: in production (HTTPS), the cookie is never transmitted in plain text;
//    - MaxAge: the cookie disappears when the token expires.
// =========================================================================

using System.Text;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens;
using RdvMedecins.Config;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Repositories;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class AuthService(UserRepository userRepository, IOptions<AuthOptions> options)
{
     // the name of the cookie that carries the token
    public const string CookieJwt = "rdvmedecins_jwt";

    private readonly AuthOptions auth = options.Value;

     // the token signature key, generated from the secret of
     // appsettings.json. Also used for VÉRIFIER tokens (see Program.cs).
    public static SymmetricSecurityKey CleDeSignature(AuthOptions auth)
    {
        var octets = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(auth.JwtSecret);
        if (octets.Length < 32)
        {
             // HMAC-SHA256 requires a key of at least 256 bits: this is
             // is clearly stated at startup rather than upon the first login
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Auth:JwtSecret doit comporter au moins 32 caractères (cf. appsettings.json).");
        }
        return new SymmetricSecurityKey(octets);
    }

     // returns null if the login does not exist or if the password is incorrect.
     // BCrypt.Verify hashes the entered password with the "salt" contained in the
     // stored hash, then compares the two results.
    public async Task<User?> ValiderUtilisateurAsync(string login, string password)
    {
        var user = await userRepository.FindByLoginAsync(login);
        if (user is null)
        {
            return null;
        }
        return BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.Verify(password, user.Password) ? user : null;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // generates the token JWT from [user] and stores it in a cookie.
     // The token is SIGNÉ (HMAC-SHA256) with the secret key: the browser
     // can read it (it is not encrypted), but cannot modify it—any
     // modification would invalidate the signature.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public void DeposerJeton(HttpResponse response, User user)
    {
        var descripteur = new SecurityTokenDescriptor
        {
            Claims = new Dictionary<string, object>
            {
                [ClaimsJwt.Sub] = user.Id,
                [ClaimsJwt.Login] = user.Login,
                [ClaimsJwt.Nom] = user.Nom,
                [ClaimsJwt.Role] = user.Role.ToString(),
            },
            Expires = DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(auth.JwtExpiresInSeconds),
            SigningCredentials = new SigningCredentials(CleDeSignature(auth), SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256),
        };
        var jeton = new JsonWebTokenHandler().CreateToken(descripteur);

        response.Cookies.Append(CookieJwt, jeton, new CookieOptions
        {
            HttpOnly = true,
            SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax,
            Secure = auth.CookieSecure,
            MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(auth.JwtExpiresInSeconds),
            Path = "/",
        });
    }

    public static void EffacerJeton(HttpResponse response) =>
        response.Cookies.Delete(CookieJwt, new CookieOptions { Path = "/" });
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 38: the service receives, via injection, the DAO containing user accounts ([UserRepository], commented out with the DAO layer) and the authentication configuration. [IOptions<AuthOptions>] provides the [Auth] section of [appsettings.json] in the form of a [AuthOptions] object ([Config] file): its [Value] property contains the secret key, the token lifetime, and the [CookieSecure] option. The service is registered as [Scoped] in [Program.cs], just like the DAO it uses (see Chapter 6);
  • line 41: the name of the cookie that carries the token;
  • lines 47–56: the signature key (see Example 25). New feature: a key that is too short is rejected with a clear exception. The method is static: it depends only on its parameter, and it is called when the application starts, by [AuthentificationJwt] (next file), at a time when no services yet exist. Since the length check occurs at this point, an incorrect configuration prevents the application from starting, rather than causing the first connection to fail;
  • lines 62–69: the account if the username and password are correct; otherwise, [null] (see Example 25). The method is asynchronous: the account lookup is a database query (see Chapter 9);
  • lines 78–92: the token, generated as in Example 25. It contains the account ID, the username, the name displayed in the navigation bar, and the role; its lifetime is determined by the configuration (two hours by default);
  • Lines 94–100: the cookie, with the options from Example 25 ([HttpOnly], [SameSite = Lax]) and two additional ones: [Secure], enabled in production (the site is served with [HTTPS]), prevents the browser from sending the cookie over an unencrypted connection; [Path = "/"] ensures it is included with every request to the site. [MaxAge] deletes the cookie when the token expires;
  • lines 104–105: Logging out deletes the cookie. For the browser to recognize the cookie to be deleted, the path ([Path]) must be that of the storage location. The method is static: it is also used by the handler [JwtBearer] (next file) and the exception filter [HtmlExceptionFilter] (folder [Web]), which do not have an instance of [AuthService] available.

docs.title: 11.13.3. Auth/AuthentificationJwt.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/AuthentificationJwt.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The configuration for token-based authentication JWT, called from
// Program.cs (builder.Services.AddAuthentificationJwt(...)).
//
// The JwtBearer “handler” in ASP.NET Core performs, for each request, the same actions as
// the Passport 'jwt' strategy and JwtAuthGuard did in NestJS:
//    1. retrieve the token;
//    2. verify its signature and expiration date;
//    3. Extract the user (HttpContext.User, see UtilisateurConnecte.cs).
//
// Three adaptations to a HTML application, using the "events" of the
// manager (the functions it calls at specific times):
//    - OnMessageReceived: the token is read from a COOKIE, not from
//      the "Authorization: Bearer ..." header;
//    - OnChallenge: When a protected page is requested without a valid token,
//      JwtBearer would respond with a 401—which is appropriate for a client JavaScript. A
//      A browser, on the other hand, must be redirected to the login page;
//    — (403: insufficient role) nothing to do here: the empty 403 response is
//      converted into an error page by UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute
//      (see Program.cs and Controllers/ErreurController.cs).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer;
using Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens;
using RdvMedecins.Config;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public static class AuthentificationJwt
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddAuthentificationJwt(this IServiceCollection services, AuthOptions auth)
    {
        services
            .AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
            .AddJwtBearer(options =>
            {
                 // we keep the token’s claim names as-is (“role,” “sub,” etc.)
                 // instead of translating them into long names in the Microsoft style
                options.MapInboundClaims = false;

                options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
                {
                    ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
                    IssuerSigningKey = AuthService.CleDeSignature(auth),
                    ValidateLifetime = true,
                     // An expired token is rejected immediately (by default, a
                     // 5-minute grace period is allowed for clock discrepancies)
                    ClockSkew = TimeSpan.Zero,
                     // Our tokens have neither an issuer (iss) nor a recipient (aud)
                    ValidateIssuer = false,
                    ValidateAudience = false,
                     // Which claim contains the name, and which one contains the role:
                     // [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")] compares the "role" claim
                    NameClaimType = ClaimsJwt.Nom,
                    RoleClaimType = ClaimsJwt.Role,
                };

                options.Events = new JwtBearerEvents
                {
                     // 1. The token is in the cookie
                    OnMessageReceived = context =>
                    {
                        context.Token = context.Request.Cookies[AuthService.CookieJwt];
                        return Task.CompletedTask;
                    },

                     // 2. Protected page without a valid token -> login page
                    OnChallenge = context =>
                    {
                         // HandleResponse(): "I'll handle the response," JwtBearer
                         // will therefore not return a 401
                        context.HandleResponse();
                         // A cookie was present but is no longer valid: the session has expired
                        if (context.Request.Cookies.ContainsKey(AuthService.CookieJwt))
                        {
                            AuthService.EffacerJeton(context.Response);
                            Flash.Deposer(context.HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED");
                        }
                        context.Response.Redirect("/login");
                        return Task.CompletedTask;
                    },
                };
            });

        return services;
    }
}

In Example 25, the configuration for [JwtBearer] was written in [Program.cs]. Here, it is stored in an extension method, which [Program.cs] calls in a single line: [builder.Services.AddAuthentificationJwt(authOptions)]. Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 32–34: the extension method (see Example 06). It directly receives a [AuthOptions] object, read from the configuration by [Program.cs]: when services are registered, dependency injection is not yet available, so we cannot request a [IOptions<AuthOptions>];
  • lines 37–42: the authentication schema [JwtBearer], which stores the token’s claim names (see Example 25);
  • lines 44–54: the checks performed on each token: the signature, using the key generated by [AuthService.CleDeSignature], and the expiration date. New feature compared to Example 25: [ClockSkew = TimeSpan.Zero]. By default, [JwtBearer] still accepts a token for five minutes after it expires, to account for a slight discrepancy between the clocks of the server that generates the token and the one that verifies it. Here, it is the same server: an expired token is rejected immediately;
  • lines 57–58: the claim [nom] yields [User.Identity.Name], the claim [role] is the one verified by [[Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")]] and [User.IsInRole] (see Example 26);
  • lines 64–67: the token is read from the cookie, not from the [Authorization] header (see Example 25);
  • lines 71–82: A request for a protected page without a valid token redirects to the login page (see Example 25). New feature (lines 77–80): If the request included a token cookie, it means the user was logged in, but their token has expired (or was tampered with). We delete this now-useless cookie and display a flash message (see Example 20; the [Flash] class is commented out in the [Web] folder): the login page will display “Your session has expired,” rather than leaving the user wondering why they are there. The message is a translation key (see Example 22).

A 403 Forbidden response (insufficient role) does not require an event: as in Example 26, the empty response is converted into an error page by [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute]. In the [NestJS] project, this task was divided among the [Passport] and [jwt] strategies (read and verify the token), the guard [JwtAuthGuard] (require a token), and the exception filter (convert the denial to a redirect); here, the handler [JwtBearer], its events, and the attribute [[Authorize]] are sufficient.

// =========================================================================
// Auth/SessionInvalideException.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The token is valid, but the account it refers to no longer exists: it was
// deleted since the login (either by the patient themselves in another
// tab, or by the ADMIN). This case is treated as an expired session:
// HtmlExceptionFilter deletes the cookie and redirects to the login page
// (the equivalent of UnauthorizedException from NestJS).

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class SessionInvalideException() : Exception("le compte de l'utilisateur connecté n'existe plus");
  • Line 13: A token may be valid (properly signed, not expired) even though the account it refers to has been deleted since the login. The patient’s pages detect this by searching for the client associated with the account (method [PatientConnecteAsync] in file [Web/Outils.cs]) and then throw this exception; the exception filter [HtmlExceptionFilter] (see Example 24 for filters) intercepts it, deletes the cookie, and redirects to the login page with the message “session expired.” The class has a main constructor with no parameters, which passes its message to the constructor of the parent class [Exception].

docs.title: 11.13.5. Auth/CaptchaService.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/CaptchaService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CAPTCHA ("test to distinguish a human from a robot") generated by the
// the server itself, without an external service: a few characters are distorted,
// scrambled by lines, in an image SVG. A human can read them with
// trouble; a bot that simply sends forms in a loop
// know how to do it.
//
// The NestJS project used the svg-captcha library. Here, there is no
// library: the image is drawn by the DessinCaptcha class (below)
// based on a small, hand-drawn vector “font.” Important
// important: each character is drawn using TRAITS (<path>), never
// written as text (<text>)—otherwise, a bot would simply have to read the
// source code of the image.
//
// How it works:
//    1. Generate() picks a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the
//       correct answer EN MÉMOIRE DU SERVEUR, under a random ID;
//    2. The page displays the image and places the identifier in a hidden field on the
//       form (the response itself never leaves the server);
//    3. Verify(id, input) compares the input to the expected response, then
//       OUBLIE this CAPTCHA: each image is used only once, so a bot cannot
//       reuse a response that has already been found.
//
// SINGLETON service (a single instance for the entire server; see
// Program.cs), used by multiple requests EN PARALLÈLE: hence the
// ConcurrentDictionary, a dictionary that multiple threads can read
// and modify at the same time without corrupting it.
//
// Assumed limitation: the memory of a single process. With multiple servers
// behind a load balancer, shared storage would be required.
// =========================================================================

using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

// ID: to be placed in the hidden field "captchaId" on the form
// Svg: the image, to be inserted as-is into the page
public record Captcha(string Id, string Svg);

public class CaptchaService
{
     // Image validity period: you have 10 minutes to fill out the form
    private static readonly TimeSpan DureeVie = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);

     // Memory safeguard: after that time, the oldest captchas are discarded
    private const int MaxCaptchas = 10_000;

     // id -> (expected response, expiration date)
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, (string Texte, DateTime Expire)> enAttente = new();

    public Captcha Generer()
    {
        Purger();
        var texte = DessinCaptcha.TexteAleatoire(5); // 5 characters
        var id = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();
        enAttente[id] = (texte, DateTime.UtcNow + DureeVie);
        return new Captcha(id, DessinCaptcha.Svg(texte));
    }

     // true if [saisie] is the correct answer to the captcha [id] (regardless of
     // case). The CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases.
     // TryRemove is ATOMIQUE: if two requests encounter the same captcha at
     // same time, only one will clear it—the other will fail.
    public bool Verifier(string? id, string? saisie)
    {
        if (id is null || saisie is null || !enAttente.TryRemove(id, out var attendu))
        {
            return false;
        }
        return attendu.Expire > DateTime.UtcNow
            && string.Equals(attendu.Texte, saisie.Trim(), StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    }

    private void Purger()
    {
        var maintenant = DateTime.UtcNow;
        foreach (var (id, captcha) in enAttente)
        {
            if (captcha.Expire <= maintenant || enAttente.Count >= MaxCaptchas)
            {
                enAttente.TryRemove(id, out _);
            }
        }
    }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The image pattern SVG (150 x 50 pixels).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
internal static class DessinCaptcha
{
    private const int Largeur = 150;
    private const int Hauteur = 50;

     // The “font”: each character is a list of strokes, each stroke a
     // sequence of points (x, y) in a 4 x 6 grid (y down).
     // Characters that are too easily confused with one another: excluded (0 O, 1 I L).
    private static readonly Dictionary<char, double[][]> Police = new()
    {
        ['A'] = [[0, 6, 2, 0, 4, 6], [0.8, 3.8, 3.2, 3.8]],
        ['B'] = [[0, 0, 0, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 3], [0, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3]],
        ['C'] = [[4, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5]],
        ['D'] = [[0, 0, 0, 6, 2.5, 6, 4, 4.5, 4, 1.5, 2.5, 0, 0, 0]],
        ['E'] = [[4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 6, 4, 6], [0, 3, 3, 3]],
        ['F'] = [[4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 6], [0, 3, 3, 3]],
        ['G'] = [[4, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5, 4, 3.5, 2.5, 3.5]],
        ['H'] = [[0, 0, 0, 6], [4, 0, 4, 6], [0, 3, 4, 3]],
        ['J'] = [[4, 0, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
        ['K'] = [[0, 0, 0, 6], [4, 0, 0, 3.5], [1.3, 2.6, 4, 6]],
        ['M'] = [[0, 6, 0, 0, 2, 3.5, 4, 0, 4, 6]],
        ['N'] = [[0, 6, 0, 0, 4, 6, 4, 0]],
        ['P'] = [[0, 6, 0, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3, 0, 3]],
        ['Q'] = [[1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5, 0, 1, 1, 0], [2.5, 4.5, 4, 6.3]],
        ['R'] = [[0, 6, 0, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3, 0, 3], [2, 3, 4, 6]],
        ['S'] = [[4, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
        ['T'] = [[0, 0, 4, 0], [2, 0, 2, 6]],
        ['U'] = [[0, 0, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5, 4, 0]],
        ['V'] = [[0, 0, 2, 6, 4, 0]],
        ['W'] = [[0, 0, 1, 6, 2, 2.5, 3, 6, 4, 0]],
        ['X'] = [[0, 0, 4, 6], [4, 0, 0, 6]],
        ['Y'] = [[0, 0, 2, 3, 4, 0], [2, 3, 2, 6]],
        ['Z'] = [[0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 6, 4, 6]],
        ['2'] = [[0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 0, 6, 4, 6]],
        ['3'] = [[0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3, 1.5, 3], [3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
        ['4'] = [[3, 6, 3, 0, 0, 4, 4, 4]],
        ['5'] = [[4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
        ['6'] = [[4, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 3]],
        ['7'] = [[0, 0, 4, 0, 1.5, 6]],
        ['8'] = [[1, 3, 0, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3, 1, 3, 0, 4, 0, 5, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3]],
        ['9'] = [[4, 3, 1, 3, 0, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
    };

    private static readonly char[] Alphabet = [.. Police.Keys];

     // a few dark colors, clearly legible against the light background
    private static readonly string[] Couleurs = ["#1f4e79", "#7b2d26", "#2e6b30", "#5b2c83", "#8a5a00", "#23395d", "#9c2a5b"];

     // RandomNumberGenerator: a “cryptographic” random number generator,
     // unpredictable (unlike Random, whose sequence could be guessed)
    public static string TexteAleatoire(int longueur) =>
        new(Enumerable.Range(0, longueur).Select(_ => Alphabet[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Alphabet.Length)]).ToArray());

    private static double Hasard(double min, double max) =>
        min + (max - min) * RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(1_000_001) / 1_000_000.0;

    public static string Svg(string texte)
    {
        var svg = new StringBuilder();
        svg.Append($"<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"{Largeur}\" height=\"{Hauteur}\" viewBox=\"0 0 {Largeur} {Hauteur}\">");
        svg.Append($"<rect width=\"100%\" height=\"100%\" fill=\"#f5f7fa\"/>");

         // the characters: each enlarged, tilted, and shifted, and each dot
         // slightly shifted at random
        var pas = (Largeur - 20) / (double)texte.Length;
        for (var i = 0; i < texte.Length; i++)
        {
            var echelle = Hasard(4.6, 5.6); // size of one grid unit, in pixels
            var angle = Hasard(-0.35, 0.35); // rotation, in radians (approximately ±20°)
            var cx = 10 + pas * (i + 0.5) + Hasard(-3, 3); // center of the character
            var cy = Hauteur / 2.0 + Hasard(-4, 4);
            var couleur = Couleurs[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Couleurs.Length)];
            var d = new StringBuilder();
            foreach (var trait in Police[texte[i]])
            {
                for (var k = 0; k < trait.Length; k += 2)
                {
                     // grid point, centered at (2, 3), distorted, rotated, positioned
                    var x = (trait[k] - 2 + Hasard(-0.2, 0.2)) * echelle;
                    var y = (trait[k + 1] - 3 + Hasard(-0.2, 0.2)) * echelle;
                    var px = cx + x * Math.Cos(angle) - y * Math.Sin(angle);
                    var py = cy + x * Math.Sin(angle) + y * Math.Cos(angle);
                    d.Append(k == 0 ? 'M' : 'L').Append(Nombre(px)).Append(' ').Append(Nombre(py)).Append(' ');
                }
            }
            svg.Append($"<path d=\"{d.ToString().TrimEnd()}\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{couleur}\" stroke-width=\"{Nombre(Hasard(2.2, 3))}\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"/>");
        }

         // 3 scrambling lines: curves that cross the image
        for (var n = 0; n < 3; n++)
        {
            var couleur = Couleurs[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Couleurs.Length)];
            svg.Append($"<path d=\"M{Nombre(Hasard(0, 20))} {Nombre(Hasard(5, 45))} " +
                       $"C{Nombre(Hasard(30, 60))} {Nombre(Hasard(0, 50))} {Nombre(Hasard(90, 120))} {Nombre(Hasard(0, 50))} " +
                       $"{Nombre(Hasard(130, 150))} {Nombre(Hasard(5, 45))}\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{couleur}\" stroke-width=\"1.3\"/>");
        }

        svg.Append("</svg>");
        return svg.ToString();
    }

     // a number with a decimal point, regardless of the server’s language
     // (in French, ToString() would write "12.5"—unreadable for SVG)
    private static string Nombre(double valeur) => valeur.ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
}

The file contains two classes: the service class, which is identical to the one in Example 27 except for one safeguard, and the [DessinCaptcha] class that generates the image, which was already discussed in Example 27 (file [Auth/DessinCaptcha.cs]). Let’s go over this code:

  • line 44: a CAPTCHA, as received by the page: the identifier, to be placed in a hidden form field, and the image [SVG];
  • lines 49–52: An image is valid for ten minutes, and there is a cap on the number of pending captchas. Each time the login page is displayed, a captcha is added to memory; without a cap, a bot that requested this page millions of times without ever responding would eventually exhaust the server’s memory;
  • line 55: username → (expected response, expiration date). The pair is a tuple whose elements are named ([Texte], [Expire]). The service is a singleton, used by concurrent requests: hence the [ConcurrentDictionary] (see Example 27);
  • lines 57–63: the cleanup, followed by a randomly generated five-character text string, stored under a random identifier ([Guid.NewGuid()], impossible to guess), and displayed;
  • lines 70–77: verification, identical to that in Example 27: the CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases ([TryRemove]), then the system verifies that it has not expired and that the entered text, with spaces removed, is correct, regardless of case. [TryRemove] is atomic: if two requests present the same CAPTCHA at the same time, only one removes it;
  • lines 80–87: Expired captchas are discarded; if the limit is reached, valid captchas are also removed until the count falls below the limit. A [ConcurrentDictionary] can be modified while it is being processed, which is not allowed with a standard [Dictionary] (see [LimiteurTentativesService], below). However, it does not preserve the insertion order: the CAPTCHAs removed in this way are not necessarily the oldest ones, whereas the [Map] from the [NestJS] project allowed the oldest ones to be removed first. This situation only occurs in the event of an attack: the approximation is sufficient;
  • line 96: the image drawing. [internal]: the class is only visible within the application itself;
  • lines 104–136: the “font”: for each character, a list of strokes, each stroke being a sequence of (x, y) coordinates in a 4 × 6 grid. The square brackets [[...]] are collection expressions ([C#] 12), a compact notation for arrays;
  • line 139: the usable characters, i.e., the font keys. [..] spreads one collection into another;
  • lines 146–147 and lines 149–150: the randomization uses [RandomNumberGenerator], a cryptographic generator whose outputs are unpredictable;
  • lines 152–194: the image is a [SVG] text, assembled into a [StringBuilder] (a string that is extended without being rewritten each time an element is added). Each character (lines 160–181) becomes a [<path>] path: each point on the grid is slightly shifted, enlarged, rotated, and placed in its position within the image, with a randomly selected color and line thickness. The characters are lines, never text: a bot cannot read them in the image’s code. Three scrambling curves then cross the image (lines 185–190);
  • line 199: the numbers in [SVG] are written with a decimal point. [CultureInfo.InvariantCulture] enforces this notation regardless of the server’s language: in French, [ToString()] would use a comma (see Chapter 5).

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/LimiteurTentativesService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second line of defense against bots (the first is the CAPTCHA): COMPTE
// attempts, and once a certain threshold is exceeded, BLOQUE for a while.
//
//    - Login: after LoginMaxEchecs failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or incorrect
//      password) for the same login from the same IP address IP, this combination
//      is blocked for LoginBlocageMinutes minutes. The same IP address IP is also
//      blocked if it accumulates 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins (a
//      bot that tries thousands of different logins);
//    - account creation: no more than InscriptionMaxParHeure accounts created per
//      per hour from the same IP address IP.
//
// Warning in the classroom: all computers frequently access the Internet
// via the MÊME address IP. This is why blocking the connection applies
// primarily on the pair (IP, login)—a student who enters the wrong password
// does not block their neighbors—and why the thresholds are adjustable
// in appsettings.json (the “Protection” section).
//
// Singleton service, called by parallel requests: all
// counter operations are performed under a lock, which ensures
// that only one thread at a time reads or modifies a counter.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
using RdvMedecins.Config;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class LimiteurTentativesService(IOptions<ProtectionOptions> options)
{
    private class Compteur
    {
        public int Nombre; // attempts counted in the current window
        public DateTime Debut; // Start of the counting window
        public DateTime BloqueJusqua; // DateTime.MinValue if not locked
    }

    private static readonly TimeSpan UneHeure = TimeSpan.FromHours(1);

    private readonly Dictionary<string, Compteur> compteurs = [];
    private readonly Lock verrou = new(); // the Lock type of .NET 9+, set to "lock"

    private readonly int maxEchecsLogin = options.Value.LoginMaxEchecs;
    private readonly TimeSpan dureeBlocageLogin = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(options.Value.LoginBlocageMinutes);
    private readonly int maxInscriptions = options.Value.InscriptionMaxParHeure;

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- connection

     // number of remaining minutes of lockout (0 = attempt is allowed)
    public int MinutesBlocageLogin(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (verrou)
        {
            return Math.Max(MinutesRestantes(CleLogin(ip, login)), MinutesRestantes(CleIp(ip)));
        }
    }

    public void EchecLogin(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (verrou)
        {
            Compter(CleLogin(ip, login), maxEchecsLogin, dureeBlocageLogin, dureeBlocageLogin);
            Compter(CleIp(ip), maxEchecsLogin * 5, dureeBlocageLogin, dureeBlocageLogin);
        }
    }

     // A successful login resets the CE login counter
    public void ReussiteLogin(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (verrou)
        {
            compteurs.Remove(CleLogin(ip, login));
        }
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

    public int MinutesBlocageInscription(string ip)
    {
        lock (verrou)
        {
            return MinutesRestantes($"inscription|{ip}");
        }
    }

     // one-hour window; once the quota is reached, access is blocked until the end of the hour
    public void InscriptionReussie(string ip)
    {
        lock (verrou)
        {
            Compter($"inscription|{ip}", maxInscriptions, UneHeure, UneHeure);
        }
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- common mechanism
     // (private methods are always called under the lock)

    private int MinutesRestantes(string cle)
    {
        if (!compteurs.TryGetValue(cle, out var c))
        {
            return 0;
        }
        var reste = c.BloqueJusqua - DateTime.UtcNow;
        return reste > TimeSpan.Zero ? (int)Math.Ceiling(reste.TotalMinutes) : 0;
    }

     // counts one attempt; if the threshold is reached within the window, locks
    private void Compter(string cle, int max, TimeSpan fenetre, TimeSpan blocage)
    {
        var maintenant = DateTime.UtcNow;
        Purger(maintenant);
        if (!compteurs.TryGetValue(cle, out var c) || maintenant - c.Debut > fenetre)
        {
            c = new Compteur { Nombre = 0, Debut = maintenant, BloqueJusqua = DateTime.MinValue };
            compteurs[cle] = c;
        }
        c.Nombre++;
        if (c.Nombre >= max)
        {
            c.BloqueJusqua = maintenant + blocage;
            c.Nombre = 0; // After the lock, the counter resets to zero
            c.Debut = c.BloqueJusqua;
        }
    }

     // Counters that are no longer in use (neither blocked nor recent) are discarded
    private void Purger(DateTime maintenant)
    {
        if (compteurs.Count < 1000)
        {
            return;
        }
        foreach (var (cle, c) in compteurs.ToList())
        {
            if (c.BloqueJusqua < maintenant && maintenant - c.Debut > UneHeure)
            {
                compteurs.Remove(cle);
            }
        }
    }

    private static string CleLogin(string ip, string login) => $"login|{ip}|{login.Trim().ToLowerInvariant()}";

    private static string CleIp(string ip) => $"ip|{ip}";
}

Compared to Example 27, the limiter protects two operations (the connection and account creation); the connection block applies to the pair (address IP, login), and the thresholds are configurable in [appsettings.json]. Let’s break down this code:

  • line 31: [IOptions<ProtectionOptions>] specifies the section [Protection] of [appsettings.json] (folder [Config]): the number of allowed failed login attempts (5 by default), the lockout duration (15 minutes), and the number of accounts created per hour (10);
  • lines 33–37: a counter: the number of attempts, the start of the counting window, and the end of the lockout ([DateTime.MinValue], the earliest possible date, if there is no lockout). This is a nested, private class: it exists only for this service. It is a class, not a [record] or a structure: a counter read from the dictionary is modified in place;
  • Lines 42–43: an ordinary [Dictionary], protected by a lock (see Example 27). A [ConcurrentDictionary] would not be sufficient: counting an attempt involves reading a counter, modifying it, and possibly replacing it, and this entire sequence of operations must be executed without another request interrupting it. Each public method therefore performs its task within a [lock (verrou)] block;
  • lines 45–47: the thresholds, read once and for all. The main constructor’s parameter can be used to initialize the fields;
  • lines 52–56: the remaining lockout time for a connection attempt: the longer of the two possible lockout periods, that of the pair (address IP, login) and that of the address IP alone;
  • lines 60–65: A failed attempt is counted twice. For the pair (address IP, login): five failed attempts with the same login block that login, from that address only. For the address IP alone, with a threshold five times higher: a bot that tries a large number of different logins is also blocked. In a classroom, all computers often connect to the Internet via the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password should not block their neighbors, hence the blocking by pair;
  • lines 70–74: a successful login resets the counter for that specific login (not the one for the address IP);
  • lines 80–84 and lines 89–93: For account creation, only successful attempts are counted: a maximum of ten accounts per hour from the same address IP. Once the quota is reached, the address is blocked for one hour;
  • lines 100–107: the remaining minutes of the block, rounded up to the next whole number ([Math.Ceiling]): it shows “1 minute” rather than “0 minutes” when there are 20 seconds remaining. These private methods do not acquire the lock: they are always called by a public method that already holds it;
  • lines 111–125: counting. An unknown key, or one whose counting window has expired, starts with a new counter. When the threshold is reached, the key is locked, and counting will resume from zero at the end of the lock;
  • lines 130–140: cleaning up counters that are no longer needed (neither locked nor recent), performed only when the dictionary exceeds 1,000 entries. We iterate through a copy of the entries ([ToList()]): a [Dictionary] cannot be modified while it is being iterated over;
  • lines 145–147: generating the dictionary keys. Spaces are removed from the login and it is converted to lowercase: [Admin] and [admin] share the same counter; a bot cannot bypass the lock by changing the case.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/PasseInscriptionService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The “pass” for creating an account.
//
// To open the “Create a Customer Account” page, you must first have
// entered the CAPTCHA from the authentication page (see
// InscriptionController, POST /registration/access). The server then issues
// a token:
//    - a random identifier, stored in a cookie named HttpOnly;
//    - valid for 15 minutes (enough time to fill out the form, even if you
//      trying multiple times after data entry errors);
//    - expires as soon as an account is created: UN captcha solved = UN account
//      . A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
//
// Without a valid passcode, GET and POST /registration redirect to the
// authentication page: typing URL /registration directly does not allow
// bypass the CAPTCHA.
//
// Like the CAPTCHA, the tokens reside in the process’s memory.
// =========================================================================

using System.Collections.Concurrent;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class PasseInscriptionService
{
    public const string Cookie = "rdvmedecins_inscription";

    private static readonly TimeSpan DureeVie = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15);
    private const int MaxPasses = 10_000;

     // ID -> expiration date
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime> passes = new();

     // Issues a new token; returns its ID
    public string Emettre()
    {
        Purger();
        var id = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();
        passes[id] = DateTime.UtcNow + DureeVie;
        return id;
    }

     // true if [id] is an existing, unexpired token
    public bool EstValide(string? id) =>
        id is not null && passes.TryGetValue(id, out var expire) && expire > DateTime.UtcNow;

     // the pass has been used: discard it
    public void Consommer(string? id)
    {
        if (id is not null)
        {
            passes.TryRemove(id, out _);
        }
    }

     // the cookie is sent by the browser only to the /registration... addresses
    public static CookieOptions OptionsCookie() => new()
    {
        HttpOnly = true,
        SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax,
        MaxAge = DureeVie,
        Path = "/inscription",
    };

    private void Purger()
    {
        var maintenant = DateTime.UtcNow;
        foreach (var (id, expire) in passes)
        {
            if (expire <= maintenant || passes.Count >= MaxPasses)
            {
                passes.TryRemove(id, out _);
            }
        }
    }
}

You can create a customer account from the login page, provided you have solved the CAPTCHA. The registration form is displayed and submitted via subsequent requests: these requests must know that a previous request successfully solved the CAPTCHA. This is the role of the token, issued and verified by [InscriptionController] (documented in the controllers):

  • line 29: the name of the cookie that carries the token;
  • lines 31–35: a token is valid for fifteen minutes; pending tokens are kept in memory, like captchas, with the same time limit;
  • lines 38–43: A pass is a random identifier, stored along with its expiration date; the controller places it in a cookie;
  • lines 47–48: the registration form is displayed—and accepted—only with a valid token. Verification does not consume the token ([TryGetValue], not [TryRemove]): the user can resubmit the form multiple times if they made input errors;
  • lines 51–55: Creating an account consumes the token: solving a CAPTCHA entitles the user to one account, and no more;
  • lines 60–65: cookie options. [new()] creates an object of the type declared by the method ([CookieOptions]). The option [Path = "/inscription"] limits the sending of the cookie to URL values that begin with [/inscription]: other requests do not carry it unnecessarily;
  • lines 68–75: the cleanup process, identical to that of the CAPTCHA.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/AuthController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Routes protected by the connection:
//    GE T         / redirects to the role’s home page (or to /login)
//    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
//    POST /logi  n checks the number of failed login attempts, CAPTCHA, and username/password
//    POST /logou t clears the token cookie
//
// A MVC controller inherits from Controller and returns a IActionResult:
// View(...) to display a page, Redirect(...) to redirect...
// [HttpGet("login")] / [HttpPost("login")]: "attribute-based routing,"
// the equivalent of @Get('login') / @Post('login').
//
// Protection against bots, in this order:
//    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
//       -> immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
//    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Denied (counted as a failed attempt);
//    3. Only then is the password verified.
// The password for a rejected attempt is not verified in steps
// 1 or 2: a bot therefore cannot learn anything by persisting.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
