using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class AuthController(
    AuthService authService,
    CaptchaService captchaService,
    LimiteurTentativesService limiteur) : Controller
{
     // the home page for each role, immediately after logging in
    public static string PageAccueil(Role role) => role == Role.USER ? "/mon-espace" : "/agenda";

    [HttpGet("/")]
    public IActionResult Accueil()
    {
         // User: the user making the request, reconstructed from the token by
         // the authentication middleware (see Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs)
        var utilisateur = User.Utilisateur();
        return Redirect(utilisateur is not null ? PageAccueil(utilisateur.Role) : "/login");
    }

     // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the
     // login (used immediately after creating an account; see InscriptionController)
    [HttpGet("login")]
    public IActionResult AfficherLogin(string? login)
    {
         // already logged in (token still valid): goes directly to the home page
        var utilisateur = User.Utilisateur();
        if (utilisateur is not null)
        {
            return Redirect(PageAccueil(utilisateur.Role));
        }
        return Formulaire(login is null ? "" : login[..Math.Min(login.Length, 30)]);
    }

     // the action parameters are populated with the fields from the
     // with the same name (template binding); [FromForm] specifies that they are retrieved from
     // the body of the request POST
    [HttpPost("login")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> SeConnecter(
        [FromForm] string? login,
        [FromForm] string? password,
        [FromForm] string? captchaId,
        [FromForm] string? captcha)
    {
        login = (login ?? "").Trim();
        password ??= "";
        var ip = AdresseIp(HttpContext);

         // 1. Too many recent failures?
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageLogin(ip, login);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return Formulaire(login, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }

         // 2. the CAPTCHA
        if (!captchaService.Verifier(captchaId, captcha))
        {
            limiteur.EchecLogin(ip, login);
            return Formulaire(login, "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA");
        }

         // 3. the password
        var user = login != "" && password != "" ? await authService.ValiderUtilisateurAsync(login, password) : null;
        if (user is null)
        {
            limiteur.EchecLogin(ip, login);
            return Formulaire(login, "LOGIN.ERROR");
        }

        limiteur.ReussiteLogin(ip, login);
        authService.DeposerJeton(Response, user);
        return Redirect(PageAccueil(user.Role));
    }

     // Logout via POST (not via a simple link GET): a third-party site
     // cannot log the user out without their knowledge (see SameSite, AuthService)
    [HttpPost("logout")]
    public IActionResult SeDeconnecter()
    {
        AuthService.EffacerJeton(Response);
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

     // the visitor’s address IP. Behind a reverse proxy (nginx...),
     // you would need to enable the middleware UseForwardedHeaders to obtain the visitor’s
     // visitor’s address rather than the proxy’s.
    public static string AdresseIp(HttpContext http) => http.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "inconnue";

     // the form, still using a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used only once)
    private ViewResult Formulaire(string login, string? erreur = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? erreurParams = null) =>
        View("Login", new LoginModele
        {
            TitrePage = "LOGIN.TITLE",
            Login = login, // The entered username is displayed again, but never the password
            Captcha = captchaService.Generer(),
            Erreur = erreur,
            ErreurParams = erreurParams,
        });
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 31–34: the controller receives the three services it needs. No attributes [[Authorize]]: its pages are accessible without being logged in;
  • line 37: The home page depends on the role: “My Space” for a patient, the calendar for others;
  • lines 39–45: The site root redirects to the role-specific home page or to the login page. The authentication middleware runs for all requests, whether protected or not: if the cookie contains a valid token, [User] is populated, even here. The [NestJS] project, on the other hand, was supposed to verify the token itself (method [lireJeton]), since the token check is not applied to this route;
  • lines 50–59: a user who is already logged in is redirected to their home page. The optional parameter [login], which comes from URL (see Example 07), pre-fills the field after an account is created. [login[..n]] (range operator) preserves the first [n] characters: its length is limited to 30, because data from the request is never used without taking precautions;
  • Lines 65–70: the fields of the login form (see Example 11), including the CAPTCHA ID, transmitted via a hidden field, and the user’s input. All are declared as [string?]: a missing field yields [null], and it is the action that determines what to do with it;
  • lines 72–74: A missing login becomes an empty string; [password ??= ""] only affects the empty string if [password] is [null];
  • lines 77–80: 1. A blocked pair isn’t even processed: neither the CAPTCHA nor the password is checked. The error is a translation key with one parameter: the number of minutes to wait;
  • lines 84–87: 2. the CAPTCHA. An incorrect CAPTCHA counts as a failure (see example 27);
  • lines 91–95: 3. Only then is the password checked. An empty username or password is not subjected to the computationally expensive [bcrypt] calculation. Unknown username or incorrect password: the same deliberately vague message (see Example 25), and another failure;
  • lines 98–100: success: counter reset to zero, token stored in the cookie, redirection to the role’s home page;
  • lines 105–109: logout, using POST (see Example 25);
  • line 115: the client’s address IP, provided by the network connection ([RemoteIpAddress], which may be [null], hence [?.] and [??]). The method is public and static: [InscriptionController] and [EspacePatientController] also use it for the limiter. Behind an intermediary server (a reverse proxy such as [nginx]), this address would be that of the proxy: the comment specifies the middleware to enable in this case;
  • lines 118–125: the login page, always with a new CAPTCHA: each image is used only once. Its template, [LoginModele] (folder [Models]), contains the page title (a translation key), the entered username (never the password), the CAPTCHA, and any error messages, along with the translation key and parameters. [erreur] and [erreurParams] are optional parameters: they default to [null] when the call does not provide them.

docs.title: 11.14. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: Before we get to the controllers and views, here’s what they have in common: translation, the parent class for views, flash messages, the exception filter, the cache for lists of doctors and clients, the preparation of forms to be re-displayed, and a few utility functions. All these files are in the [Web] folder. It brings together most of the techniques from Examples 16 through 24.

docs.title: 11.14.1. Web/Traducteur.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Traducteur.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// French/English translation of the interface.
//
// The dictionaries are the MÊMES files, which are the same as those in the NestJS project
// (i18n/fr.json, i18n/en.json), which are read only once at startup. A view
// Razor translates a key with @T("CLE") (see Web/PageVue.cs).
//
// ASP.NET Core also offers its own system (IStringLocalizer and
// .resx files); keeping the JSON files allows you to share the
// dictionaries with other versions of the application.
//
// LA LANGUE COURANTE: this is the localization middleware for ASP.NET Core
// (UseRequestLocalization, see Program.cs), which determines it for each request,
// based on a cookie, and stores it in CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.
// =========================================================================

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public partial class Traducteur
{
    public static readonly string[] Langues = ["fr", "en"];
    public const string LangueParDefaut = "fr";

     // language -> (full key "LOGIN.TITLE" -> text)
    private readonly Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> dictionnaires = [];

    public Traducteur(IWebHostEnvironment environnement)
    {
        foreach (var langue in Langues)
        {
            var chemin = Path.Combine(environnement.ContentRootPath, "i18n", $"{langue}.json");
            using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(File.ReadAllText(chemin));
            var dictionnaire = new Dictionary<string, string>();
            Aplatir(document.RootElement, "", dictionnaire);
            dictionnaires[langue] = dictionnaire;
        }
    }

     // the language of the current request: "fr" or "en"
    public static string LangueCourante()
    {
        var langue = CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.TwoLetterISOLanguageName;
        return Langues.Contains(langue) ? langue : LangueParDefaut;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Translate("MEDECINS.ADDED", { ["nom"] = "Marie PELISSIER" })
        // -> searches for "MEDECINS.ADDED" in the dictionary for the current language,
           // and replaces {name} with its value. A key missing from the
           // is searched for in French; if it is missing everywhere, the
           // key itself is displayed (thus immediately flagging an omission).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public string Traduire(string? cle, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? parametres = null)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(cle))
        {
            return "";
        }
        var texte = dictionnaires[LangueCourante()].GetValueOrDefault(cle)
                    ?? dictionnaires[LangueParDefaut].GetValueOrDefault(cle)
                    ?? cle;
        if (parametres is null || parametres.Count == 0)
        {
            return texte;
        }
        return Parametre().Replace(texte, m => parametres.TryGetValue(m.Groups[1].Value, out var valeur) ? valeur : m.Value);
    }

     // { "LOGIN": { "TITLE": "Login" } } -> { "LOGIN.TITLE": "Login" }
    private static void Aplatir(JsonElement noeud, string prefixe, Dictionary<string, string> resultat)
    {
        foreach (var propriete in noeud.EnumerateObject())
        {
            var cle = prefixe == "" ? propriete.Name : $"{prefixe}.{propriete.Name}";
            if (propriete.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object)
            {
                Aplatir(propriete.Value, cle, resultat);
            }
            else
            {
                resultat[cle] = propriete.Value.GetString() ?? "";
            }
        }
    }

     // the regular expression {name}, compiled once and for all by the
     // C# compiler ("source generator" [GeneratedRegex])
    [GeneratedRegex(@"\{(\w+)\}")]
    private static partial Regex Parametre();
}

This is the translation service from Example 22, saved as a singleton in [Program.cs]: The dictionaries [i18n/fr.json] and [i18n/en.json] are the same files as those in version [NestJS], read only once at startup. There is only one difference:

  • lines 65–67: a key missing from the English dictionary is looked up in the French dictionary ([LangueParDefaut]); if it is missing everywhere, the key itself is displayed. The two [??] operators are chained together: the first value that is not [null] is taken.

docs.title: 11.14.2. Web/PageVue.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/PageVue.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The parent class of TOUTES, the application's Razor views (see
// Views/_ViewImports.cshtml: @inherits PageVue<TModel>).
//
// A .cshtml view is compiled into a C# class that is a child of RazorPage<TModel>.
// By inserting our own class, we provide all views with what
// they need, regardless of the page:
//    - @T("CLE"         ) : the translation of a key (the equivalent of the helper
//                           Handlebars {{t 'CLE'}});
//    - Langu            age : "fr" or "en";
//    - User         : the logged-in user, for the navigation bar;
//    - MessageFlas      h : the flash message for the request;
//    - Path              : the requested URL (active menu in the navigation bar).
// In NestJS, this information was passed through res.locals.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor.Internal;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public abstract class PageVue<TModel> : RazorPage<TModel>
{
     // [RazorInject]: the property is populated via dependency injection,
     // just as the @inject directive would in a view
    [RazorInject]
    public Traducteur Traducteur { get; set; } = null!;

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // @T("BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT", ("schedule", "8:00 - 8:20"))
     // The parameters are "tuples" (name, value): a compact syntax
     // for writing value pairs.
     // The returned text is then ÉCHAPPÉ by Razor (< becomes <): a name
     // entered by a user cannot therefore inject HTML into the page.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public string T(string? cle, params (string Nom, object? Valeur)[] parametres) =>
        Traducteur.Traduire(cle, parametres.ToDictionary(p => p.Nom, p => p.Valeur?.ToString() ?? ""));

     // the same one, with the parameters of a flash message or a MetierException
    public string T(string? cle, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? parametres) => Traducteur.Traduire(cle, parametres);

    public string Langue => Traducteur.LangueCourante();

    public UtilisateurVue? Utilisateur => UtilisateurVue.De(Context.User.Utilisateur());

    public MessageFlash? MessageFlash => Flash.Lire(Context);

    public string Chemin => Context.Request.Path.Value ?? "/";

     // "active" if the current page is under this path (navigation bar menu)
    public string Actif(string prefixe) => Chemin.StartsWith(prefixe, StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "active" : "";
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the logged-in user, as seen by the views
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public record UtilisateurVue(string Login, string Nom, string Role, bool EstAdmin, bool EstPatient)
{
    public static UtilisateurVue? De(UtilisateurConnecte? u) =>
        u is null
            ? null
            : new UtilisateurVue(
                u.Login,
                u.Nom,
                u.Role.ToString(),
                EstAdmin: u.Role == Entities.Role.ADMIN, // ADMIN: Doctors / Clients menus
                EstPatient: u.Role == Entities.Role.USER); // USER: My Space menu
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 25: the parent class of all views, designated by the [@inherits] directive of [Views/_ViewImports.cshtml], as in Example 22. It serves the same purpose as [res.locals] in version [NestJS]: it provides each view with what all pages need;
  • lines 29–30: the translation service, injected into the property (see Example 22);
  • lines 39–40: the [T] method from Example 22: [@T("CLE", ("nom", valeur))]. The rendered text is escaped by [Razor]: a name entered by a user cannot inject HTML into the page;
  • line 43: a second version of [T], which directly accepts a dictionary: this is the form in which the parameters of a flash message or a [MetierException] are passed. Two methods with the same name, which differ in their parameters, are overloaded methods: the compiler selects the correct one based on the arguments;
  • line 45: the current language ([fr] or [en]), for the page’s [lang] attribute and the FR / EN;
  • Line 47: the logged-in user, for the navigation bar, or [null] if there is none. [Context.User] is the request user, reconstructed from the token JWT by the authentication middleware (see Chapter 8); the method [Utilisateur()] (file [Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs]) extracts the account from it. In version [NestJS], an interceptor was required to copy [req.user] into [res.locals] after the guards; here, the property is calculated when the view reads it, well after authentication;
  • line 49: the request’s flash message (see [Web/Flash.cs], below);
  • lines 51–54: the path of the requested URL, and the method that returns [active] if the current page is under a given path: this is how the navigation bar highlights the current menu item, for example [@Actif("/mon-")] (see Example 16). [StringComparison.Ordinal] compares characters one by one, regardless of language;
  • lines 60–70: the logged-in user as seen by the views: login, name, role, and two Booleans, [EstAdmin] and [EstPatient], which prevent the views from comparing roles. The static method [De] creates this object from the logged-in account, or returns [null]; the operator [? :] chooses between the two. The arguments [EstAdmin:] and [EstPatient:] are named: the parameter name is written before the value, which makes the call more readable.

docs.title: 11.14.3. Web/Flash.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Flash.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Flash" messages: a message to be displayed UNE times on the page
// SUIVANTE. This is the natural complement to the "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern
// used by all forms in the application: a successful POST does not
// does not generate a page; it redirects (302) to a GET page—if
// the user then reloads that page (F5), the browser does not resend
// the form a second time. The message, however, must survive the
// redirect.
//
// In NestJS, we had programmed this ourselves (a short-lived cookie).
// ASP.NET Core MVC provides it by default: it is TempData. A stored value
// in TempData is retained (by default in an encrypted cookie) until
// a subsequent request is made to LISE; it is then deleted.
// =========================================================================

using System.Text.Json;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public enum TypeFlash
{
    Success, // Bootstrap `alert-success` class: at the top of the page
    Danger, // an error: at the bottom of the page (see Views/Shared/_Erreurs.cshtml)
}

// key: translation key; parameters: its parameters ({name}, {login}...)
public record MessageFlash(TypeFlash Type, string Cle, Dictionary<string, string>? Parametres = null);

public static class Flash
{
    private const string Cle = "flash";

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // sends a flash message, which will be displayed by the PROCHAINE page.
     // This is done via ITempDataDictionaryFactory (and not via the TempData
     // of a controller) in order to post a message from N'IMPORTE OÙ:
     // a controller, but also the authentication JWT (session expired, see
     // Auth/AuthentificationJwt.cs), which runs outside of MVC.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static void Deposer(HttpContext http, TypeFlash type, string cle, Dictionary<string, string>? parametres = null)
    {
        var tempData = TempDataDe(http);
         // TempData can only store simple values: the
         // message as plain text JSON
        tempData[Cle] = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new MessageFlash(type, cle, parametres));
         // Save(): writes the cookie immediately (outside of MVC, no one
         // would do this for us)
        tempData.Save();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // reads (and therefore clears) the flash message from the request. The page can
     // request this multiple times (the success message is displayed at the top, the
     // error message at the bottom): we store it in HttpContext.Items, a dictionary
     // that exists for the duration of the request.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static MessageFlash? Lire(HttpContext http)
    {
        if (http.Items.TryGetValue(Cle, out var dejaLu))
        {
            return dejaLu as MessageFlash;
        }
        MessageFlash? message = null;
        if (TempDataDe(http)[Cle] is string json)
        {
            try
            {
                message = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<MessageFlash>(json);
            }
            catch (JsonException)
            {
                 // Unreadable message: it is ignored
            }
        }
        http.Items[Cle] = message;
        return message;
    }

    private static ITempDataDictionary TempDataDe(HttpContext http) =>
        http.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<ITempDataDictionaryFactory>().GetTempData(http);
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 23–26: the two types of messages: a success message, displayed at the top of the page (partial view [_Flash.cshtml]), and an error message, displayed at the bottom (partial view [_Erreurs.cshtml]);
  • line 30: a flash message consists of a translation key and its parameters, not pre-translated text; it will be translated on the next page, in that page’s language;
  • line 32: a static class that contains only functions (see [Web/Outils.cs]). [TempData] (see Example 20) does most of the work: it stores the value in an encrypted cookie until the next request and deletes it once it has been read. In the [NestJS] version, this short-lived cookie had been programmed manually;
  • lines 43–51: sets a message. [TempData] can only store simple values (text, numbers): the message is stored as text JSON ([JsonSerializer.Serialize]). The method receives [HttpContext] and not the [TempData] property of a controller: it can therefore be called from outside MVC, for example by the authentication JWT, when a session has expired (see [Auth/AuthentificationJwt.cs]). Outside of MVC, no one would save [TempData] at the end of the request: [Save()] writes the cookie immediately;
  • Lines 60–79: reads the request message. Reading [TempData] marks it as consumed; however, the page requests it twice (at the top for a success, at the bottom for an error). The first call therefore stores the result in [HttpContext.Items], the request-scope dictionary (see Chapter 6), where the second call retrieves it (line 62);
  • lines 71–73: [Deserialize] reconstructs the object [MessageFlash] from JSON. An unreadable text should not cause the page to fail: the exception is caught and the message is ignored;
  • lines 82–83: the [TempData] from the request, obtained from the [ITempDataDictionaryFactory] service. [RequestServices] provides access to dependency injection from a static class, which cannot receive services via its constructor.

docs.title: 11.14.4. Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// How errors become HTML pages. Three mechanisms
// ASP.NET Core mechanisms share the work (see Program.cs):
//
//    1. this exception filter MVC: a SessionInvalideException (account
//       deleted since logging in) -> return to the login page;
//    2. UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/error/{0}"): any 400 response,
//       403 or 404 SANS content (return BadRequest(), insufficient role, page
//       unknown...) is replaced by the corresponding error page;
//    3. UseExceptionHandler("/error/500"): any other exception (a true
//       error) is logged in the server log, and the user
//       sees the 500 error page—never the call stack.
//
// In NestJS, a single filter (HtmlExceptionFilter) handled all of this.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Filters;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public class HtmlExceptionFilter : IExceptionFilter
{
    public void OnException(ExceptionContext context)
    {
        if (context.Exception is SessionInvalideException)
        {
            AuthService.EffacerJeton(context.HttpContext.Response);
            Flash.Deposer(context.HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED");
            context.Result = new RedirectResult("/login");
            context.ExceptionHandled = true;
        }
         // The other exceptions are not handled here: they are propagated
         // to UseExceptionHandler (page 500)
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Line 25: An exception filter, as in Example 24, added as a global filter in [Program.cs]. In version [NestJS], a single filter converted all errors into HTML pages. Here, the work is shared between two middleware components of the framework, configured in [Program.cs]: [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute] replaces 400, 403, and 404 responses with no content with the corresponding error page (see Example 24), and [UseExceptionHandler("/erreur/500")] intercepts all other exceptions: the error is logged in the server log, along with its call stack, but the user sees only the 500 error page, as these details could assist an attacker;
  • lines 29–34: the filter handles only one scenario: the logged-in user’s account has been deleted since they logged in, even though their token is still valid (see [Web/Outils.cs], below). The token cookie is cleared, a “session expired” flash message is displayed, and the user is redirected to the login page. The other exceptions are not marked as handled: they continue on to [UseExceptionHandler].

docs.title: 11.14.5. Web/ApplicationModel.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/ApplicationModel.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache/frontend already present on the server JSON (equivalent to the
// [ApplicationModel] class from the Spring project): the lists of doctors and
// client lists are read once at startup and then served from memory.
//
// These lists can be CHANGER (the ADMIN adds, modifies, or deletes
// doctors and clients): every write operation therefore goes through this facade,
// which then updates the relevant list immediately afterward. This is the whole point of a
// entry point UNIQUE to the business layer: the rule “update =>
// cache reload" is implemented only here.
//
// An important difference from NestJS: the DURÉE DE VIE of the objects.
//    - In NestJS, all services were singletons.
//    - Here, the DbContext—that is, the repositories and the business layer—experiences the
//      the duration of the UNE request HTTP (“scoped” lifetime; see Program.cs).
//    - However, the cache itself must persist from one request to the next.
// We therefore separate the two roles:
//    - CacheListes (singleton): the two lists, and nothing else;
//    - ApplicationModel (scoped): the facade, which uses the business layer of
//      the current request and updates the cache.
// =========================================================================

using RdvMedecins.Domain;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache itself, shared by all requests (singleton).
//
// ASP.NET Core processes requests EN PARALLÈLE across multiple threads (Node,
// itself has only one). Therefore, we never modify a list in place: we
// REMPLACE in its entirety with a new one. The exchange of a reference is atomic;
// "volatile" ensures that all threads immediately see the new list.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class CacheListes
{
    private volatile IReadOnlyList<Medecin> medecins = [];
    private volatile IReadOnlyList<Client> clients = [];

    public IReadOnlyList<Medecin> Medecins
    {
        get => medecins;
        set => medecins = value;
    }

    public IReadOnlyList<Client> Clients
    {
        get => clients;
        set => clients = value;
    }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The (scoped) facade: same contract as the business layer (IMetier).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class ApplicationModel(IMetier metier, CacheListes cache) : IMetier
{
     // Initial loading of both lists, called once at startup
     // (see Program.cs). If the database is inaccessible, the exception stops the
     // server with an explicit message—clearer than starting up “empty.”
    public async Task ChargerAsync()
    {
        await RechargerMedecinsAsync();
        await RechargerClientsAsync();
    }

    private async Task RechargerMedecinsAsync() => cache.Medecins = await metier.GetAllMedecinsAsync();

    private async Task RechargerClientsAsync() => cache.Clients = await metier.GetAllClientsAsync();

     // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    public Task<List<Medecin>> GetAllMedecinsAsync() => Task.FromResult(cache.Medecins.ToList());

    public Task<List<Client>> GetAllClientsAsync() => Task.FromResult(cache.Clients.ToList());

     // the doctor whose user account is [idUser]—is used for preselection,
     // for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar
    public Medecin? GetMedecinByUserId(int idUser) => cache.Medecins.FirstOrDefault(m => m.IdUser == idUser);

     // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    public Task<List<Creneau>> GetAllCreneauxAsync(int idMedecin) => metier.GetAllCreneauxAsync(idMedecin);

    public Task<List<Rv>> GetRvMedecinJourAsync(int idMedecin, DateOnly jour) => metier.GetRvMedecinJourAsync(idMedecin, jour);

    public Task<Client?> GetClientByIdAsync(int id) => metier.GetClientByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Medecin?> GetMedecinByIdAsync(int id) => metier.GetMedecinByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Rv?> GetRvByIdAsync(int id) => metier.GetRvByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Creneau?> GetCreneauByIdAsync(int id) => metier.GetCreneauByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<AgendaMedecinJour?> GetAgendaMedecinJourAsync(int idMedecin, DateOnly jour) =>
        metier.GetAgendaMedecinJourAsync(idMedecin, jour);

     // no cache here: the most recent data is what counts (a patient
     // who has just modified or deleted their account)
    public Task<Client?> GetClientByUserIdAsync(int idUser) => metier.GetClientByUserIdAsync(idUser);

    public Task<List<Rv>> GetRvAVenirClientAsync(int idClient) => metier.GetRvAVenirClientAsync(idClient);

    public Task<Rv> AjouterRvAsync(DateOnly jour, Creneau creneau, Client client) => metier.AjouterRvAsync(jour, creneau, client);

    public Task SupprimerRvAsync(Rv rv) => metier.SupprimerRvAsync(rv);

     // ------------------------------------------------ entries => reload

    public async Task<Medecin> AjouterMedecinAsync(DonneesPersonne donnees)
    {
        var medecin = await metier.AjouterMedecinAsync(donnees);
        await RechargerMedecinsAsync();
        return medecin;
    }

    public async Task<Medecin> ModifierMedecinAsync(int id, DonneesPersonne donnees)
    {
        var medecin = await metier.ModifierMedecinAsync(id, donnees);
        await RechargerMedecinsAsync();
        return medecin;
    }

    public async Task SupprimerMedecinAsync(int id)
    {
        await metier.SupprimerMedecinAsync(id);
        await RechargerMedecinsAsync();
    }

    public async Task<Client> AjouterClientAsync(DonneesPersonne donnees)
    {
        var client = await metier.AjouterClientAsync(donnees);
        await RechargerClientsAsync();
        return client;
    }

    public async Task<Client> ModifierClientAsync(int id, DonneesPersonne donnees)
    {
        var client = await metier.ModifierClientAsync(id, donnees);
        await RechargerClientsAsync();
        return client;
    }

    public async Task SupprimerClientAsync(int id)
    {
        await metier.SupprimerClientAsync(id);
        await RechargerClientsAsync();
    }
}

Lists of doctors and clients are displayed on almost every page (calendar drop-down lists, administration pages). Rather than retrieving them from the database with every request, they are kept in memory: this is application-scope data (see Chapter 6). Version [NestJS] assigned this role to a single service, which was a singleton like all [NestJS] services. In [ASP.NET Core], this is impossible: the business layer uses [DbContext], which exists only for the duration of a request ([Scoped] service; see Chapter 9), and a singleton cannot accept a [Scoped] service. We therefore separate the two roles into two classes.

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 39: the cache itself, registered as a singleton ([AddSingleton<CacheListes>()] within [Program.cs]). It contains only the two lists;
  • Lines 41–42: [ASP.NET Core] processes requests in parallel across multiple threads ([threads]), whereas [Node.js] has only one. A shared list must therefore never be modified while another request is iterating through it. The rule we’ve chosen is simple: we never modify a list; we replace it with a new one. Replacing a reference is done in a single operation, and the keyword [volatile] ensures that all threads immediately see the new list. [IReadOnlyList] allows only reading: the compiler prohibits adding or removing an element;
  • Line 60: the facade, registered as service [Scoped] ([AddScoped<ApplicationModel>()]). It receives the business layer for the current request and the shared cache. It implements the same [IMetier] interface as the business layer: for the controllers, it is the business layer, and it is the only one they receive;
  • Lines 65–68: the initial loading of the two lists. It is called once, by [Program.cs], before the server starts. A [Scoped] service exists only within a scope: [Program.cs] creates one for this purpose ([CreateScope]). If the database is inaccessible, the exception terminates the application with an explicit message, which is better than starting a server with empty lists;
  • lines 71–73: reloading a list: the entire list is read from the database and replaces the one in the cache;
  • lines 77–79: the lists are served from memory. The [IMetier] interface declares an asynchronous method: [Task.FromResult] creates a task that has already completed, which carries the result. [ToList()] returns a copy of the list: the caller can modify it without affecting the cache;
  • line 83: the doctor associated with an account, retrieved from the cache: a logged-in doctor immediately sees their own schedule;
  • lines 87–110: the other requests are forwarded as-is to the business layer;
  • line 104: a client associated with an account is intentionally not looked up in the cache; a patient who has just modified or deleted their account must be displayed as they appear in the database;
  • lines 114–151: Any write operation involving doctors or clients is followed by a refresh of the relevant list. Since this service is the only entry point for controllers to the business layer, the rule “write = cache refresh” is implemented only here, and the cache cannot become stale. If the business layer rejects the operation ([MetierException]), the exception terminates the method before the cache is reloaded, as this step is no longer necessary.

docs.title: 11.14.6. Web/Validation.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Validation.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What’s needed for a rejected form: the errors in
// field-by-field input errors, and the fields to highlight in red.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;
using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public static class Validation
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // ModelState (filled in by MVC when the form is linked) -> the
     // field dictionary -> message key, keeping only the first
     // message for each field: { "Name": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", ... }
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static Dictionary<string, string> ErreursDe(ModelStateDictionary modelState)
    {
        var erreurs = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        foreach (var (champ, entree) in modelState)
        {
            if (entree.Errors.Count > 0)
            {
                var message = entree.Errors[0].ErrorMessage;
                erreurs[champ] = string.IsNullOrEmpty(message) ? "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM" : message;
            }
        }
        return erreurs;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the form fields affected by each business "data entry" error
     // (a duplicate): they are highlighted in red, with the message at the bottom of the page
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static readonly Dictionary<string, string[]> ChampsErreursMetier = new()
    {
        ["ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"] = ["login"],
        ["ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"] = ["prenom", "nom"],
        ["ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS"] = ["prenom", "nom"],
    };

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // prepares a form template for its (re)display:
        // er     rors : message below each field rejected by validation
        // e      rror : LE page error message, displayed at the bottom of the page;
                       // default: "The form contains errors." if there
                       // there are field errors
        // autresChamps: fields to be highlighted in red SANS custom message
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static T Preparer<T>(
        T modele,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? erreurParams = null) where T : FormulaireVue
    {
        modele.Erreurs = erreurs ?? new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        modele.ChampsInvalides = new HashSet<string>(modele.Erreurs.Keys.Concat(autresChamps ?? []), StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        modele.Erreur = erreur ?? (modele.Erreurs.Count > 0 ? "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM" : null);
        modele.ErreurParams = erreurParams;
        return modele;
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 20–31: Convert [ModelState] (see examples 07 and 19) into a simple “field → message key” dictionary. Only the first message for each field is retained: a single message is displayed under the field. The dictionary ignores uppercase letters (line 22): [ModelState] names the fields based on the properties ([Nom], [Login]), whereas the views request them based on the HTML fields ([nom], [login]);
  • lines 27–28: As a precaution, an error without a message (such as one caused by an exception) is assigned the generic message [ERRORS.INVALID_FORM];
  • lines 38–42: certain errors in the business layer relate to specific fields: a username that is already taken, or a doctor or client with the same name. These fields will be highlighted in red, with the message displayed at the bottom of the page. The syntax [["clé"] = valeur] populates the dictionary as soon as it is created;
  • lines 53–64: prepares a form template for display or redisply: the messages below the fields ([Erreurs]), the fields to be framed in red ([ChampsInvalides]: those with a message, plus the [autresChamps] fields, line 61), the message at the bottom of the page, and its parameters. In the absence of an explicit message, field errors result in the message “The form contains errors” (line 62). The method is generic: the constraint [where T : FormulaireVue] (line 58) accepts any model derived from [FormulaireVue] (see [Models/ModelesVues.cs]), and it returns the model with its exact type, ready to be passed to [View]. The parameters have default values ([= null]): the caller provides only those it needs.

docs.title: 11.14.7. Web/Outils.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Outils.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Small utility functions of the web layer:
//    - Labels: "Ms. Alice DURAND";
//    - DatesWeb: dates "yyyy-MM-dd", times "8:05", days "Wednesday, September 23, 2026";
//    - Input  : reads a positive integer sent by the browser;
//    - Patien t: the patient (Client entity) of the logged-in user.
//
// "static" classes: they contain only functions; no objects of these classes are ever created
// objects of these classes.
// =========================================================================

using System.Globalization;
using System.Security.Claims;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public static class Libelles
{
     // "Ms. Alice DURAND"
    public static string Libelle(Personne p) => $"{p.Titre} {p.Prenom} {p.Nom}";
}

public static class DatesWeb
{
     // the date format in URL and in the <input type="date"> field
    public const string FormatIso = "yyyy-MM-dd";

     // true if [jour] is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format
     // ("2026-02-30" is rejected)
    public static bool EstUneDateValide(string? texte, out DateOnly jour) =>
        DateOnly.TryParseExact(texte, FormatIso, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out jour);

    public static string Iso(DateOnly jour) => jour.ToString(FormatIso, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

     // "8:05" rather than "8:5"
    public static string FormaterHeure(int h, int m) => $"{h}:{m:00}";

    public static string Horaire(Creneau c) => $"{FormaterHeure(c.Hdebut, c.Mdebut)} - {FormaterHeure(c.Hfin, c.Mfin)}";

     // "Wednesday, September 23, 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026", depending on the
     // language of the request (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, set by the
     // localization middleware—see Program.cs)
    public static string FormaterJour(DateOnly jour) =>
        jour.ToString("dddd d MMMM yyyy", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture);
}

public static class Saisie
{
     // "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", null -> null
    public static int? EntierPositif(string? valeur) =>
        int.TryParse(valeur, NumberStyles.None, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var n) && n > 0 ? n : null;
}

public static class Patient
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // The patient (Client entity) corresponding to the logged-in user.
    //
     // The token JWT contains only the ID of COMPTE (users.id). For a role
     // For USER, the corresponding client is identified using the clients.user column.
    //
     // If there is no match, it means the account was deleted since the
     // login, even though its token is still valid: it is treated as a
     // expired session (see SessionInvalideException).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static async Task<Client> PatientConnecteAsync(ApplicationModel application, ClaimsPrincipal user)
    {
        var utilisateur = user.Utilisateur() ?? throw new SessionInvalideException();
        return await application.GetClientByUserIdAsync(utilisateur.UserId) ?? throw new SessionInvalideException();
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 24: the name of a doctor or a client: “Ms. Alice DURAND.” The parameter is of type [Personne], the parent class of entities [Medecin] and [Client]: the same function is used for both;
  • line 30: the date format in the URL entities and in the [<input type="date">] field;
  • Lines 34–35: true if the text is a date in the [yyyy-MM-dd] format that exists; [2026-02-30] is rejected (see Example 12). The result is returned in the parameter [out jour]. [CultureInfo.InvariantCulture] makes the analysis independent of the query language;
  • line 37: the reverse operation: a date to the text [yyyy-MM-dd];
  • lines 40–42: a time in the [8:05] format (the [00] format requires two digits for the minutes), and the time of a time slot: [8:00 - 8:20];
  • lines 47–48: a day written out in full, according to the request’s locale, as determined by the localization middleware (see Example 22): “mercredi 23 septembre 2026” or “Wednesday 23 September 2026”;
  • lines 54–55: an identifier sent by the browser (in the URL or a form field): a strictly positive integer, or [null]. [NumberStyles.None] accepts only digits: no signs, spaces, or thousands separators. The controller simply needs to test [null];
  • lines 70–73: the patient (entity [Client]) associated with the logged-in user. The token JWT contains only the account ID; we look for the customer associated with that account. If it no longer exists, it means the account has been deleted since the user logged in: [SessionInvalideException] will be processed by the [HtmlExceptionFilter] filter described above, which redirects to the login page. [?? throw] throws an exception when the value on the left is [null] (see Chapter 9).

docs.title: 11.15. Form and View Templates
docs.text: Two types of classes transport data between the browser, controllers, and views: forms, populated by the model binding based on what the browser sends, and view models, prepared by controllers for the views. The former correspond to the DTO objects in version [NestJS], while the latter correspond to the objects passed to [res.render].

docs.title: 11.15.1. Models/Formulaires.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Models/Formulaires.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The fields in the "person" forms and their constraints. Three
// forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//    ChampsPersonn               e title, first name, last name
//     ├─ FormulairePerson       ne + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
//                                   │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
//     ├─ FormulaireInscripti    on + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
//                                   │ (a patient creates an account)
//     └─ FormulaireMonComp      te + username, optional new password,
//                                    ACTUEL password required, version
//                                    (a patient modifies their account)
//
// LIAISON DE MODÈLE (model binding): when a controller action receives
// a parameter from one of these classes, ASP.NET Core MVC creates the object and
// populates each property with the form field of the same name (without
// case sensitivity: the “name” field populates the Name property).
//
// VALIDATION: Immediately afterward, MVC checks the attributes [Required],
// [MaxLength]... (standard namespace System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations,
// the equivalent of `class-validator`) and stores the errors in ModelState.
// The controller then simply needs to test ModelState.IsValid.
//
// The error messages are translation strings (see i18n/*.json).
//
// NETTOYAGE DE LA SAISIE (the equivalent of @Transform in class-transformer):
//    - MVC already converts an empty field to null;
//    - the setters below remove unnecessary spaces and set the
//      login in lowercase. A password, however, is not "cleaned" (
//      spaces may be part of it).
// All properties are “nullable” (string?): a field may still
// be missing in the data sent by the browser; [Required] requires it.
// =========================================================================

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

public static class ReglesSaisie
{
    public static readonly string[] Titres = ["Mr", "Mme", "Melle"];

     // login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
    public const string FormatLogin = "^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$";

     // minimum password length for a patient: CHOISI
    public const int MotDePasseMin = 6;

     / / " dupont " -> "dupont"  ; " " -> null
    public static string? Nettoyer(string? valeur) => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(valeur) ? null : valeur.Trim();
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "custom" validation attribute: the value must be included in a list.
// Simply inherit from ValidationAttribute and write IsValid.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class ParmiAttribute(params string[] valeurs) : ValidationAttribute
{
     // null is accepted here: it is the role of [Required] to require it
    public override bool IsValid(object? value) => value is null || valeurs.Contains(value as string);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
public class ChampsPersonne
{
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    [Parmi("Mr", "Mme", "Melle", ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    public string? Titre { get; set; }

     // maximum lengths = those of the columns SQL (VARCHAR(20))
    private string? prenom;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Prenom
    {
        get => prenom;
        set => prenom = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value);
    }

    private string? nom;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Nom
    {
        get => nom;
        set => nom = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value);
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
public class FormulairePersonne : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

     // optional (see DonneesPersonne, Business Line/IMetier.cs)
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

     // optional; 72 characters maximum (if longer, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

     // hidden field in the edit form (optimistic lock).
     // int? : a missing or empty field returns null; text that is not a
     // number results in a binding error (see Program.cs, ModelBindingMessageProvider)
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient registration
public class FormulaireInscription : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    [MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")]
    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage My Account"
public class FormulaireMonCompte : ChampsPersonne
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(ReglesSaisie.FormatLogin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = ReglesSaisie.Nettoyer(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

     // optional: blank = password unchanged
    [MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }

     // The password ACTUEL, required for any account changes
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    public string? MotDePasseActuel { get; set; }

    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

Let's discuss this code:

  • line 43: possible titles;
  • line 46: the format of a username, described by a regular expression: 1 to 30 characters consisting of lowercase letters, digits, a period, a hyphen, and an underscore;
  • line 49: the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient. This is a constant ([const]), so it can be used as an argument for an attribute, such as [[MinLength(ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin)]] below;
  • line 52: cleaning up an entry: leading and trailing spaces are removed, and a field consisting solely of spaces becomes [null], meaning it is invalid;
  • lines 59–62: a validation attribute we wrote: the value must appear in a list. All we need to do is derive it from [ValidationAttribute] and redefine [IsValid]. [null] is accepted: it is the role of [[Required]] to reject a missing field. We use it under the name [[Parmi]]: by convention, the suffix [Attribute] can be omitted;
  • Line 66: the identity fields, common to all three forms. All properties are of type [string?]: a field may always be missing in the data sent by the browser, and it is [[Required]] that requires it. Error messages are translation keys (see Example 22);
  • Lines 68–70: the title, which is required and selected from the list. The values are repeated in [[Parmi(...)]]: an attribute’s argument must be known at compile time, which is not the case for the array [ReglesSaisie.Titres] (a [static readonly] field, created at runtime);
  • lines 73–80 and lines 83–90: the first name and last name, which are required and may be up to 20 characters long (the width of the SQL columns). These properties have a body: their value is stored in a private field, and [set] cleans it up as it passes through. Since the model binding affects the properties before validation, it is the cleaned-up value that is validated. This is equivalent to the [@Transform] in version [NestJS]; [ASP.NET Core MVC] already automatically converts an empty field to [null];
  • line 95: the ADMIN form, for adding or editing a doctor or a client. The class inherits the identity fields and their validation attributes;
  • lines 97–104: the login, which is optional here but must be in the correct format if present (line 100); it is sanitized and converted to lowercase. [?.] calls [ToLowerInvariant] only if the value is not [null];
  • lines 108–109: the password, also optional, with a maximum of 72 characters: the [bcrypt] algorithm, which encrypts it, ignores any characters following it. A password is not sanitized: spaces are included as part of it;
  • line 114: the record’s version, in a hidden field of the update form (optimistic lock; see Example 28). A missing or empty field results in [null]; text that is not a number produces a binding error, whose message is configured in [Program.cs] (see Example 19);
  • Line 118: A patient creates an account: username, password (6 to 72 characters, line 131), and confirmation (lines 135–136) are required. Verifying that the password matches its confirmation involves two fields: this is checked by the validator ([Controllers/InscriptionController.cs]);
  • Line 140: A patient modifying their account. The new password is optional (line 153): if left blank, the password remains unchanged; its confirmation (line 157) is therefore not required here. The current password, however, is required for any changes (lines 160–161), and the record version is stored in a hidden field (line 163).

docs.title: 11.15.2. Models/ModelesVues.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Models/ModelesVues.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "View models": what each controller passes to
// its view (return View("...", model)), in a C# class TYPÉE. In a
// Razor view, @model AgendaModele declares the model type: the compiler
// then checks every @Model.Xxx in the view—a typo results in a
// compilation error, not an empty section on the page.
//
// A rule already followed with Handlebars: no logic in views. The
// controllers prepare formatted data DÉJÀ ("Ms. Marie
// PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", Selectionne = true...) and already filtered according to
// the user’s role; the views simply place them in the HTML.
// =========================================================================

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// what TOUTES the pages have in common, as read by the template
// (Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public abstract class ModeleVue
{
     // translation key for the page title (<title>)
    public string TitrePage { get; set; } = "APP.TITLE";

     // LE page error message, displayed at the bottom of the page
     // (see Views/Shared/_Erreurs.cshtml); null = no error
    public string? Erreur { get; set; }

    public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? ErreurParams { get; set; }
}

// an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
public record OptionVue(int Id, string Libelle, bool Selectionne);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
public class LoginModele : ModeleVue
{
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public required Auth.Captcha Captcha { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ calendar
public class LigneAgendaVue
{
    public int IdCreneau { get; init; }
    public string Horaire { get; init; } = ""; // "8:00 - 8:20"
    public bool Libre { get; init; }
    public string? Patient { get; init; } // display name for a booked time slot; null = “Reserved”
    public bool Moi { get; init; } // the logged-in patient’s appointment
    public bool Reservable { get; init; } // Display the "Book" button?
    public string UrlReserver { get; init; } = "";
    public int? IdRv { get; init; } // filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
}

public record AgendaVue(string Medecin, string Jour, List<LigneAgendaVue> Lignes);

public class ReservationVue
{
    public int IdCreneau { get; init; }
    public string Horaire { get; init; } = "";
     // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the list of patients to choose from
    public List<OptionVue> Clients { get; init; } = [];
     // USER: the patient is the patient themselves
    public string? Patient { get; init; }
}

public class AgendaModele : ModeleVue
{
    public List<OptionVue> Medecins { get; set; } = [];
    public int? IdMedecin { get; set; }
    public string Jour { get; set; } = ""; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
    public AgendaVue? Agenda { get; set; }
    public ReservationVue? Reservation { get; set; }
    public string UrlRetour { get; set; } = "/agenda"; // the displayed calendar, without the booking window
     // Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the explanatory message
     // why there is no “Book” button
    public string? Info { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Person" forms

// the values displayed in the form fields (never the password)
public class ValeursPersonne
{
    public string Titre { get; set; } = "Mr";
    public string Prenom { get; set; } = "";
    public string Nom { get; set; } = "";
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// what the common partial _ChampsPersonne.cshtml uses (title, first name, last name)
public abstract class FormulaireVue : ModeleVue
{
    public ValeursPersonne Valeurs { get; set; } = new();

     // field -> key of the message displayed SOUS this field (input error)
    public Dictionary<string, string> Erreurs { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

     // fields to be highlighted in red (Bootstrap "is-invalid" class): those that have
     // a message, plus any others (duplicate first name + last name, login already taken...)
    public HashSet<string> ChampsInvalides { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    public string? ErreurDe(string champ) => Erreurs.GetValueOrDefault(champ);

    public string ClasseInvalide(string champ) => ChampsInvalides.Contains(champ) ? "is-invalid" : "";

    public IEnumerable<(string Valeur, bool Selectionne)> Titres =>
        ReglesSaisie.Titres.Select(t => (t, t == Valeurs.Titre));
}

public class FormulairePersonneModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public bool Creation { get; set; } // true: add; false: update
    public string Action { get; set; } = ""; // URL from POST
    public string UrlListe { get; set; } = "";
}

public class InscriptionModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public int MotDePasseMin => ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin;
}

public class MonCompteModele : FormulaireVue
{
    public int MotDePasseMin => ReglesSaisie.MotDePasseMin;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ lists of doctors / clients

// translation keys specific to each person type
public record ClesPersonnes(
    string Titre, // "Doctors"
    string Ajouter, // "Add a doctor"
    string Modifier, // "Edit a doctor"
    string Vide, // "No doctors."
    string ConfirmerSuppression, // "Delete this doctor and their account?"
    string Ajoute, // "The doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    string Modifie,
    string Supprime);

public record PersonneVue(string Titre, string Prenom, string Nom, string Login, string UrlModifier, string UrlSupprimer);

public class ListePersonnesModele : ModeleVue
{
    public required ClesPersonnes Cles { get; set; }
    public string UrlAjouter { get; set; } = "";
    public List<PersonneVue> Personnes { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient area
public record RendezVousVue(int Id, string Jour, string Horaire, string Medecin, string UrlAgenda);

public class EspaceModele : ModeleVue
{
    public string Patient { get; set; } = "";
    public List<RendezVousVue> RendezVous { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
public class ErreurModele : ModeleVue
{
    public int Code { get; set; }
    public string Message { get; set; } = "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR";
}

The view templates follow the rule already applied with [Handlebars]: no logic in the views. The controllers prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views simply place this data into the HTML. Each view declares the type of its template ([@model AgendaModele], see Example 13): the compiler checks each [@Model.Xxx], and a typo results in a compilation error.

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 22–31: what all pages have in common, as read by the [_Layout.cshtml] template: the translation key for the page title (line 25), and the page’s error message, displayed at the bottom, along with its parameters. The class is abstract: each page has its own template, which derives from it;
  • line 35: an option from a drop-down list (a doctor, a patient), already marked as selected or unselected (see Example 18);
  • lines 38–41: the login page: the username already entered and the CAPTCHA to be displayed. The keyword [required] requires the person creating the object to assign a value to the property; failing to do so results in a compilation error;
  • lines 45–54: a calendar entry, i.e., a time slot. The controller has already determined everything: whether the patient’s name is displayed (a patient cannot see the names of others), whether the “Reserve” button is displayed, and whether the “Cancel” button is displayed ([IdRv] is set). The properties [init] can only be assigned a value when the object is created;
  • Line 57: A doctor's schedule for a single day: the doctor's name, the day spelled out in full, and the lines;
  • Lines 59–66: The appointment window: the list of patients for ADMIN and the doctors, or just the name of the logged-in patient;
  • lines 69–79: the calendar page: the list of doctors, the selected doctor and day, the calendar ([null] as long as no doctor is selected), the booking window (if present), the calendar URL without this window (line 76), and the message explaining to a patient why they cannot book an appointment;
  • lines 85–91: the values displayed in the fields of a “person” form, never the password: a password is not sent back to the browser;
  • line 95: the parent class of the templates for the three “person” forms, the one required by [Validation.Preparer]: the field values, the messages below the fields (line 100), and the fields to be highlighted in red (line 104). A [HashSet] is a set: each element appears only once, and the membership test is fast;
  • Lines 106–108: two methods for views: a field’s message (or [null]), and the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid], which frames a field in red. Views are named, for example, [@Model.ClasseInvalide("login")];
  • lines 110–111: the options in the title list, with the selected option marked (see Example 18). Each option is a tuple [(Valeur, Selectionne)];
  • lines 114–118: the ADMIN form, used for adding and modifying entries (see Example 28): the mode, the form submission URL, and the list URL for the back button;
  • lines 121–128: the registration and account management forms; they pass the minimum password length to the view, which is used as the [{min}] parameter for the field’s error message and, for registration, for the help text;
  • lines 134–142: the doctor and client management pages are the same views; only their text differs. This [record] contains the translation keys specific to each type of person;
  • lines 144–150: a row in the list of doctors or clients, with the addresses of its Edit and Delete buttons, and the template for the list page;
  • lines 154–159: the patient’s area: their name and upcoming appointments, each with a link to the daily calendar;
  • lines 163–166: the error page: the code HTTP and the message key, which by default is that of a server error.

docs.title: 11.16. The Web Layer: Controllers
docs.text: Controllers are the visible part of the web layer: each one receives requests from a group of pages, reads their parameters, queries the business layer (always through the [ApplicationModel] service), then selects a view and passes it a typed model, or redirects the request. All POST forms follow the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (see Example 20); all messages are translation keys, translated by the view. The connection controller, [AuthController], has been commented out for authentication.

docs.title: 11.16.1. Controllers/LangueController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/LangueController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two buttons FR / EN on the
// navigation bar. Unsecured route: it should be possible to change the language before
// logging in.
//
// The selection is stored in LE a cookie in the localization middleware
// of ASP.NET Core (CookieRequestCultureProvider, see Program.cs): with each
// subsequent request, this middleware re-reads it and sets the request’s language
// (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture / CurrentUICulture). Then we return to the
// page we came from.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class LangueController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("langue/{langue}")]
    public IActionResult Changer(string langue)
    {
        if (!Traducteur.Langues.Contains(langue))
        {
            return NotFound(); // -> 404 error page (see Program.cs)
        }
        Response.Cookies.Append(
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.DefaultCookieName,
             // cookie value: "c=en|uic=en" (format language, text language)
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.MakeCookieValue(new RequestCulture(langue)),
            new CookieOptions { MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365), SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, HttpOnly = true, Path = "/" });
        return Redirect(PageDOrigine());
    }

     // the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the
     // browser. We only keep the path (/agenda?...): redirect to
     // a complete address provided by the request would allow us to send
     // the user to a different site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”).
    private string PageDOrigine()
    {
        var referer = Request.Headers.Referer.ToString();
        if (!Uri.TryCreate(referer, UriKind.Absolute, out var url))
        {
            return "/";
        }
        return url.AbsolutePath.StartsWith("/langue/", StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "/" : url.PathAndQuery;
    }
}

This is, except for one line, the controller from Example 22: same route [/langue/{langue}], same localization middleware cookie, same return to the original page via the header [Referer]. Two clarifications:

  • line 34: the option [Path = "/"] makes the cookie valid for all addresses on the site, regardless of the page from which the language was changed;
  • line 49: if the original page is itself a [/langue/...] page, the user is redirected to the site’s root rather than back to that page, which would cause the browser to go in a loop.

docs.title: 11.16.2. Controllers/AgendaController.cs
docs.text: The application’s main page and the most feature-rich controller. Let’s break it down section by section.

docs.title: 11.16.2.1. The URL files on the page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/AgendaController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The calendar page: selecting a doctor and a day, that
// doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling appointments.
//
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-2             3 the page
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&reserve=7    the same page, with
//                                                           the booking window
//                                                           for time slot 7 is open
//    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
//    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
//
// The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, add it
// to favorites, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line
// of JavaScript.
//
// What everyone sees and can do:
//
//    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
//                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
//    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
//                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
//                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
//
//    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITÉ: for a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
// simply hidden by the view—it is never included in the template
// passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
// nor is it hidden (otherwise, simply “View Source” would reveal it).
//
// No reservations in the past: the “Reserve” button only appears
// for today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it
// in any case).
//
// [Authorize] on the class: all actions require a logged-in user
// (equivalent to @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)). [Authorize(Roles =
// "...")] on an action also requires one of the listed roles (RolesGuard +
// @Roles). Without a valid token: redirect to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize]
[Route("agenda")]
public class AgendaController(ApplicationModel application) : Controller
{
     // what the controller knows about the user to determine what to display
    private record Droits(
        bool Gestionnaire, // ADMIN or DOCTOR
        Client? Patient, // the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise null
        bool PatientPeutReserver); // USER with no upcoming appointments
  • Lines 7–12: the page’s routes. Note that the booking window is not opened by [JavaScript]: it is a parameter of URL ([reserver=7]) that instructs the server to render the page with the window open. The “Book” button is therefore simply a link. The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, bookmark it, or use the browser’s “Back” button;
  • lines 18–28: what each role sees and can do. This table is the page’s “specification”: the rest of the controller implements it;
  • lines 30–33: the privacy rule, which we’ll come back to: the names of other patients are not hidden by the view; they are never sent to the browser;
  • lines 55–57: [[Authorize]] on the class: all actions require a logged-in user, regardless of their role (see Example 25). [[Route("agenda")]] is the prefix for all routes in the controller (see Example 02). The controller receives the [ApplicationModel] service via injection (see Example 06) through its main constructor: the parameters written in parentheses after the class name are accessible in all of its methods;
  • lines 60–63: what the controller knows about the logged-in user, calculated once per request (see [DroitsAsync], below). A private [record], declared inside the class: it is used only by that class. A handler is a ADMIN or a DOCTOR; [Patient] is populated only for a client (role USER).

docs.title: 11.16.2.2. GET /calendar
docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /calendar
     // The parameters of URL are read in raw format (Request.Query), to distinguish
     // a ABSENT parameter from a VIDE parameter (?idMedecin=).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Afficher()
    {
        string? erreur = null;
        var utilisateur = User.Utilisateur()!;
        var droits = await DroitsAsync(utilisateur);

         // the day: the one from URL if it is valid, otherwise today
        var jour = Dates.Aujourdhui();
        if (Request.Query.TryGetValue("jour", out var jourBrut))
        {
            if (DatesWeb.EstUneDateValide(jourBrut, out var jourDemande))
            {
                jour = jourDemande;
            }
            else
            {
                erreur = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE";
            }
        }
        var jourReservable = jour >= Dates.Aujourdhui();

         // the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
        var idMedecin = Saisie.EntierPositif(Request.Query["idMedecin"]);
        if (!Request.Query.ContainsKey("idMedecin") && utilisateur.Role == Role.DOCTOR)
        {
            idMedecin = application.GetMedecinByUserId(utilisateur.UserId)?.Id;
        }

        var medecins = (await application.GetAllMedecinsAsync())
            .Select(m => Option(m, m.Id == idMedecin))
            .ToList();

         // the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
        AgendaVue? agenda = null;
        if (idMedecin is int id && erreur is null)
        {
            var agendaMedecin = await application.GetAgendaMedecinJourAsync(id, jour);
            if (agendaMedecin is null)
            {
                erreur = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND";
            }
            else
            {
                var lignes = agendaMedecin.CreneauxMedecinJour.Select(cmj =>
                {
                    var (creneau, rv) = (cmj.Creneau, cmj.Rv);
                    var libre = rv is null;
                     // the logged-in patient’s appointment?
                    var moi = rv is not null && droits.Patient is not null && rv.IdClient == droits.Patient.Id;
                    return new LigneAgendaVue
                    {
                        IdCreneau = creneau.Id,
                        Horaire = DatesWeb.Horaire(creneau),
                        Libre = libre,
                         // LE privacy setting: a patient only receives the name
                         // for the SON appointment; for others, null (the view displays “Reserved”)
                        Patient = rv is not null && (droits.Gestionnaire || moi) ? Libelles.Libelle(rv.Client) : null,
                        Moi = moi,
                        Reservable = libre && jourReservable && (droits.Gestionnaire || droits.PatientPeutReserver),
                        UrlReserver = UrlAgenda(id, jour, creneau.Id),
                        IdRv = rv is not null && droits.Gestionnaire ? rv.Id : null,
                    };
                }).ToList();
                agenda = new AgendaVue(Libelles.Libelle(agendaMedecin.Medecin), DatesWeb.Iso(jour), lignes);
            }
        }
  • Lines 6–7: the route [GET /agenda] (controller prefix, followed by an empty string). The action has no parameters: it automatically reads URL as [Request.Query] (see Example 05). The model binding would convert a [int? idMedecin] parameter to [null] whether it is missing or empty; however, these two cases must be distinguished (see below);
  • Lines 10–11: the logged-in user and their permissions. [Utilisateur()] is an extension method (see Example 06) defined in [Auth/UtilisateurConnecte.cs]: it reads the token’s claims and converts them into a typed object. [!] informs the compiler that the result is not [null]: this is certain, since [[Authorize]] has filtered out unauthenticated requests;
  • lines 14–26: the requested day, if valid; today otherwise. [TryGetValue] returns [false] if the parameter [jour] is missing: in that case, it returns today, without a message.
