If present but invalid ([jour=2026-02-30]), it generates an error message. Reservations can only be made starting today ([jourReservable]);
  • lines 29–32: the requested doctor. [Saisie.EntierPositif] (record [Web]) returns a strictly positive integer, or [null] if the value is missing, empty, or invalid. If the [idMedecin] parameter is missing from URL, a logged-in doctor sees their own schedule: this is their home page. If it is empty ([idMedecin=], the “Choose a Doctor” option in the list), no schedule is displayed;
  • lines 35–37: the options in the doctors’ drop-down list, read from the cache of [ApplicationModel]; the option for the requested doctor is selected (see the [Option] function at the end of the file and Example 18);
  • lines 40–46: The schedule is calculated only if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. [idMedecin is int id] checks that the value (of type [int?]) is not [null], and stores its value in a new variable [id], of type [int]. An unknown doctor ID triggers a message, not an error page;
  • lines 50–56: The schedule calculated by the business layer (a [AgendaMedecinJour] object from the [Domain] record) is converted into array elements, one per time slot. [var (creneau, rv) = ...] breaks down a value pair into two variables. [moi] determines whether the appointment belongs to the logged-in patient;
  • Lines 58–59: The view receives only data that has already been formatted ([8:00 - 8:20]); it no longer has anything to calculate;
  • line 63: the application’s privacy control. The patient’s name is included in the model only for an administrator or for the patient whose appointment it is. For everyone else, the model contains [null], and the view displays “Reserved.” The name is not simply hidden by the view: it is never sent to the browser, and “View Page Source” would not reveal it;
  • lines 65–67: what the view must display, as determined by the controller: the “Reserve” button (available time slot, date not past, and user authorized to reserve), its link (the page’s URL, with [reserver]), and the “Cancel” button ([IdRv] is populated only for an administrator). The view does not make any decisions: it follows these instructions;
  • line 70: the complete schedule: the doctor, the day, the rows.

  • lines 3–5: the time slot for which URL is requesting a reservation ([reserver=7]). It must appear in the displayed schedule and be bookable by this user: a manually created URL (a past time slot, a booked time slot, or a slot for another doctor) does not open the window. [agenda?.Lignes] is equivalent to [null] if [agenda] is [null] (operator [?.]);
  • lines 6–15: the window template. An administrator selects a patient from a list (all clients, read from the cache); a patient makes a reservation for themselves: the window simply displays their name. [[]] is an empty list;
  • lines 19–29: the page template. Its classes ([AgendaModele], [AgendaVue], [LigneAgendaVue], [ReservationVue], [OptionVue]) are defined in [Models/ModelesVues.cs]; [TitrePage] and [Erreur] are derived from their common parent class [ModeleVue]. [TitrePage] is, like all texts, a translation key;
  • line 27: the address of the displayed calendar, without the booking window—this is the address of the button that closes the window;
  • line 28: an informational message for patients who already have an upcoming appointment: it explains why they do not see a “Book” button.

docs.title: 11.16.2.4. POST /calendar/book
docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /calendar/boo  k fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
    //
     // For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: they book
     // always books for himself. Trusting a field sent by the
     // browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
    //
     // "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not
     // generate a page here—we post a flash message and redirect
     // to the calendar (see Web/Flash.cs).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("reserver")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR,USER")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Reserver(
        [FromForm] string? idMedecin,
        [FromForm] string? jour,
        [FromForm] string? idCreneau,
        [FromForm] string? idClient)
    {
        if (!LireAgendaDemande(idMedecin, jour, out var idMed, out var jourDemande)
            || Saisie.EntierPositif(idCreneau) is not int idCre)
        {
            return BadRequest(); // -> “Invalid request” page (see Program.cs)
        }

        Client? client;
        if (User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
        {
            client = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        }
        else
        {
            if (Saisie.EntierPositif(idClient) is not int idCli)
            {
                 // No patient selected: the booking window reopens
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT");
                return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande, idCre));
            }
            client = await application.GetClientByIdAsync(idCli);
        }

        var creneau = await application.GetCreneauByIdAsync(idCre);
        if (client is null)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else if (creneau is null || creneau.IdMedecin != idMed)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            try
            {
                 // the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
                 // patient, available time slot) are verified by the business layer
                await application.AjouterRvAsync(jourDemande, creneau, client);
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "AGENDA.BOOKED");
            }
             // "when": an exception filter. Same rule, but a message to the second
             // person when the patient makes the appointment themselves (“You have
             // already...” rather than “This patient...””)
            catch (MetierException e) when (e.Cle == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" && User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
            {
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO");
            }
             // any other MetierException becomes a flash message; the other
             // exceptions (true errors) are not caught: 500 page
            catch (MetierException e)
            {
                Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Parametres));
            }
        }
        return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande));
    }
  • Lines 12–13: [[Authorize(Roles = ...)]] on the action is added to the class’s [[Authorize]]: all three roles can make reservations (see Example 26). Here, this attribute imposes no further restrictions; it documents the rule and would protect it if a fourth role were to appear;
  • lines 15–18: the fields in the reservation window form (see Example 11). They are received as strings and then carefully converted;
  • lines 20–23: the doctor and the day are hidden fields in the form; they allow the user to return to the displayed calendar. If they are invalid, the request did not originate from our page: it was manually crafted. [BadRequest()] returns a 400 response with no content, which the [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute] middleware transforms into an error page (see Example 24). [is not int idCre] is the opposite of [is int]: true if the value is [null]; otherwise, [idCre] receives the value;
  • Lines 27–29: For a patient, the [idClient] field is ignored—the system always makes the reservation for the patient itself. Relying on this field, which is sent by the browser, would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name. [Patient.PatientConnecteAsync] (record [Web]) identifies the client using the token; [nameof(Role.USER)] is the string ["USER"], verified by the compiler;
  • Lines 33–39: A manager who has not selected a patient is redirected to the booking window (URL with [reserver]), accompanied by a pop-up error message. [Flash.Deposer] (record [Web]) stores the message in [TempData] (see Example 20);
  • lines 42–49: the patient must exist, and the time slot must exist and belong to the doctor in the calendar: you cannot book a time slot belonging to one doctor for another;
  • lines 57–58: The business rules (not in the past, slot available, only one upcoming appointment per patient) are verified by the business logic layer, which raises a [MetierException] in case of rejection;
  • Lines 63–65: [when] adds a condition to [catch]: it is an exception filter [C#]. This block only catches the [MetierException] if the condition is true: for a patient, the message “this patient already has an appointment” is replaced by a second-person message. Otherwise, the exception proceeds to the next [catch];
  • lines 69–71: any other [MetierException] becomes a flash message, along with its key and parameters ([e.Parametres] is a read-only dictionary: a copy is made of it, of the type expected by [Flash.Deposer]). The other exceptions are not caught: these are true errors, which result in a 500 error page;
  • Line 74: the PRG schema: regardless of the result, a flash message is displayed and the user is redirected to the calendar, which will display the message. In version [NestJS], a utility function handled this business error conversion; here, the two [catch] blocks are sufficient.

docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /calendar/ca  ncel fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
     // (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("annuler")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Annuler([FromForm] string? idRv, [FromForm] string? idMedecin, [FromForm] string? jour)
    {
        if (!LireAgendaDemande(idMedecin, jour, out var idMed, out var jourDemande)
            || Saisie.EntierPositif(idRv) is not int id)
        {
            return BadRequest();
        }
        var rv = await application.GetRvByIdAsync(id);
        if (rv is null)
        {
             // already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            await application.SupprimerRvAsync(rv);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "AGENDA.CANCELLED");
        }
        return Redirect(UrlAgenda(idMed, jourDemande));
    }
  • lines 5–7: Cancellation is restricted to administrators; a patient cancels their appointment from “My Account” (see [EspacePatientController]). A patient who sends this request would receive a 403 page;
  • Lines 9–12: The same checks as for the reservation;
  • lines 14–18: An appointment that has already been canceled (by double-clicking or by another administrator) triggers an error message, not an error page;
  • lines 22–25: deletion, followed by schema PRG.

docs.title: 11.16.3. Controllers/PersonnesControllerBase.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/PersonnesControllerBase.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Physician management and client management (reserved for ADMIN) are
// IDENTIQUES: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
// writing the same actions twice, we write them once in this
// class ABSTRAITE and GÉNÉRIQUE, from which MedecinsController inherits
// ([Route("medecins")]) and ClientsController ([Route("clients")]). Each
// subclass simply needs to specify its “configuration”: which methods
// to call, and which labels to display.
//
// The routes defined in ICI ([HttpGet("ajouter")]...) are inherited, and
// supplement the subclass’s route. Thus, for each one, we obtain:
//
//    GE T /doctor                  s list
//    GE T /doctors/add            empty form
//    POST /doctors/add            create
//    GE T /doctors/{id}/edit      pre-filled form
//    POST /doctors/{id}/edit      edit
//    POST /doctors/{id}/delete     deletion
//
// (and the same URL under /clients). The views are also shared:
// Views/People/Liste.cshtml and Views/People/Formulaire.cshtml.
//
// An abstract class is never treated as a controller by MVC: only
// its concrete subclasses are.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

// what each subclass must provide
public record ConfigPersonnes<T>(
    string Url, // "/doctors" or "/clients"
    ClesPersonnes Cles,
    Func<Task<List<T>>> Lister,
    Func<int, Task<T?>> Trouver,
    Func<DonneesPersonne, Task<T>> Ajouter,
    Func<int, DonneesPersonne, Task<T>> Modifier,
    Func<int, Task> Supprimer) where T : Personne;

public abstract class PersonnesControllerBase<T>(ApplicationModel application) : Controller where T : Personne
{
    protected ApplicationModel Application { get; } = application;

    protected abstract ConfigPersonnes<T> Config { get; }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors (or /clients)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Liste()
    {
        var personnes = await Config.Lister();
        return View("~/Views/Personnes/Liste.cshtml", new ListePersonnesModele
        {
            TitrePage = Config.Cles.Titre,
            Cles = Config.Cles,
            UrlAjouter = $"{Config.Url}/ajouter",
            Personnes = personnes
                .Select(p => new PersonneVue(p.Titre, p.Prenom, p.Nom, p.User?.Login ?? "",
                    $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/modifier", $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/supprimer"))
                .ToList(),
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/add
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("ajouter")]
    public IActionResult FormulaireAjout() => AfficherFormulaire(null, new ValeursPersonne());

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/add
     // [formulaire] has been filled out ET validated by MVC: ModelState indicates whether the
     // entry is correct.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("ajouter")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Ajouter(FormulairePersonne formulaire)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return AfficherFormulaire(null, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var personne = await Config.Ajouter(Donnees(formulaire));
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Ajoute, Parametres(personne));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            return AfficherErreurMetier(null, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/{id}/edit
     // {id:int} : a "route constraint"—/doctors/abc/edit does not
     // corresponds to any route (404 page)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("{id:int}/modifier")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> FormulaireModification(int id)
    {
        var personne = await Config.Trouver(id);
        if (personne is null)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        return AfficherFormulaire(id, new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = personne.Titre,
            Prenom = personne.Prenom,
            Nom = personne.Nom,
            Login = personne.User?.Login ?? "",
            Version = personne.Version,
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/{id}/edit
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/modifier")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Modifier(int id, FormulairePersonne formulaire)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return AfficherFormulaire(id, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var personne = await Config.Modifier(id, Donnees(formulaire));
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Modifie, Parametres(personne));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            return AfficherErreurMetier(id, ValeursSaisies(formulaire), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/{id}/delete
     // (The browser prompts for confirmation—"Are you sure?"—before
     // the form is submitted; see wwwroot/js/app.js)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/supprimer")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Supprimer(int id)
    {
        var personne = await Config.Trouver(id);
        try
        {
            await Config.Supprimer(id);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, Config.Cles.Supprime, Parametres(personne));
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Parametres));
        }
        return Redirect(Config.Url);
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

     // id null: create form; otherwise: update form
    private ViewResult AfficherFormulaire(
        int? id,
        ValeursPersonne valeurs,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null)
    {
        var creation = id is null;
        return View("~/Views/Personnes/Formulaire.cshtml", Validation.Preparer(
            new FormulairePersonneModele
            {
                TitrePage = creation ? Config.Cles.Ajouter : Config.Cles.Modifier,
                Creation = creation,
                Action = creation ? $"{Config.Url}/ajouter" : $"{Config.Url}/{id}/modifier",
                UrlListe = Config.Url,
                Valeurs = valeurs,
            },
            erreurs, erreur, autresChamps));
    }

     // A business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed,
     // with the user’s input and the message from the business layer
    private IActionResult AfficherErreurMetier(int? id, ValeursPersonne valeurs, MetierException e)
    {
        if (e.Cle is "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND" or "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
        {
             // deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: return to the list
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, e.Cle);
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
         // the message moves to the bottom of the page; the relevant fields, if any, are
         // highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct
        return AfficherFormulaire(id, valeurs, null, e.Cle, Validation.ChampsErreursMetier.GetValueOrDefault(e.Cle));
    }

     // what the user entered (excluding the password: it is never sent back to the browser)
    private static ValeursPersonne ValeursSaisies(FormulairePersonne f) => new()
    {
        Titre = f.Titre ?? "",
        Prenom = f.Prenom ?? "",
        Nom = f.Nom ?? "",
        Login = f.Login ?? "",
        Version = f.Version,
    };

     // the submitted form -> the data expected by the business layer
    private static DonneesPersonne Donnees(FormulairePersonne f) => new()
    {
        Titre = f.Titre!,
        Nom = f.Nom!,
        Prenom = f.Prenom!,
        Login = f.Login,
        Password = f.Password,
        Version = f.Version,
    };

     // {name} and {login} for the "added / modified / deleted" messages
    private static Dictionary<string, string> Parametres(Personne? personne) => personne is null
        ? new() { ["nom"] = "", ["login"] = "" }
        : new() { ["nom"] = $"{personne.Prenom} {personne.Nom}", ["login"] = personne.User?.Login ?? "" };
}

The management of doctors and clients is identical. Rather than writing two similar controllers, we write their actions once, in an abstract and generic parent class. Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 15–20: the routes for doctors; the same ones exist in [/clients];
  • lines 22–23: the views are also shared (file [Views/Personnes]);
  • lines 25–26: MVC accepts only concrete classes as controllers: only [MedecinsController] and [ClientsController] receive requests;
  • lines 38–45: the configuration provided by each subclass: the base URL, the texts (translation keys, grouped in [record] and [ClesPersonnes] from [Models/ModelesVues.cs]), and the functions to be called for listing, searching, adding, modifying, and deleting. [Func<int, Task<T?>>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns a [Task<T?>]: this is how methods are stored in properties, to be called later. [where T : Personne] is a constraint on the generic type: [T] will be either [Medecin] or [Client], two classes derived from [Personne]; the code can therefore use [p.Prenom] or [p.User], which are common to all people;
  • Line 47: the parent class, which is generic (see the [PageVue<TModel>] class in Example 22) and abstract. It receives [ApplicationModel] via its main constructor and passes it to its subclasses via the protected property [Application] ([protected]: visible only to subclasses);
  • line 51: an abstract property: each subclass must define it;
  • lines 56–69: the list. The route attributes set on a parent class’s methods are inherited: combined with the subclass’s [[Route("medecins")]], they yield [GET /medecins]. For each person, the model contains the URL for their Edit and Delete buttons. [p.User?.Login ?? ""]: the login for the associated account, or an empty string if the person does not have an account;
  • line 60: the view is specified by its full path. If only its name were used, MVC would search for it in the controller’s folder ([Views/Medecins] or [Views/Clients], see Example 13), whereas it is shared by both;
  • lines 75–76: the empty form;
  • lines 83–98: the addition, in three steps, as in Example 28. The parameter [formulaire] was populated and validated by MVC prior to the call (see Example 19): an invalid entry redisplays the form, showing the entered values and a message below each incorrect field; a valid entry is passed to the business layer, then the browser is redirected to the list, with a flash message (PRG); a rejection by the business layer (a homonym, a login already in use) re-displays the form;
  • Lines 107–121: the pre-filled modification form. The route constraint [:int] (see Example 02) only accepts an integer identifier: [/medecins/abc/modifier] does not correspond to any route, resulting in a 404 page ([ParseIntPipe] derived from [NestJS] resulted in a 400 error). A nonexistent person also results in a 404. The version number, a hidden field in the form, will be used for the optimistic lock (see example 28);
  • lines 128–143: the update, following the same pattern as the insertion;
  • lines 152–165: deletion. The person is retrieved beforehand to display their name in the confirmation message. A rejection from the business layer (e.g., a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message on the list page;
  • lines 171–188: the form for creation ([id] is equivalent to [null]), as for modification: only the title and mailing address change. [Validation.Preparer] (file [Web]) populates the template with field-specific error messages, the footer message, and the fields to be highlighted in red;
  • lines 193–203: a person who has since been deleted (by another administrator) is listed again; other business errors re-display the form, with the footer message and the affected fields highlighted in red ([Validation.ChampsErreursMetier] associates each error code with its corresponding fields: [prenom] and [nom] for a homonym). [is "A" or "B"] compares a value to several constants;
  • lines 207–213: the values to be redisplayed—never the password;
  • lines 217–224: the data transmitted to the business layer. The [!] fields pose no risk: validation has verified the presence of these fields;
  • lines 228–230: the [{nom}] and [{login}] parameters in the success messages: the person’s first and last name, and their login.

// =========================================================================
// Controllers/MedecinsController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Physician management (ADMIN role only). All actions are
// inherited from PersonnesControllerBase: all that remains here is to specify QUOI
// "Call" and QUELS "Display" labels.
//
// [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")] set on CLASSE applies to all its
// actions, including inherited ones.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")]
[Route("medecins")]
public class MedecinsController(ApplicationModel application) : PersonnesControllerBase<Medecin>(application)
{
    protected override ConfigPersonnes<Medecin> Config => new(
        Url: "/medecins",
        Cles: new ClesPersonnes(
            Titre: "MEDECINS.TITLE",
            Ajouter: "MEDECINS.ADD",
            Modifier: "MEDECINS.EDIT",
            Vide: "MEDECINS.EMPTY",
            ConfirmerSuppression: "MEDECINS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
            Ajoute: "MEDECINS.ADDED",
            Modifie: "MEDECINS.UPDATED",
            Supprime: "MEDECINS.DELETED"),
        Lister: Application.GetAllMedecinsAsync,
        Trouver: Application.GetMedecinByIdAsync,
        Ajouter: Application.AjouterMedecinAsync,
        Modifier: Application.ModifierMedecinAsync,
        Supprimer: Application.SupprimerMedecinAsync);
}
  • Lines 20–22: Reserved for ADMIN. The attribute set on the class applies to all its actions, including inherited ones. The controller inherits from [PersonnesControllerBase<Medecin>]: the parent class’s type, [T], becomes [Medecin]. Its main constructor passes [application] to the parent class’s constructor. (In [TypeScript], an explicit constructor had to be written so that [NestJS] would know what to inject; there is no need for that here);
  • lines 24–34: the configuration. [override] redefines the parent class’s abstract property; [=>] turns it into a computed property, which creates the object each time it is read. The named arguments ([Url:], [Cles:]...) make the list readable;
  • lines 35–39: the functions to be called, which are methods of [ApplicationModel]. [Application.GetAllMedecinsAsync], written without parentheses, does not call the method: it refers to it, and the compiler converts it to a value of the expected type [Func].

docs.title: 11.16.6. Controllers/InscriptionController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/InscriptionController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Create a customer account": a patient who does not yet have an account
// creates one themselves. Protected paths NON (we don’t have an account yet, per
// definition):
//
//    POST /registration/acc  ess "Create a customer account" button on the
//                              authentication page: verifies the CAPTCHA from
//                              CETTE page, then opens the form
//    GE T /registrat        ion the form
//    POST /registrati        on the registration process, then returns to the login page
//
// The process is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
// authentication page:
//    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form
//       to /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server
//       issues a token (see Auth/PasseInscriptionService.cs);
//    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
//       authentication page—entering URL directly does nothing;
//    3. The pass is used up upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA
//       allows you to create UN an account;
//    4. In addition, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is
//       limited (see Auth/LimiteurTentativesService.cs).
//
// The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the
// "Clients" page (same business-layer method: AjouterClientAsync), if this
// is simply the patient CHOISIT entering their login and password (required,
// with confirmation).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Route("inscription")]
public class InscriptionController(
    ApplicationModel application,
    CaptchaService captchaService,
    LimiteurTentativesService limiteur,
    PasseInscriptionService passes) : Controller
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /registration/a  ccess fields: captchaId, captcha (those on the
     // authentication page; username and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("acces")]
    public IActionResult Acces([FromForm] string? captchaId, [FromForm] string? captcha)
    {
        var ip = AuthController.AdresseIp(HttpContext);

         // too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageInscription(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", new() { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

         // captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with
         // a new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
        if (!captchaService.Verifier(captchaId, captcha))
        {
            limiteur.EchecLogin(ip, "");
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

         // Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and open the form
        Response.Cookies.Append(PasseInscriptionService.Cookie, passes.Emettre(), PasseInscriptionService.OptionsCookie());
        return Redirect("/inscription");
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /registration
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Formulaire()
    {
        if (!ALaissezPasser())
        {
            return RetourLogin();
        }
        return Afficher(new ValeursPersonne());
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /registration
     // The parameter [formulaire] is filled in, and VALIDÉ is replaced by MVC before the call:
     // The validation result is in ModelState.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Creer(FormulaireInscription formulaire)
    {
        if (!ALaissezPasser())
        {
            return RetourLogin();
        }
        var ip = AuthController.AdresseIp(HttpContext);
        var valeurs = new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = formulaire.Titre ?? "Mr",
            Prenom = formulaire.Prenom ?? "",
            Nom = formulaire.Nom ?? "",
            Login = formulaire.Login ?? "",
        };

         // 1. Too many accounts created recently from this address?
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageInscription(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, null, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", null, new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }

         // 2. All data entry errors at once (fields + confirmation):
             // The user corrects them all at once
        var erreurs = Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState);
        if (!erreurs.ContainsKey("password") && !erreurs.ContainsKey("confirmation") && formulaire.Password != formulaire.Confirmation)
        {
            erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER";
        }
        if (erreurs.Count > 0)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, erreurs);
        }

         // 3. Creation (customer + account USER, in a transaction)
        try
        {
             // "!": this tells the compiler that these values are not null -
             // this is true, since the validation ([Required]) was successful
            await application.AjouterClientAsync(new DonneesPersonne
            {
                Titre = formulaire.Titre!,
                Nom = formulaire.Nom!,
                Prenom = formulaire.Prenom!,
                Login = formulaire.Login,
                Password = formulaire.Password,
            });
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
             // username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
            return Afficher(valeurs, null, e.Cle, Validation.ChampsErreursMetier.GetValueOrDefault(e.Cle));
        }

         // 4. The password has been used: it will not allow you to create a second account
        passes.Consommer(Request.Cookies[PasseInscriptionService.Cookie]);
        Response.Cookies.Delete(PasseInscriptionService.Cookie, new CookieOptions { Path = "/inscription" });
        limiteur.InscriptionReussie(ip);

         // 5. Return to the login page; username is pre-filled
        Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "INSCRIPTION.DONE", new() { ["login"] = formulaire.Login! });
        return Redirect($"/login?login={Uri.EscapeDataString(formulaire.Login!)}");
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

    private bool ALaissezPasser() => passes.EstValide(Request.Cookies[PasseInscriptionService.Cookie]);

     // No valid passcode: return to the authentication page
    private RedirectResult RetourLogin()
    {
        Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

     // The form; the password is never sent back to the browser
    private ViewResult Afficher(
        ValeursPersonne valeurs,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? erreurParams = null) =>
        View("Inscription", Validation.Preparer(
            new InscriptionModele { TitrePage = "INSCRIPTION.TITLE", Valeurs = valeurs },
            erreurs, erreur, autresChamps, erreurParams));
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 14–24: protection against bots, in four steps. The CAPTCHA and attempt limiter were introduced in Example 27;
  • lines 40–45: The controller does not have the [[Authorize]] attribute; its pages are open to everyone. It receives four services via injection;
  • lines 51–52: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page sends the login form to this address (attribute [formaction]; see Example 20). Only the CAPTCHA fields are read;
  • line 54: the browser’s address IP, via a static method from [AuthController];
  • lines 57–61: Too many accounts have been created from this address within the last hour: the user is redirected to the login page, with a pop-up message indicating the number of minutes to wait. [new() { ["minutes"] = ... }] creates the message parameter dictionary: its type is inferred from the parameter of [Flash.Deposer];
  • lines 66–70: a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username): a bot cannot keep trying indefinitely. Returning to the login page displays a new image;
  • lines 74–75: the CAPTCHA is correct: a pass (see [Auth/PasseInscriptionService.cs]) is stored in a cookie, and the browser is redirected to the form;
  • Lines 81–88: the form, only with a valid pass. Typing the address [/inscription] directly is pointless;
  • lines 96–97: creation. The form [FormulaireInscription] (file [Models]) was linked and validated by MVC;
  • lines 99–101: The pass is verified again: the request POST might have been sent without going through the form;
  • lines 104–109: the values to be redisplayed in case of an error, without the password. The default title is [Mr];
  • lines 113–116: the time limit, checked again at the time of creation;
  • lines 121–128: input errors, field by field (see Example 19). The match between the password and its confirmation—which spans two fields—is verified here manually; it is tested only if these two fields are otherwise correct. All errors are reported together: the user corrects them all at once;
  • lines 136–148: creation of the customer and their account USER, using the business layer method employed by ADMIN. If a username or first-name-last-name combination is already taken, the form is re-displayed with the relevant fields highlighted in red; the token remains valid;
  • Lines 152–154: The pass has been used: it is consumed on the server side, and its cookie is deleted. To delete a cookie, you must specify the same path ([Path]) as when it was created: the pass cookie is sent only to addresses [/inscription...]. The creation is finally counted toward the hourly limit;
  • lines 157–158: return to the login page, with the username pre-filled, and a success message. [Uri.EscapeDataString] encodes the username so it can be included in a URL;
  • line 163: the token is read from the request cookie;
  • lines 166–169: if no pass is present, return to the login page with a message;
  • lines 173–181: the form, prepared by [Validation.Preparer], is the same as those for doctors and clients. [erreurParams] is used for the parameters of the footer message (the number of minutes).

docs.title: 11.16.7. Controllers/EspacePatientController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/EspacePatientController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The patient's pages (role USER), the one they see right
// after logging in:
//
//    GE T /my-space               home page: [Gérer mon compte],
//                                   [Voir un agenda], and their upcoming appointment
//    POST /my-space/cancel        cancels the appointment SON
//    GE T /my-accou              nt account modification form
//    POST /my-accoun              t update
//    POST /my-account/delete      Delete account (and its appointments)
//
// Golden rule for this controller: the patient in question is TOUJOURS, the one associated with
// token (Patient.PatientConnecteAsync), never a username sent by the
// browser. A patient can therefore neither view, modify, nor cancel what
// belongs to another patient, even if they create their own requests.
//
// Any modification or deletion of the account requires the password
// ACTUEL: someone who finds a session that has been left open would be unable
// change the password or delete the account. Incorrect
// are counted as login failures (same limit).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Metier;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize(Roles = "USER")]
public class EspacePatientController(
    ApplicationModel application,
    AuthService authService,
    LimiteurTentativesService limiteur) : Controller
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /my-space
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("mon-espace")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Espace()
    {
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        var rendezVous = await application.GetRvAVenirClientAsync(patient.Id);
        return View("Espace", new EspaceModele
        {
            TitrePage = "ESPACE.TITLE",
            Patient = Libelles.Libelle(patient),
            RendezVous = rendezVous.Select(rv => new RendezVousVue(
                rv.Id,
                DatesWeb.FormaterJour(rv.Jour),
                DatesWeb.Horaire(rv.Creneau),
                Libelles.Libelle(rv.Creneau.Medecin),
                 // link to the doctor’s schedule for that day: the patient sees their name there
                $"/agenda?idMedecin={rv.Creneau.Medecin.Id}&jour={DatesWeb.Iso(rv.Jour)}")).ToList(),
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /my-space/cancel   field: idRv
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("mon-espace/annuler")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> AnnulerRv([FromForm] string? idRv)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        var rv = Saisie.EntierPositif(idRv) is int id ? await application.GetRvByIdAsync(id) : null;
         // a nonexistent appointment, and one for a patient with the ID AUTRE, receive
         // the same response: we do not disclose information about other people’s appointments
        if (rv is null || rv.IdClient != patient.Id)
        {
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            await application.SupprimerRvAsync(rv);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "AGENDA.CANCELLED");
        }
        return Redirect("/mon-espace");
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /my-account
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("mon-compte")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> FormulaireCompte()
    {
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        return Afficher(new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = patient.Titre,
            Prenom = patient.Prenom,
            Nom = patient.Nom,
            Login = patient.User.Login,
            Version = patient.Version,
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /my-account
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("mon-compte")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> ModifierCompte(FormulaireMonCompte formulaire)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        var valeurs = new ValeursPersonne
        {
            Titre = formulaire.Titre ?? patient.Titre,
            Prenom = formulaire.Prenom ?? "",
            Nom = formulaire.Nom ?? "",
            Login = formulaire.Login ?? "",
            Version = formulaire.Version,
        };

        var erreurs = Validation.ErreursDe(ModelState);
        if (!erreurs.ContainsKey("password") && formulaire.Password is not null && formulaire.Password != formulaire.Confirmation)
        {
            erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER";
        }
        if (erreurs.Count > 0)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, erreurs);
        }

         // the current password
        var erreurMotDePasse = await VerifierMotDePasseActuelAsync(patient, formulaire.MotDePasseActuel);
        if (erreurMotDePasse is not null)
        {
            var (cle, parametres) = erreurMotDePasse.Value;
            return Afficher(
                valeurs,
                cle == "ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD" ? new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["motDePasseActuel"] = cle } : null,
                cle,
                null,
                parametres);
        }

        try
        {
            var client = await application.ModifierClientAsync(patient.Id, new DonneesPersonne
            {
                Titre = formulaire.Titre!,
                Nom = formulaire.Nom!,
                Prenom = formulaire.Prenom!,
                Login = formulaire.Login,
                Password = formulaire.Password, // null = unchanged
                Version = formulaire.Version,
            });
             // the login and display name are DANS the token: one is issued
             // new; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name
            authService.DeposerJeton(Response, client.User);
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "MON_COMPTE.UPDATED");
            return Redirect("/mon-espace");
        }
        catch (MetierException e)
        {
            return Afficher(valeurs, null, e.Cle, Validation.ChampsErreursMetier.GetValueOrDefault(e.Cle));
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /my-account/delete   field: motDePasseSuppression
     // The account, the client, and TOUS their appointments are all deleted,
     // and then the patient is logged out.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("mon-compte/supprimer")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> SupprimerCompte([FromForm] string? motDePasseSuppression)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.PatientConnecteAsync(application, User);
        var erreurMotDePasse = await VerifierMotDePasseActuelAsync(patient, motDePasseSuppression);
        if (erreurMotDePasse is not null)
        {
            var (cle, parametres) = erreurMotDePasse.Value;
            Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Danger, cle, parametres);
            return Redirect("/mon-compte");
        }
        await application.SupprimerClientAsync(patient.Id);
        AuthService.EffacerJeton(Response);
        Flash.Deposer(HttpContext, TypeFlash.Success, "MON_COMPTE.DELETED");
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

     // null if the current password is correct; otherwise, the message key
     // (and its parameters). The return type is a nullable "tuple."
    private async Task<(string Cle, Dictionary<string, string>? Parametres)?> VerifierMotDePasseActuelAsync(
        Client patient, string? motDePasse)
    {
        var ip = AuthController.AdresseIp(HttpContext);
        var login = patient.User.Login;
        var minutes = limiteur.MinutesBlocageLogin(ip, login);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return ("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }
        var ok = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(motDePasse) && await authService.ValiderUtilisateurAsync(login, motDePasse) is not null;
        if (!ok)
        {
            limiteur.EchecLogin(ip, login);
            return ("ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD", null);
        }
        return null;
    }

    private ViewResult Afficher(
        ValeursPersonne valeurs,
        Dictionary<string, string>? erreurs = null,
        string? erreur = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? autresChamps = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? erreurParams = null) =>
        View("Compte", Validation.Preparer(
            new MonCompteModele { TitrePage = "MON_COMPTE.TITLE", Valeurs = valeurs },
            erreurs, erreur, autresChamps, erreurParams));
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 14–17: the golden rule of this controller: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token, never an identifier sent by the browser;
  • lines 35–39: reserved for patients. The controller has no [[Route]] attribute: each action provides its full address, since they do not share a prefix ([/mon-espace], [/mon-compte]);
  • lines 44–59: the “My Account” page. [Patient.PatientConnecteAsync] identifies the user based on the token; if their account has been deleted since they logged in, it triggers a [SessionInvalideException], which the [Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs] filter redirects back to the login page. The date is formatted by [DatesWeb.FormaterJour] according to the language of the request, set by the localization middleware (see Example 22); each appointment includes a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day;
  • lines 66–82: cancellation of the patient’s appointment. [condition ? valeur1 : valeur2] returns the appointment here, or [null] if the ID is invalid. A nonexistent appointment and one belonging to another patient (line 73) receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments;
  • lines 88–98: the account form, pre-filled, with the version number (optimistic lock);
  • lines 105–106: the modification process, in three steps: validation, verification of the current password, business logic;
  • lines 109–115: the values to be redisplayed in case of an error, never passwords;
  • lines 118–125: input errors. The new password is optional (blank: unchanged); its confirmation is compared only if it was entered;
  • lines 129–138: the current password. [var (cle, parametres) = ...] parses the pair returned by the verification. An incorrect password is displayed below its field and at the bottom of the page; a lockout (too many attempts) is shown only at the bottom of the page, along with the number of minutes;
  • lines 143–150: modification by the business layer, which applies the same rules as for ADMIN (uniqueness, optimistic lock);
  • line 154: the token contains the login and the display name: after a change, a new token is issued; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name;
  • lines 158–160: a rejection by the business layer re-displays the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;
  • lines 169–183: Deleting the account, which also requires the current password. An error is indicated by a pop-up message on the account page (PRG);
  • lines 180–181: Deletion of the record, the account, and all appointments (the business layer method used by ADMIN), followed by logout: the token cookie is cleared;
  • lines 190–191: verification of the current password. This returns [null] if the password is correct; otherwise, it returns a tuple: a pair of named values (the message key and its parameters). The final [?] makes this tuple “nullable”;
  • lines 195–198: The current password is subject to the same limiter as the connection (see Example 27). Someone who found a session that remained open would be unable to change the password, delete the account, or attempt passwords indefinitely;
  • lines 200–204: the authentication process itself, handled by [AuthService]; a failed authentication attempt is counted as a failed login attempt;
  • lines 209–217: the account form.

// =========================================================================
// Controllers/ErreurController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The error page (400, 403, 404, 500).
//
// You can never reach it via a link: these are the middleware components
// UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/error/{0}") and
// UseExceptionHandler("/error/500") (see Program.cs), which RÉ-EXÉCUTENT the
// failed the request with this address, to generate the page to be returned to the
// instead of an empty response or an exception.
//
// [Route] without [HttpGet]: the action accepts all methods HTTP - the
// a re-executed request retains its original method (a rejected POST remains a POST).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class ErreurController : Controller
{
    private static readonly Dictionary<int, string> Messages = new()
    {
        [StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest] = "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST",
        [StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden] = "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN",
        [StatusCodes.Status404NotFound] = "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND",
    };

    [Route("erreur/{code:int}")]
    public IActionResult Afficher(int code)
    {
         // the page retains the original error code (404 remains 404...); an
         // unexpected error becomes a 500 error
        if (code < 400 || code > 599)
        {
            code = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError;
        }
        Response.StatusCode = code;
        return View("Erreur", new ErreurModele
        {
            TitrePage = "ERROR_PAGE.TITLE",
            Code = code,
            Message = Messages.GetValueOrDefault(code, "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR"),
        });
    }
}

This is the controller from Example 24, with translated messages:

  • lines 23–28: the message key for each error code. [static readonly]: a single dictionary, created when the class is loaded and never replaced;
  • lines 30–31: [[Route]], which lacks the HTTP method, accepts all methods: a re-executed POST request (for example, a patient attempting a cancellation reserved for administrators) remains a POST request;
  • lines 35–37: a non-error code HTTP (a manually entered [/erreur/200] address) becomes a 500 error;
  • line 39: the page retains the original error code;
  • lines 40–44: the page template. [GetValueOrDefault] returns the key associated with the code, or [ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR] for any other code (500 in particular).

docs.title: 11.17. The Views
docs.text:
The views have almost nothing to decide: their template has been prepared by the controllers in the classes of the [Models/ModelesVues.cs] file (which buttons to display, which URL elements, which translation keys). Each view declares the type of its template ([@model], see Example 13): a typo in [@Model.Xxx] will cause a compilation error. Each view also begins with a comment [Razor] [@* ... *@] that describes its role; these comments do not appear in the pages sent to the browser.

One difference from the examples in Chapter 4: the case study does not use Tag Helpers. Partial views are inserted using [@await Html.PartialAsync("_Nom")], the equivalent of the [<partial name="_Nom">] tag from Example 15. A second, optional argument provides the partial view’s model; without it, the partial view receives the page’s model. The method is asynchronous (the partial view may need to be compiled or read from disk): [await] waits for its result.

@* =========================================================================
   Views/_ViewImports.cshtml
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Lu avant CHAQUE vue de ce dossier et de ses sous-dossiers : les "using"
   communs, et la classe mère de toutes les vues (Web/PageVue.cs), qui leur
   apporte @T("CLE"), Utilisateur, MessageFlash...
   TModel désigne le type du modèle de chaque vue (@model ...).
   ========================================================================= *@
@using RdvMedecins
@using RdvMedecins.Models
@using RdvMedecins.Web
@inherits RdvMedecins.Web.PageVue<TModel>
  • lines 9–11: the namespaces whose types are used by the views: the view templates ([RdvMedecins.Models]), the flash messages ([RdvMedecins.Web]);
  • line 12: the parent class of all views, [Web/PageVue.cs], as in Example 22. It provides them with the translation [@T("CLE")], the language [Langue], the logged-in user [Utilisateur], the flash message [MessageFlash], the requested path [Chemin], and the method [Actif] (active menu item in the navigation bar). In version [NestJS], this information was passed through [res.locals]. There is no [@addTagHelper] directive: the application does not use Tag Helpers.
