  • lines 12–17: [Request.Form] contains the fields of a HTML form (body type [application/x-www-form-urlencoded]), without any binding or conversion. [Request.ContentType] is the body type;
  • lines 23–25: [[FromBody]] instructs the system to read the request body as a JSON document (this is what a [JavaScript] client sends). [JsonElement] represents any JSON document; a class could have been declared;
  • lines 30–32: [[FromForm]]: a field in the form;
  • lines 37–43: the entire form, bound and validated by the [PersonneModele] class from Example 08.

The [-d] option of [curl] sends a POST request with a body in the format of a HTML ([application/x-www-form-urlencoded]):

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42" http://localhost:5000/post/action01

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"typeRecu":"application/x-www-form-urlencoded","champs":{"nom":"martin","age":"42"}}

The same content in JSON format:

curl -i -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nom":"martin","age":42}' http://localhost:5000/post/action02

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"typeRecu":"application/json","corps":{"nom":"martin","age":42}}

(for [Windows], enter [-d "{\"nom\":\"martin\",\"age\":42}"] at the command prompt). The age is a string in the first case (a HTML form carries only text) and a number in the second. A [[FromBody]] action rejects a body that is not in the JSON format, returning a 415 error ([Unsupported Media Type]):

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42" http://localhost:5000/post/action02

HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Length: 0

The other two actions:

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42" http://localhost:5000/post/action03

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

nom = [martin]

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42&titre=Mme" http://localhost:5000/post/action04

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"personne":{"nom":"martin","age":42,"titre":"Mme","email":null},"valide":true,"erreurs":[]}

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=200" http://localhost:5000/post/action04

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"personne":{"nom":"martin","age":200,"titre":null,"email":null},"valide":false,"erreurs":["l'âge doit être compris entre 0 et 150","le titre est obligatoire","titre inconnu"]}

An action POST returns a 200 status code, just like an action GET ([NestJS], on the other hand, returned a 201 by default). For a HTML application, a POST action responds either with a page (the form redisplayed) or with a redirect (see Example 20).

docs.title: 3.6. Example 12: Custom Binding and Validation
docs.text:
You can extend the template binding and validation. The case study makes moderate use of these features, but understanding them helps you grasp how [ASP.NET Core] works.

12-liaison-perso/
├── Controllers/
│   └── ExemplesController.cs
├── Liaison/
│   ├── DateFrBinder.cs
│   ├── LangueBinder.cs
│   └── SansEspaceAttribute.cs
├── appsettings.json
├── Exemple12.csproj
└── Program.cs

docs.title: 3.6.1. A model binder: DateFrBinder
docs.text:
A model binder is the object that constructs a parameter’s value from the request. [ASP.NET Core] provides them for all common types; you can write your own. The file [Liaison/DateFrBinder.cs]:

using System.Globalization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;

namespace Exemple12.Liaison;

// a "model binder": converts a French date "23/09/2026" to DateOnly
public class DateFrBinder : IModelBinder
{
    public Task BindModelAsync(ModelBindingContext contexte)
    {
         // the raw value, found in URL, the form, the route...
        var brut = contexte.ValueProvider.GetValue(contexte.ModelName).FirstValue;
        if (DateOnly.TryParseExact(brut, "dd/MM/yyyy", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out var date))
        {
             // success: the value that the action will receive
            contexte.Result = ModelBindingResult.Success(date);
        }
        else
        {
             // failure: an error in ModelState ("02/31/2026" is also rejected)
            contexte.ModelState.AddModelError(contexte.ModelName, $"[{brut}] n'est pas une date jj/mm/aaaa valide");
        }
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
  • line 7: a model binder implements the [IModelBinder] interface;
  • line 9: its method [BindModelAsync] receives the binding context: the parameter name ([ModelName]), the value sources ([ValueProvider]: URL, the form, the route...), [ModelState]...;
  • line 12: the raw value of the parameter ([FirstValue]: the first one, if there are multiple);
  • lines 13–16: [DateOnly.TryParseExact] converts a string in the [jj/mm/aaaa] format to [DateOnly] (a date without a time), and returns [false] if this is impossible, including for a date that does not exist (02/31/2026). If successful, [ModelBindingResult.Success(date)] provides the value that the action will receive;
  • line 21: if the operation fails, an error is added to [ModelState];
  • line 23: the method is asynchronous by nature ([Task]), but there is nothing to wait for: it returns a task that has already completed.

docs.title: 3.6.2. A second model binder: LangueBinder
docs.text:
A parameter may come from somewhere other than URL or the form. The file [Liaison/LangueBinder.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;

namespace Exemple12.Liaison;

// the browser’s preferred language, read from the header
// "Accept-Language: fr-FR,fr;q=0.9,en;q=0.8" -> "fr"
public class LangueBinder : IModelBinder
{
    public Task BindModelAsync(ModelBindingContext contexte)
    {
        var entete = contexte.HttpContext.Request.Headers.AcceptLanguage.ToString();
        var premiere = entete.Split(',')[0].Trim();
        var langue = premiere.Length >= 2 ? premiere[..2].ToLowerInvariant() : "fr";
        contexte.Result = ModelBindingResult.Success(langue);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}
  • line 11: the [Accept-Language] header, which specifies the user’s preferred languages;
  • lines 12–13: the first two letters of the first language. [premiere[..2]] is a range ([range]): the characters with indices 0 and 1.

docs.title: 3.6.3. A validation attribute: [SansEspace]
docs.text:
The file [Liaison/SansEspaceAttribute.cs]:

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

namespace Exemple12.Liaison;

// a "custom" validation attribute: [SansEspace]
public class SansEspaceAttribute : ValidationAttribute
{
    public SansEspaceAttribute() : base("le champ {0} ne doit pas contenir d'espace")
    {
    }

    public override bool IsValid(object? valeur)
    {
         // null is accepted: it is the role of [Required] to require it
        return valeur is not string texte || !texte.Contains(' ');
    }
}
  • line 6: a validation attribute inherits from [ValidationAttribute]. By convention, the name of an attribute class ends with [Attribute], which is omitted in practice: [[SansEspace]];
  • line 8: the default error message, passed to the parent class. [{0}] will be replaced by the field name;
  • Lines 12–15: The rule. [valeur is not string texte]: If the value is not a string ([null], for example), it is accepted; otherwise, it is assigned to the variable [texte], which must not contain any spaces. The case study has an attribute of this type: [[Parmi]].

docs.title: 3.6.4. The controller
docs.text:
The file [Controllers/ExemplesController.cs]:

using Exemple12.Liaison;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple12.Controllers;

[Route("exemples")]
public class ExemplesController : Controller
{
     // /examples/calendar?day=9/23/2026: a custom model binder
    [HttpGet("agenda")]
    public IActionResult Agenda([ModelBinder(typeof(DateFrBinder))] DateOnly jour)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(ModelState[nameof(jour)]!.Errors[0].ErrorMessage);
        }
        return Ok($"agenda du jour [{jour:yyyy-MM-dd}]");
    }

     // /examples/hello: a parameter that does not come from URL, but from a header
    [HttpGet("bonjour")]
    public string Bonjour([ModelBinder(typeof(LangueBinder))] string langue)
    {
        return langue == "en" ? "Hello!" : "Bonjour !";
    }

     // /examples/search?motCle=aspnet: a custom validation attribute
    [HttpGet("recherche")]
    public IActionResult Recherche([SansEspace] string? motCle)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(ModelState[nameof(motCle)]!.Errors[0].ErrorMessage);
        }
        return Ok($"recherche de [{motCle}]");
    }
}
  • line 11: the attribute [[ModelBinder]] specifies the model binder to be used for this parameter;
  • line 15: an invalid date results in a 400 error, with the message from the model binder;
  • line 22: the parameter [langue] is provided by the second model binder;
  • line 29: A validation attribute can also be applied directly to an action parameter.

The results:

curl -i "http://localhost:5000/exemples/agenda?jour=23/09/2026"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

agenda du jour [2026-09-23]

curl -i "http://localhost:5000/exemples/agenda?jour=2026-09-23"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

[2026-09-23] n'est pas une date jj/mm/aaaa valide

curl -i "http://localhost:5000/exemples/agenda?jour=31/02/2026"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

[31/02/2026] n'est pas une date jj/mm/aaaa valide

curl -i -H "Accept-Language: fr-FR,fr;q=0.9" http://localhost:5000/examples/hello

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Bonjour !

curl -i -H "Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9" http://localhost:5000/examples/hello

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Hello!

(The [-H] option of [curl] adds a header to the request)

curl -i "http://localhost:5000/exemples/recherche?motCle=aspnet"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

recherche de [aspnet]

curl -i "http://localhost:5000/exemples/recherche?motCle=asp%20net"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

le champ motCle ne doit pas contenir d'espace

([%20] encodes a space in a URL)

docs.title: 3.6.5. Conclusion
docs.text: The action template is constructed by the template binding based on the request: route parameters, URL, form fields, JSON body, and headers. The values are converted to the parameter types and then validated against the attributes. The result of these two steps is stored in [ModelState]. For a server JSON, [[ApiController]] automatically rejects an invalid model; for a HTML application, the action itself tests [ModelState.IsValid] (example 09) so that the form can be redisplayed. This is the subject of the next chapter.

docs.title: 7. The lifecycle of a request
docs.text:
Between the arrival of a request and the execution of the action, [ASP.NET Core] involves several types of objects, each with a specific role. We have already encountered some of them: middleware ([UseStaticFiles], [UseRequestLocalization], the middleware from Example 23), and the model binding ([IModelBinder], Example 12). The MVC component adds filters that run around the action. The case study uses each of them:

ObjectRoleIn the case studymiddlewarePrepares the request; does not yet know the actionstatic files, language, authentication (reading the token), error pagesauthorization filterallow or deny access to the action[[Authorize]], [[Authorize(Roles = ...)]]Template bindingConvert and validate parametersforms, [ModelState]action filterCode before and after the action(not used: services and the view parent class are sufficient)exception filterConvert an exception into a responseSession expired: redirect to /login

docs.title: 7.1. Example 24: The steps in processing a request
docs.text:
Example 24 has an action that calculates the square of a number, and one object of each type. Each writes a line to the console, so we can see the order in which they are executed.

24-cycle-de-vie/
├── Controllers/
│   ├── CalculController.cs
│   └── ErreurController.cs
├── Filtres/
│   ├── BloquerAttribute.cs
│   ├── ChronoAttribute.cs
│   ├── EntierBinder.cs
│   ├── JournalMiddleware.cs
│   └── PageErreurFilter.cs
├── Views/
│   ├── Calcul/
│   │   └── Resultat.cshtml
│   ├── Shared/
│   │   ├── _Layout.cshtml
│   │   └── Erreur.cshtml
│   └── _ViewStart.cshtml
├── appsettings.json
├── Exemple24.csproj
└── Program.cs

The file [Filtres/JournalMiddleware.cs]:

namespace Exemple24.Filtres;

// a middleware class: it receives the rest of the pipeline
// (next) in its constructor, and processes each request in InvokeAsync
public class JournalMiddleware(RequestDelegate next)
{
    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext contexte)
    {
        Console.WriteLine();
        Console.WriteLine($"--- {contexte.Request.Method} {contexte.Request.Path}{contexte.Request.QueryString}");
        Console.WriteLine("1. middleware (avant)");
        await next(contexte); // the entire rest of the pipeline: routing, filters, action, view
        Console.WriteLine($"8. middleware (après : code {contexte.Response.StatusCode})");
    }
}
  • Line 5: A middleware can be a class. Its constructor takes a [RequestDelegate]: the rest of the pipeline (the subsequent middlewares, followed by MVC);
  • line 7: the [InvokeAsync] method is called for each request;
  • line 12: the middleware calls the rest of the pipeline and waits for it to finish. If it did not call it, the request would stop there (it would then have to generate the response itself). The code placed before this call executes on the outbound request, and the code placed after it executes on the return: the middleware “wraps” everything else and sees the final status code of the response.

The file [Filtres/BloquerAttribute.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Controllers;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Filters;

namespace Exemple24.Filtres;

// an AUTORISATION filter: it determines whether the action can be executed.
// It is also an attribute: it is applied to a controller or an action.
public class BloquerAttribute : Attribute, IAuthorizationFilter
{
    public void OnAuthorization(AuthorizationFilterContext contexte)
    {
         // The filter knows the target action, unlike middleware
        var action = (ControllerActionDescriptor)contexte.ActionDescriptor;
        Console.WriteLine($"2. filtre d'autorisation (action visée : {action.ActionName})");
        if (contexte.HttpContext.Request.Query.ContainsKey("bloquer"))
        {
             // Setting `Result` short-circuits the rest of the process: no binding, no action
            contexte.Result = new StatusCodeResult(StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden);
        }
    }
}
  • line 9: an authorization filter implements [IAuthorizationFilter]. The class also derives from [Attribute]: it can be applied, in square brackets, to a controller or an action;
  • lines 14–15: Unlike middleware, the filter knows the target action ([ActionDescriptor]). This is what allows the [[Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")]] attribute (see the next chapter) to protect only certain actions;
  • lines 16–19: A filter rejects the request by setting [contexte.Result]: the sequence (binding, action) is not executed, and this result becomes the response. Here, a 403 response (access denied), with no content.

The file [Filtres/EntierBinder.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;

namespace Exemple24.Filtres;

// Model binding for an integer parameter (see Example 12)
public class EntierBinder : IModelBinder
{
    public Task BindModelAsync(ModelBindingContext contexte)
    {
        var valeur = contexte.ValueProvider.GetValue(contexte.ModelName).FirstValue;
        Console.WriteLine($"3. liaison de modèle (valeur reçue : \"{valeur}\")");
        if (int.TryParse(valeur, out var entier))
        {
            contexte.Result = ModelBindingResult.Success(entier);
        }
        else
        {
            contexte.ModelState.AddModelError(contexte.ModelName, $"\"{valeur}\" n'est pas un nombre entier.");
        }
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

A custom template binding, like those in Example 12. An invalid value does not stop anything: the error is logged in [ModelState], and the action determines the outcome (line 18).

The file [Filtres/ChronoAttribute.cs]:

using System.Diagnostics;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Filters;

namespace Exemple24.Filtres;

// an ACTION filter: code before and after the action.
// ActionFilterAttribute: a framework class, whose useful methods are redefined
public class ChronoAttribute : ActionFilterAttribute
{
    private const string Cle = "chrono";

    public override void OnActionExecuting(ActionExecutingContext contexte)
    {
         // The action’s parameters are already bound: the filter can read them
        Console.WriteLine($"4. filtre d'action (avant ; paramètres : {string.Join(", ", contexte.ActionArguments.Values)})");
        contexte.HttpContext.Items[Cle] = Stopwatch.StartNew();
    }

    public override void OnActionExecuted(ActionExecutedContext contexte)
    {
        var chrono = (Stopwatch)contexte.HttpContext.Items[Cle]!;
         // contexte.Exception: any exception thrown by the action
        var issue = contexte.Exception is null ? "" : $", exception {contexte.Exception.GetType().Name}";
        Console.WriteLine($"6. filtre d'action (après, {chrono.ElapsedMilliseconds} ms{issue})");
    }
}
  • line 8: an action filter. [ActionFilterAttribute] is a framework class that already implements the necessary interfaces: we override ([override]) the relevant methods;
  • Lines 12–16: [OnActionExecuting] runs before the action. Model binding has already taken place: the action parameters are available ([ActionArguments]). A timer is started ([Stopwatch]), stored in [HttpContext.Items] (query scope; see Chapter 6);
  • lines 19–24: [OnActionExecuted] runs after the action. If the action threw an exception, it is available in [contexte.Exception]. An action filter can also override the result of the action ([contexte.Result]).

The file [Filtres/PageErreurFilter.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Filters;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures;

namespace Exemple24.Filtres;

// an EXCEPTIONS filter: it transforms an exception into a response
public class PageErreurFilter(IModelMetadataProvider metadonnees) : IExceptionFilter
{
    public void OnException(ExceptionContext contexte)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"x. filtre d'exceptions ({contexte.Exception.GetType().Name} : {contexte.Exception.Message})");
         // Instead of the default error page, our Error view is displayed, with status code 500
        contexte.Result = new ViewResult
        {
            ViewName = "Erreur",
            StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError,
            ViewData = new ViewDataDictionary(metadonnees, contexte.ModelState) { Model = 500 },
        };
        contexte.ExceptionHandled = true; // The exception is handled: it does not propagate further up the chain
    }
}
  • Line 9: An exception filter implements [IExceptionFilter]. It receives exceptions thrown by the model binding, the action filters, and the action. This is a service: it receives the [IModelMetadataProvider] object via injection, which is necessary to construct the [ViewData] dictionary for a view;
  • lines 15–20: instead of the default error page, the filter generates a HTML page: the [Erreur] view, with status code 500. This is what the [View] method of a controller does, written here by hand;
  • Line 21: The exception is marked as handled; it does not propagate further up the chain.

The file [Program.cs]:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Exemple24.Filtres;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(options =>
{
     //: a GLOBAL filter: it applies to all actions in the application
    options.Filters.Add<PageErreurFilter>();
});
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));

var app = builder.Build();

// The middleware runs in the order in which it is added
app.UseMiddleware<JournalMiddleware>();
// an error response SANS with content (400, 403, 404...): the request is re-executed
// request with the URL /error/{code}, which generates a page
app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/erreur/{0}");
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "commun", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • line 10: a global filter is applied to all actions in the application. It is added to the options of MVC;
  • line 17: a class-based middleware is added via [UseMiddleware]. Middlewares execute in the order they are added: this one is first, so it processes all requests;
  • line 20: a framework middleware. When an error response (codes 400–599) has no content, it re-executes the request using the address [/erreur/{code}] (where [{0}] is replaced by the code), and returns the resulting page while retaining the error code. This is how 403 responses from the authorization filter, 400 responses from the action, and 404 responses from routing become HTML pages.

The [Controllers/CalculController.cs] file:

using Exemple24.Filtres;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple24.Controllers;

// Two filters set on the controller: they apply to all of its actions
[Bloquer]
[Chrono]
public class CalculController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("carre/{n}")]
    public IActionResult Carre([ModelBinder(typeof(EntierBinder))] int n)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"5. action Carre({n}) ; modèle valide : {ModelState.IsValid}");
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(); // A 400 with no content: see UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute
        }
        if (n == 13)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("13 porte malheur"); // an “unexpected” error
        }
        return View("Resultat", n * n);
    }
}
  • lines 7–8: two filters applied to the controller; they apply to all of its actions (they can also be applied to a single action);
  • line 12: the custom parameter binding;
  • lines 15–17: an invalid parameter: a 400 response with no content;
  • lines 19–21: an “unexpected” error, to see the exception filter in action.

The file [Controllers/ErreurController.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple24.Controllers;

public class ErreurController : Controller
{
     // [Route] without the HTTP method: the re-executed request retains its original method
    [Route("erreur/{code:int}")]
    public IActionResult Afficher(int code)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"7. page d'erreur {code} (requête ré-exécutée)");
        Response.StatusCode = code; // the page retains the error code
        return View("Erreur", code);
    }
}
  • line 8: the action for the error page. [[Route]], without a method; HTTP, accepts all methods: a re-executed POST request remains a POST request;
  • Line 12: The page retains the original error code.

The file [Views/Shared/Erreur.cshtml]:

@* la page d'erreur ; son modèle : le code d'erreur *@
@model int
@{
    var message = Model switch
    {
        400 => "Requête incorrecte.",
        403 => "Accès refusé.",
        404 => "Page introuvable.",
        _ => "Erreur interne du serveur.",
    };
}
<div class="alert alert-danger">
  <h1 class="h4">Erreur @Model</h1>
  <p class="mb-0">@message</p>
</div>
  • Lines 4–10: a switch expression [C#]: it returns the value of the first branch whose pattern matches the template. [_] corresponds to everything else. The view is in [Views/Shared]: it is found regardless of the controller ([CalculController] for the exception filter, [ErreurController] otherwise).

Five requests: a normal calculation (http://localhost:5000/carre/7), an invalid parameter ([/carre/abc]), a request blocked by the authorization filter ([/carre/7?bloquer=1]), an unexpected error ([/carre/13]), and an unknown address ([/inconnue]). The server console:

--- GET /carre/7
1. middleware (avant)
2. filtre d'autorisation (action visée : Carre)
3. liaison de modèle (valeur reçue : "7")
4. filtre d'action (avant ; paramètres : 7)
5. action Carre(7) ; modèle valide : True
6. filtre d'action (après, 0 ms)
8. middleware (après : code 200)

--- GET /carre/abc
1. middleware (avant)
2. filtre d'autorisation (action visée : Carre)
3. liaison de modèle (valeur reçue : "abc")
4. filtre d'action (avant ; paramètres : )
5. action Carre(0) ; modèle valide : False
6. filtre d'action (après, 0 ms)
7. page d'erreur 400 (requête ré-exécutée)
8. middleware (après : code 400)

--- GET /carre/7?bloquer=1
1. middleware (avant)
2. filtre d'autorisation (action visée : Carre)
7. page d'erreur 403 (requête ré-exécutée)
8. middleware (après : code 403)

--- GET /carre/13
1. middleware (avant)
2. filtre d'autorisation (action visée : Carre)
3. liaison de modèle (valeur reçue : "13")
4. filtre d'action (avant ; paramètres : 13)
5. action Carre(13) ; modèle valide : True
6. filtre d'action (après, 0 ms, exception InvalidOperationException)
x. filtre d'exceptions (InvalidOperationException : 13 porte malheur)
8. middleware (après : code 500)

--- GET /inconnue
1. middleware (avant)
7. page d'erreur 404 (requête ré-exécutée)
8. middleware (après : code 404)

This log shows:

  • the order of the steps: middleware, authorization filter, model binding, action filter (before), action, action filter (after), and then the middleware again, which sees the final response code;
  • the authorization filter that rejects the request bypasses the rest of MVC (no binding, no action);
  • an invalid parameter does not prevent the action from executing: the action itself decides, based on [ModelState] (see example 09);
  • an exception from the action is handled by the exception filter, which generates the response;
  • an empty error response (400, 403, 404) is converted into a page by re-executing the request (step 7). For an unknown address, MVC does not even come into play: no route matches.

The resulting pages:

Let's check that the error code is preserved:

curl -i http://localhost:5000/carre/7?block=1

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Cycle de vie</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3">
    <div class="alert alert-danger">
  <h1 class="h4">Erreur 403</h1>
  <p class="mb-0">Accès refusé.</p>
</div>

  </div>
</body>
</html>

The case study combines these mechanisms: [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/erreur/{0}")] and a controller ([ErreurController]) for 400, 403, and 404 pages; the [UseExceptionHandler("/erreur/500")] middleware, which similarly re-executes any request that ends with an unhandled exception; and an exception filter ([Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs]) for a specific case: an expired session does not display an error page but redirects to the login page.

docs.title: 4. The View and Its Model
docs.text: Up to this point, actions have generated their own responses. In a MVC application, this is the role of a view: a file that describes the page HTML, with placeholders for the data passed to it by the action—the view’s template. [ASP.NET Core MVC] uses the [Razor] view engine: A view is a [.cshtml] file, derived from HTML, into which [C#] code is inserted, preceded by the character [@]. [Razor] is part of the framework: there is nothing to install.

docs.title: 4.1. Example 13: An Initial View
docs.text:
The [Program.cs] file:

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// MVC services: ET controllers and Razor views
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • Line 4: [AddControllersWithViews] replaces [AddControllers] from the previous examples. It adds view services to the controller services: the [Razor] engine, view file search, and Tag Helpers (Example 15).

The view template is a simple class. The file [Models/PageModele.cs]:

namespace Exemple13.Models;

// the view model: the data that the action passes to the view
public record PageModele(string Titre, string Message, string Heure);
  • line 4: a [record] is a class whose properties are set by the constructor; here, three strings: [Titre], [Message], and [Heure]. This is a concise way to define a class that simply carries data.

The file [Controllers/VuesController.cs]:

using Exemple13.Models;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple13.Controllers;

public class VuesController : Controller
{
     // View(model): the view named after the action (Views/Vues/Index.cshtml)
    [HttpGet("/")]
    public IActionResult Index()
    {
        var modele = new PageModele(
            "Ma première vue",
            "Cette page a été fabriquée par Razor, sur le serveur.",
            DateTime.Now.ToString("HH:mm:ss"));
        return View(modele);
    }

     // View(name, model): the view is selected by the action
    [HttpGet("bonjour/{nom}")]
    public IActionResult Bonjour(string nom)
    {
        if (nom == "inconnu")
        {
            Response.StatusCode = 404;
            return View("Inconnu", nom);
        }
        var modele = new PageModele(
            $"Bonjour {nom}",
            "Cette fois, l'action a désigné la vue par son nom.",
            DateTime.Now.ToString("HH:mm:ss"));
        return View("Index", modele);
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Line 6: The controller derives from class [Controller], rather than [ControllerBase]: [Controller] adds to [ControllerBase] everything related to views (methods [View], [ViewData], [TempData], etc.);
  • lines 12–15: the action generates the view template: a title, a message, and the current time;
  • line 16: [View(modele)] returns a [ViewResult]: the action no longer generates the response; instead, it designates a view and passes a template to it. If no view name is specified, the view with the same name as the action is used: [Index];
  • lines 23–26: When the view depends on the request, the action selects the view. Here, the name [inconnu] displays the view [Inconnu], with status code 404. The template for this view is a simple string;
  • line 32: the action [Bonjour] explicitly specifies the view [Index] by name: two actions share the same view, with different templates.

Where does [ASP.NET Core] look for the view [Index] for action [VuesController.Index]? By convention, in two folders, in this order:

  • [Views/Vues/Index.cshtml]: the folder named after the controller (without the suffix [Controller]);
  • [Views/Shared/Index.cshtml]: the folder containing views shared by all controllers (see Example 15).

If the view is not found anywhere, an exception lists the paths that were checked. The project files:

13-premiere-vue/
├── Controllers/
│   └── VuesController.cs
├── Models/
│   └── PageModele.cs
├── Views/
│   ├── Vues/
│   │   ├── Inconnu.cshtml
│   │   └── Index.cshtml
│   └── _ViewImports.cshtml
├── appsettings.json
├── Exemple13.csproj
└── Program.cs

The file [Views/_ViewImports.cshtml]:

@* les "using" communs à toutes les vues du dossier Views *@
@using Exemple13.Models
  • Line 1: [@* ... *@] is a comment [Razor]: it does not appear on the generated page (unlike a comment HTML [<!-- -->]);
  • Line 2: The directives in the [_ViewImports.cshtml] file apply to all views in its folder and subfolders. [@using Exemple13.Models] allows you to write [PageModele] instead of [Exemple13.Models.PageModele] in the views.

The [Views/Vues/Index.cshtml] file:

@* le type du modèle de cette vue *@
@model PageModele
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>@Model.Titre</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>@Model.Titre</h1>
  <p>@Model.Message</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à @Model.Heure.</p>
</body>
</html>
  • line 2: the directive [@model] declares the type of the view template. In the view, the property [Model] is then of type [PageModele], and the compiler verifies that [Model.Titre] exists;
  • Lines 7–12: Each expression [@Model.Titre] is replaced by the corresponding value from the template. [Razor] recognizes the end of an expression on its own: in [@Model.Heure.], the period is followed by a tag, so it is not a property access.

A view is a [C#] file in disguise: when the project is compiled ([dotnet build]), each [.cshtml] file is translated into a [C#] class, which is compiled along with the rest of the application. An error in a view ([@Model.Titr]) is therefore reported during compilation. The result, in the URLhttp://localhost:5000/:

The source code of the page received by the browser no longer contains any trace of [Razor]:

curl http://localhost:5000/

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Ma premiè view </title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Ma premiè view </title>
  <p>Cette page a été generated by Razor on the server.</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à 12:12:36.</p>
</body>
</html>

Note that the accented characters inserted by the expression [@] have been encoded: [è] is the code for the character [è]. The text typed directly into the view ([Page fabriquée à]) remained unchanged. The browser displays both correctly, but the code HTML is difficult to read. We’ll see in Example 15 how to avoid this. The URL http://localhost:5000/bonjour/martin displays the same view using a different template:

and http://localhost:5000/bonjour/inconnu displays a different view:

curl -i http://localhost:5000/hello/unknown

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inconnu</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Personne ne s'appelle [inconnu] ici.</h1>
</body>
</html>

The file [Views/Vues/Inconnu.cshtml]:

@* le modèle de cette vue est une simple chaîne : le nom demandé *@
@model string
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inconnu</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Personne ne s'appelle [@Model] ici.</h1>
</body>
</html>
  • Line 2: The template for this view is a string;
  • line 10: [@Model] is the string itself.

docs.title: 4.2. Example 14: The Razor language
docs.text:
[Razor] is not a “logic-free” template language like [Handlebars]: you can write [C#] code within a view (conditions, loops, variables, method calls). This freedom requires discipline: the view must remain purely for formatting; calculations and decisions belong to the action and the services. Example 14 provides an overview of the syntax. The template, file [Models/BasesModele.cs]:

namespace Exemple14.Models;

public record Produit(string Nom, decimal Prix, bool EnStock);

public record Adresse(string Rue, string Ville);

public class BasesModele
{
    public string Titre { get; set; } = "";
    public string Nom { get; set; } = "";
    public string? Surnom { get; set; }
    public string Html { get; set; } = "";
    public bool Connecte { get; set; }
    public string Devise { get; set; } = "";
    public List<Produit> Produits { get; set; } = [];
    public List<Produit> Panier { get; set; } = [];
    public Adresse Adresse { get; set; } = new("", "");
}

The file [Controllers/BasesController.cs]:

using Exemple14.Models;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple14.Controllers;

public class BasesController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("/")]
    public IActionResult Index()
    {
        var modele = new BasesModele
        {
            Titre = "Les bases de Razor",
            Nom = "Martin",
            Surnom = null,
            Html = "<b>ceci est du HTML</b>",
            Connecte = true,
            Devise = "€",
            Produits =
            [
                new Produit("Clavier", 25m, true),
                new Produit("Souris", 12.5m, false),
                new Produit("Écran", 149m, true),
            ],
            Panier = [],
            Adresse = new Adresse("12 rue des Lilas", "Angers"),
        };
        return View(modele);
    }
}
  • Lines 11–26: The action populates the template: a few strings, a Boolean, a list of three products, an empty shopping cart, and an address. [Surnom] is intentionally the same as [null].

The view, file [Views/Bases/Index.cshtml]:

@model BasesModele
@* un bloc de code C#: it doesn't produce anything on the page *@
@{
    var total = Model.Produits.Sum(p => p.Prix);
    var nombre = Model.Produits.Count;
}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>@Model.Titre</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>@Model.Titre</h1>
  @* 1. afficher une valeur du modèle ; une valeur null n'affiche rien *@
  <p>1. Nom : @Model.Nom - surnom : [@Model.Surnom]</p>
  @* 2. @ échappe le HTML, @Html.Raw l'insère tel quel *@
  <p>2a. @Model.Html</p>
  <p>2b. @Html.Raw(Model.Html)</p>
  @* 3. une condition *@
  @if (Model.Connecte)
  {
    <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
  }
  else
  {
    <p>3. Vous n'êtes pas connecté.</p>
  }
  @* 4. une boucle ; les variables de la boucle sont des variables C# *@
  <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
    @for (var i = 0; i < Model.Produits.Count; i++)
    {
      var produit = Model.Produits[i];
      <li>n° @i : @produit.Nom, @produit.Prix @Model.Devise
        @(produit.EnStock ? "(en stock)" : "(épuisé)")
        @if (i == 0) { <text>- le premier</text> }
        @if (i == Model.Produits.Count - 1) { @:- le dernier, vu par @Model.Nom
        }
      </li>
    }
  </ul>
  @* 5. la liste vide *@
  <p>5. Votre panier :
    @if (Model.Panier.Count == 0)
    {
      <text>il est vide.</text>
    }
    else
    {
      foreach (var p in Model.Panier) { <span>@p.Nom</span> }
    }
  </p>
  @* 6. une expression explicite @( ... ), et les variables du bloc @{ } *@
  <p>6. @nombre produits, pour un total de @(total) @Model.Devise ; prix moyen : @((total / nombre).ToString("0.00")) @Model.Devise</p>
  <p>7. Adresse : @Model.Adresse.Rue, @Model.Adresse.Ville.ToUpper()</p>
  <p>8. Une adresse électronique : contact@exemple.fr</p>
</body>
</html>

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 2–5: A block of code named [@{ ... }] contains instructions named [C#]. It does not produce anything on the page. The variables it declares ([total], [nombre]) can be used later in the view;
  • line 16: a value [null] ([@Model.Surnom]) displays nothing, with no error;
  • Lines 18–19: An expression [@...] escapes the special characters in HTML ([<] becomes [<]...): the text is displayed as-is. [@Html.Raw(...)] inserts it without escaping: it is interpreted as HTML. [Html.Raw] is used only for HTML generated by the application, never for data entered by a user: the user could inject HTML, or even [JavaScript], into the page (an attack known as [XSS], [cross-site scripting]);
  • Lines 21–27: a condition. After [@if (...)], the content within the curly braces is HTML: [Razor] recognizes the start of a tag and reverts to HTML mode. We return to [C#] via [@];
  • lines 32–40: a loop from [for] to [C#]. [var produit = ...] is an instruction [C#], [<li>] of HTML: [Razor] alternates between the two without any specific marker;
  • Line 36: an explicit expression [@( ... )]. Parentheses are required whenever the expression contains spaces or operators (in this case, the conditional operator [? :]);
  • line 37: To write unformatted text within a [C#] block, enclose it in the special tag [<text>], which does not appear on the page;
  • line 38: [@:] does the same thing for the rest of the line;
  • lines 45–51: An empty list is simply [if]. In the [else] block, already in [C#] mode, [foreach] is written without [@];
  • line 55: the variables of the [@{ }] block and explicit expressions, including a method call: [ToString("0.00")] formats a number with two decimal places;
  • line 56: a pointed path [@Model.Adresse.Rue], and a method call [ToUpper()];
  • line 57: [Razor] recognizes that a [@] placed between two alphanumeric characters is not code: [contact@exemple.fr] is an email address. To write a [@] that would be ambiguous, we duplicate it: [@@].

The result, URL, is http://localhost:5000/:

The code HTML produces:

curl http://localhost:5000/

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Les bases de Razor</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Les bases de Razor</h1>
  <p>1. Nom : Martin - surnom : []</p>
  <p>2a. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
  <p>2b. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
    <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
  <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
      <li>n° 0 : Clavier, 25 €
        (en stock)
- le premier      </li>
      <li>n° 1 : Souris, 12.5 €
        (éthené)
      </li>
      <li>n° 2 : Éscreen, 149 €
        (en stock)
 - le dernier, vu par Martin
      </li>
  </ul>
  <p>5. Votre panier :
il est vide.  </p>
  <p>6. 3 produits, pour un total de 186.5 € ; average price: 62.17 €</p>
  <p>7. Adresse : 12 rue des Lilas, ANGERS</p>
  <p>8. Une adresse électronique : contact@exemple.fr</p>
</body>
</html>

Note the spaces and blank lines left by the [C#] instructions: they have no effect on the display. We also see the encoding of accented characters derived from expressions ([€] for [€], [é] for [é]), which is corrected in the following example.

docs.title: 4.3. Example 15: Template, Partial Views, Static Files
docs.text:
The pages of a website share a common template (header, navigation bar, footer). [Razor] refers to this template as a “layout”: each view is inserted into it. Reusable page components are partial views. Finally, pages require static files (style sheets, images, scripts), which are served as-is, without going through a controller. The files in the example:

15-gabarit/
├── Controllers/
│   └── PagesController.cs
├── Views/
│   ├── Pages/
│   │   ├── Accueil.cshtml
│   │   ├── Brute.cshtml
│   │   └── Equipe.cshtml
│   ├── Shared/
│   │   ├── _Carte.cshtml
│   │   ├── _Layout.cshtml
│   │   └── _Navbar.cshtml
│   ├── _ViewImports.cshtml
│   └── _ViewStart.cshtml
├── wwwroot/
│   └── css/
│       └── styles.css
├── appsettings.json
├── Exemple15.csproj
└── Program.cs

The file [Program.cs]:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();
// Razor writes accented characters exactly as they appear (not "é") ;
// < > & " ' remain escaped
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));

var app = builder.Build();

// 1. Static files in the wwwroot folder: wwwroot/css/styles.css is served at /css/styles.css
app.UseStaticFiles();
// 2. Bootstrap, shared by the examples: the examples/common/bootstrap folder is served at /bootstrap
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "commun", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 9: the [HtmlEncoder] service is the one used by [Razor] to escape the expressions in [@]. By default, it only allows characters from the basic Latin alphabet to pass through: this is what encoded [é] as [é]. We replace this service with an encoder that allows all characters to pass through ([UnicodeRanges.All]). The dangerous characters ([<], [>], [&], ["], [']) remain escaped: the protection against injection in HTML remains intact. All of the following examples, as well as the case study, include this line;
  • line 14: a middleware component (see Chapter 7) that serves files from the [wwwroot] folder of the project: the file [wwwroot/css/styles.css] is served to URL and [/css/styles.css]. If the file does not exist, the request continues on to the controllers;
  • Lines 16–19: A second static file service. The CSS [Bootstrap] framework is common to all examples: it is stored only once, in the [exemples/commun/bootstrap] folder, and served under the prefix [/bootstrap]. [PhysicalFileProvider] refers to a folder on the disk; [ContentRootPath] is the project folder. Thus, [exemples/commun/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css] is served to URL and [/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css]. The case study, on the other hand, places [Bootstrap] in its own folder, [wwwroot].

Let’s check:

curl -i http://localhost:5000/css/styles.css

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 422
Content-Type: text/css

/* a few additional Bootstrap settings */
body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

/* the template's footer */
.pied {
  margin-top: 2rem;
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: #6c757d;
}

/* error messages at the bottom of the page on a light pink background */
.zone-erreur {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef;
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

The file [Views/_ViewStart.cshtml]:

@* exécuté avant chaque vue : toutes les vues utilisent le gabarit _Layout *@
@{
    Layout = "_Layout";
}
  • Line 3: The file [_ViewStart.cshtml] is executed before each view in its folder and subfolders. It sets the [Layout] property: all views use the [_Layout] template, which is searched for in the view’s folder and then in [Views/Shared].

The file [Views/_ViewImports.cshtml]:

@* les Tag Helpers d'ASP.NET Core : des balises HTML "enrichies", comme <partial> *@
@addTagHelper *, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers
@using Exemple15.Controllers
  • Line 2: Enables the Tag Helpers provided by [ASP.NET Core]: HTML tags or attributes processed by the server. The [<partial>] tag is one such example. [*] means “all Tag Helpers in the assembly” [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers];
  • Line 3: The type [Membre] is declared in the controllers namespace.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  @* ViewData["Titre"] : une valeur déposée par la vue, lue par le gabarit *@
  <title>@ViewData["Titre"] - Mon site</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3">
    <partial name="_Navbar" />
    @* la vue demandée par l'action est insérée ici *@
    @RenderBody()
    @* Context : la requête en cours (HttpContext), accessible à toute vue *@
    <footer class="pied">Page [@Context.Request.Path] - © @DateTime.Now.Year</footer>
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • line 7: [ViewData] is a dictionary shared by a view and its template (and by the action, which can also store values in it). The view stores its title there, and the template displays it;
  • lines 8–9: the style sheets, served by [UseStaticFiles];
  • line 13: insertion of the partial view [_Navbar], searched for in the view’s folder and then in [Views/Shared];
  • line 15: the location where [Razor] inserts the view requested by the action;
  • line 17: [Context] is the [HttpContext] object of the current request (see Example 05), accessible to any view: the template displays the requested path without each action having to pass it along.

The file [Views/Shared/_Navbar.cshtml]:

<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">Mon site</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    <a class="nav-link" href="/">Accueil</a>
    <a class="nav-link" href="/equipe">Équipe</a>
    <a class="nav-link" href="/brute">Page sans gabarit</a>
  </div>
</nav>

The file [Views/Shared/_Carte.cshtml]:

@* une "carte" Bootstrap ; son modèle : un Membre (nom, fonction) *@
@model Membre
<div class="card">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">@Model.Nom</h5>
    <p class="card-text">@Model.Fonction</p>
  </div>
</div>

By convention, the name of a partial view or template begins with [_]: these are not complete pages. The partial view [_Carte] has its own template (line 2), a name, and a function. The type [Membre] is declared in the controller. The file [Controllers/PagesController.cs]:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple15.Controllers;

public record Membre(string Nom, string Fonction);

public class PagesController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("/")]
    public IActionResult Accueil()
    {
        return View();
    }

    [HttpGet("equipe")]
    public IActionResult Equipe()
    {
        List<Membre> membres =
        [
            new Membre("Marie Pélissier", "Directrice"),
            new Membre("Jacques Bromard", "Développeur"),
            new Membre("Philippe Jandot", "Graphiste"),
        ];
        return View(membres);
    }

    [HttpGet("brute")]
    public IActionResult Brute()
    {
        return View();
    }
}
  • line 5: the type of team members;
  • line 12: the action [Accueil] has no template: [View()] with no arguments;
  • lines 18–24: the action [Equipe] passes a list of members.

The partial view is used in two ways. The file [Views/Pages/Accueil.cshtml]:

@{
    ViewData["Titre"] = "Accueil";
}
<h1>Bienvenue</h1>
<p>Cette page ne contient que son propre contenu : l'entête, la barre de
  navigation et le pied de page viennent du gabarit <code>_Layout.cshtml</code>.</p>
<partial name="_Carte" model='new Membre("Une vue partielle", "insérée avec un modèle fabriqué sur place")' />
  • line 2: the view places its title in [ViewData], for the template;
  • Line 7: The [model] attribute of the [<partial>] tag provides the template for the partial view: in this case, an object created on the fly. This is a [C#] expression: it is enclosed in apostrophes so that quotation marks can be used within it.

The file [Views/Pages/Equipe.cshtml]:

@model List<Membre>
@{
    ViewData["Titre"] = "Notre équipe";
}
<h1>Notre équipe</h1>
<div class="row g-3">
  @foreach (var membre in Model)
  {
    <div class="col-md-4">
      @* la vue partielle reçoit comme modèle le membre courant *@
      <partial name="_Carte" model="membre" />
    </div>
  }
</div>
  • Line 11: The partial view receives the current loop iteration as its template.

The file [Views/Pages/Brute.cshtml]:

@* Layout = null : cette vue n'utilise pas le gabarit, c'est une page complète *@
@{
    Layout = null;
}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Page brute</title>
</head>
<body>
  <p>Cette page n'utilise pas le gabarit : ni Bootstrap, ni barre de navigation.</p>
  <p><a href="/">Retour à l'accueil</a></p>
</body>
</html>
  • Line 3: Setting [Layout] to [null] in a view cancels the selection of [_ViewStart.cshtml]: The view [Brute] is a complete HTML page. You could also specify a different template ([Layout = "_Autre"]).

The resulting pages, at URL http://localhost:5000/, http://localhost:5000/equipe, and http://localhost:5000/brute:

The template, partial views, and [ViewData] are exactly what the case study uses: a [_Layout.cshtml] template, partial views for the navigation bar, messages, and confirmation windows.

docs.title: 4.4. Example 16: Helpers
docs.text:
A view often requires small formatting functions: formatting a date or a price, capitalizing text, creating a badge HTML... With [Razor], these are simple methods [C#], called within an expression [@]. [ASP.NET Core] also offers Tag Helpers: [C#] code that acts on a HTML tag when the page is rendered.

The [Aides/Formats.cs] file:

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Html;

namespace Exemple16.Aides;

// standard C# functions that can be called from views: @Formats.Monnaie(...)
public static class Formats
{
     // "keyboard" -> "CLAVIER"
    public static string Majuscules(string? texte) => (texte ?? "").ToUpperInvariant();

     // an amount in a currency, formatted according to the current language (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
     // "C" = currency; the object NumberFormatInfo specifies the currency symbol
    public static string Monnaie(decimal montant, string devise = "EUR")
    {
        var format = (NumberFormatInfo)CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.NumberFormat.Clone();
        format.CurrencySymbol = devise == "USD" ? "$" : "€";
        return montant.ToString("C", format);
    }

     // a date written out in full, in the local language: "Wednesday, September 23, 2026"
    public static string Date(DateTime quand) => quand.ToString("D", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture);

     // A helper that generates HTML: it returns IHtmlContent, which Razor does not escape.
     // It is then up to the helper to escape the data it inserts (HtmlEncoder)
    public static IHtmlContent Badge(int stock)
    {
        var classe = stock > 0 ? "text-bg-success" : "text-bg-danger";
        var texte = HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode(stock > 0 ? $"{stock} en stock" : "épuisé");
        return new HtmlString($"<span class=\"badge {classe}\">{texte}</span>");
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 8: a static class—its methods are called without creating an object, [Formats.Majuscules(...)];
  • line 11: capitalization. [ToUpperInvariant] is independent of the user’s language;
  • lines 15–19: an amount in a currency. The format ["C"] ([currency]) formats an amount according to the current locale ([CultureInfo.CurrentCulture]): decimal separator, thousands separator, and currency symbol position. The locale rules are copied ([Clone]) to change the currency symbol;
  • line 23: a date written out in full (format ["D"]), in the language of the current culture;
  • lines 27–31: a helper that generates HTML. The output of a [@] expression is escaped, unless it is a [IHtmlContent]: pre-generated HTML. [HtmlString] is the simplest implementation of this. The helper must then escape the data it inserts into its HTML ([HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode]) itself.

The [TagHelpers/ActifTagHelper.cs] file:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.TagHelpers;

namespace Exemple16.TagHelpers;

// A tag helper: it applies to <a> tags that have the "active" attribute
// <a href="/products" active="/products"> receives the "active" class if the
// current page is under this path
[HtmlTargetElement("a", Attributes = "actif")]
public class ActifTagHelper(IHttpContextAccessor accesseur) : TagHelper
{
     // the value of the attribute `active="..."`
    public string Actif { get; set; } = "";

    public override void Process(TagHelperContext contexte, TagHelperOutput sortie)
    {
        var chemin = accesseur.HttpContext?.Request.Path.Value ?? "/";
        var estActif = Actif == "/" ? chemin == "/" : chemin.StartsWith(Actif, StringComparison.Ordinal);
        if (estActif)
        {
            sortie.AddClass("active", HtmlEncoder.Default); // adds the class to the "class" attribute
        }
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 10: The Tag Helper applies to [<a>] tags that have the [actif] attribute;
  • line 11: a Tag Helper derives from the [TagHelper] class. It is a service: it receives a [IHttpContextAccessor] via injection, which provides access to the current request;
  • line 14: the value of the [actif="..."] attribute is assigned to the property of the same name;
  • Lines 16–22: The method [Process] is called for each relevant tag. If the page path begins with the value of the attribute, the class CSS [active] is added to the tag ([AddClass]). The [actif] attribute itself does not appear in the generated page: the Tag Helper has consumed it.

The file [Program.cs]:

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));
// IHttpContextAccessor: provides access to the current request (used by ActifTagHelper)
builder.Services.AddHttpContextAccessor();

var app = builder.Build();

// a middleware: the formatting language comes from the ?lang=en parameter of URL
app.Use(async (contexte, suite) =>
{
    var langue = contexte.Request.Query["lang"] == "en" ? "en-US" : "fr-FR";
    CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = new CultureInfo(langue);
    await suite(contexte); // control is passed to the following middleware
});

app.UseStaticFiles();
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "commun", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • line 10: registers the [IHttpContextAccessor] service, used by the Tag Helper;
  • lines 15–19: middleware written directly into [Program.cs], executed for each request. It selects the culture based on the [lang] parameter from URL, then passes control to the next middleware ([suite]). This is a simple way to test; the next chapter will cover it better.

The [Views/_ViewImports.cshtml] file:

@addTagHelper *, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers
@* nos propres Tag Helpers, ceux de l'assemblage Exemple16 *@
@addTagHelper *, Exemple16
@using Exemple16.Aides
@using Exemple16.Controllers
  • Line 3: We enable the Tag Helpers for our own project (the [Exemple16] assembly);
  • line 4: views can write [Formats.Monnaie(...)].

The [Views/Shared/_Navbar.cshtml] file:

<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">Helpers</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    @* 1. une condition écrite dans la vue *@
    <a class="nav-link @(Context.Request.Path == "/" ? "active" : "")" href="/">Accueil</a>
    @* 2. notre Tag Helper : l'attribut actif="..." *@
    <a class="nav-link" href="/produits" actif="/produits">Produits</a>
    @* 3. un Tag Helper d'ASP.NET : asp-action fabrique l'URL de l'action *@
    <a class="nav-link" asp-controller="Pages" asp-action="Produits" asp-route-lang="en">Products (en)</a>
  </div>
</nav>
  • Lines 4–5: First way to highlight the current page’s link: a condition written in the view;
  • line 7: second, more concise method: our Tag Helper. This is the one used in the case study;
  • line 9: a Tag Helper for [ASP.NET Core]. The attributes [asp-controller] and [asp-action] denote an action; the Tag Helper calculates its URL based on the routes (here, [/produits]) and writes it to the [href] attribute. [asp-route-lang="en"] adds a parameter, which is placed in URL ([?lang=en]) since the route does not contain a [lang] parameter. If the action’s URL is changed, the link follows suit.

The code HTML in the navigation bar, from URL to [/produits]:

<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">Helpers</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    <a class="nav-link " href="/">Accueil</a>
    <a class="nav-link active" href="/produits">Produits</a>
    <a class="nav-link" href="/produits?lang=en">Products (en)</a>
  </div>
</nav>

The file [Views/Pages/Produits.cshtml]:

@model List<Produit>
@{
    ViewData["Titre"] = "Produits";
}
<h1>Produits</h1>
<table class="table table-sm w-auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Produit</th><th>Prix</th><th>Prix en dollars</th><th>Stock</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    @foreach (var produit in Model)
    {
      <tr>
        <td>@Formats.Majuscules(produit.Nom)</td>
        <td>@Formats.Monnaie(produit.Prix)</td>
        <td>@Formats.Monnaie(produit.Prix, "USD")</td>
        <td>@Formats.Badge(produit.Stock)</td>
      </tr>
    }
  </tbody>
</table>
  • Lines 12–15: The helpers are called within [@] expressions. [Badge] returns HTML, inserted without escaping.

The resulting pages, in French (http://localhost:5000/, http://localhost:5000/produits) and then in English (http://localhost:5000/produits?lang=en):

The prices change format depending on the language: [1 149,90 €] in French, [€1,149.90] in English.

docs.title: 4.5. Example 17: a GET form
docs.text:
A HTML form submitted using the GET method places its fields in the URL. This is the appropriate method for a search: it does not modify anything, and the resulting URL can be bookmarked or shared. The case study uses it to select a doctor and a date.

The [Models/Livre.cs] file:

namespace Exemple17.Models;

public record Livre(string Titre, string Auteur, string Genre);

// the view template: the input (to redisplay it), the categories, and the results
public record RechercheModele(string MotCle, string Genre, string[] Genres, List<Livre> Resultats);
  • Line 6: The view template contains the entered values ([MotCle], [Genre]), so that the form can display them again, along with the list of genres and the results.

The file [Controllers/LivresController.cs]:

using Exemple17.Models;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple17.Controllers;

public class LivresController : Controller
{
    private static readonly List<Livre> Livres =
    [
        new Livre("Le Rouge et le Noir", "Stendhal", "roman"),
        new Livre("Les Fleurs du mal", "Baudelaire", "poésie"),
        new Livre("Madame Bovary", "Flaubert", "roman"),
        new Livre("Alcools", "Apollinaire", "poésie"),
        new Livre("Le Cid", "Corneille", "théâtre"),
    ];

    private static readonly string[] Genres = ["roman", "poésie", "théâtre"];

     // GET / and GET /search?motCle=...&genre=...: the ET form and its results
    [HttpGet("/")]
    [HttpGet("recherche")]
    public IActionResult Recherche(string? motCle, string? genre)
    {
        var mot = (motCle ?? "").Trim().ToLower();
        var resultats = Livres
            .Where(l => mot == "" || l.Titre.ToLower().Contains(mot) || l.Auteur.ToLower().Contains(mot))
            .Where(l => string.IsNullOrEmpty(genre) || l.Genre == genre)
            .ToList();
        return View(new RechercheModele(motCle ?? "", genre ?? "", Genres, resultats));
    }
}
  • lines 8–14: the books, in memory;
  • lines 20–21: two route attributes: the action processes [GET /] and [GET /recherche];
  • Line 22: The parameters [motCle] and [genre] are linked to the parameters of the same name in URL. On the first visit, the form has not yet been submitted: their values are [null];
  • lines 25–28: filtering, using [LINQ]. An empty keyword or an empty category does not filter anything;
  • line 29: the view template.

The file [Views/Livres/Recherche.cshtml]:

@model RechercheModele
<h1 class="h3">Recherche de livres</h1>
@* method="get" : les champs sont envoyés dans l'URL (?motCle=...&genre=...) *@
<form method="get" action="/recherche" class="row g-2 align-items-end mb-3">
  <div class="col-auto">
    <label class="form-label" for="motCle">Titre ou auteur</label>
    @* value="@Model.MotCle" : le champ réaffiche ce qui a été saisi *@
    <input class="form-control" id="motCle" name="motCle" value="@Model.MotCle">
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <label class="form-label" for="genre">Genre</label>
    <select class="form-select" id="genre" name="genre">
      <option value="">(tous)</option>
      @foreach (var genre in Model.Genres)
      {
        @* un attribut booléen : écrit si la condition est vraie, omis sinon *@
        <option value="@genre" selected="@(genre == Model.Genre)">@genre</option>
      }
    </select>
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Rechercher</button>
  </div>
</form>
<p>@Model.Resultats.Count livre(s) trouvé(s).</p>
<ul>
  @foreach (var livre in Model.Resultats)
  {
    <li><i>@livre.Titre</i>, @livre.Auteur (@livre.Genre)</li>
  }
</ul>
  • line 4: [method="get"] and [action="/recherche"]: submitting the form is a [GET /recherche?motCle=...&genre=...] request. The parameter names are the [name] attribute of each field;
  • Line 8: The [value] attribute re-displays the entry;
  • line 17: In the drop-down list, the option corresponding to the selected gender is assigned the attribute [selected]. [Razor] handles Boolean attributes in a specific way: if the value is [true], it writes [selected="selected"]; if it is [false], it does not write the attribute at all. This is exactly what HTML requires, for which the mere presence of the attribute [selected] is sufficient to select the option.

On the first display (http://localhost:5000/), and then after a search:

The address bar shows the parameters that were sent. Accented characters and spaces are encoded there ([%C3%A9]...): this is the URL encoding, which [ASP.NET Core] decodes before the template binding.

docs.title: 4.6. Example 18: Form Fields
docs.text:
Example 18 includes all types of HTML fields: text, password, date, radio buttons, checkboxes, drop-down list, multi-select list, text box, and hidden field. It shows how the server receives them and how the view displays them.

The [Services/ListesService.cs] file:

namespace Exemple18.Services;

public record Pays(string Code, string Nom);

// the lists provided by the form. In a real application, they
// would come from a database: they would be read UNE times at startup,
// since they are the same for all users
public class ListesService
{
    public string[] Titres { get; } = ["Mr", "Mme", "Melle"];

    public Pays[] Pays { get; } =
    [
        new Pays("fr", "France"),
        new Pays("be", "Belgique"),
        new Pays("ch", "Suisse"),
        new Pays("ca", "Canada"),
    ];

    public string[] Loisirs { get; } = ["lecture", "musique", "sport", "cinéma"];

    public string[] Langues { get; } = ["français", "anglais", "espagnol", "allemand"];
}

The lists offered by the form are provided by a service. They are the same for all users: a service instantiated only once (a singleton; see Chapter 6) is the natural place to store them. It is saved in [Program.cs]:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Exemple18.Services;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();
// Razor writes accented characters as-is (not "é");
// < > & " ' remain escaped
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));
// form lists: the same for everyone, a single object (singleton)
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ListesService>();

var app = builder.Build();

// 1. Static files in the wwwroot folder: wwwroot/css/styles.css is served at /css/styles.css
app.UseStaticFiles();
// 2. Bootstrap, shared by the examples: the examples/common/bootstrap folder is served at /bootstrap
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "commun", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • line 12: a single instance of [ListesService], shared by all requests.

The file [Models/Saisie.cs]:

namespace Exemple18.Models;

// what the user entered: the model binding populates each property
// with the field of the same name (for checkboxes, all checked values are included)
public class Saisie
{
    public string? Nom { get; set; }
    public string? MotDePasse { get; set; }
    public string? Commentaire { get; set; }
    public string? Titre { get; set; }
    public string[] Loisirs { get; set; } = [];
    public string? Pays { get; set; }
    public string[] Langues { get; set; } = [];
    public DateOnly? Naissance { get; set; }
    public string? Jeton { get; set; }
}

// an option from a list, and its state (checked / selected)
public record Option(string Valeur, string Libelle, bool Choisie);

// the view template
public class FormulaireModele
{
    public required Saisie Saisie { get; init; }
    public required List<Option> Titres { get; init; }
    public required List<Option> Loisirs { get; init; }
    public required List<Option> Pays { get; init; }
    public required List<Option> Langues { get; init; }
    public string? Recu { get; init; } // what the server received, to display it
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 5–15: the input. The template binding populates each property with the field of the same name. The checkboxes and the drop-down list are arrays ([string[]]): they receive all the values sent (see Example 10). The date of birth is converted to [DateOnly];
  • line 19: an option from a list: its value, its label, and a Boolean indicating whether it is checked or selected;
  • lines 22–29: the view template. The keyword [required] requires that the property be provided when the object is created; [init] prevents it from being modified afterward.

The [Controllers/FormulaireController.cs] file:

using Exemple18.Models;
using Exemple18.Services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple18.Controllers;

[Route("formulaire")]
public class FormulaireController(ListesService listes) : Controller
{
     // GET: the form, with initial values
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Afficher()
    {
        var initial = new Saisie { Titre = "Mme", Pays = "fr", Langues = ["français"], Jeton = "A7X2" };
        return View("Formulaire", Modele(initial, null));
    }

     // POST: the model binding populates [saisie]; the form is redisplayed
    [HttpPost("")]
    public IActionResult Traiter(Saisie saisie)
    {
         // what the browser actually sent, field by field
        var recu = string.Join("\n", Request.Form.Select(c => $"{c.Key} = [{string.Join(", ", c.Value.ToArray())}]"));
        return View("Formulaire", Modele(saisie, recu));
    }

     // the view template: the lists, with each option marked as checked /
     // selected based on the input. The view will then only need to check a Boolean.
    private FormulaireModele Modele(Saisie saisie, string? recu) => new()
    {
        Saisie = saisie,
        Titres = listes.Titres.Select(t => new Option(t, t, t == saisie.Titre)).ToList(),
        Loisirs = listes.Loisirs.Select(l => new Option(l, l, saisie.Loisirs.Contains(l))).ToList(),
        Pays = listes.Pays.Select(p => new Option(p.Code, p.Nom, p.Code == saisie.Pays)).ToList(),
        Langues = listes.Langues.Select(l => new Option(l, l, saisie.Langues.Contains(l))).ToList(),
        Recu = recu,
    };
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 8: the list service is injected;
  • lines 11–15: [GET /formulaire] displays the form with initial values;
  • lines 19–24: [POST /formulaire] receives the user input—populated by the model binding—and redraws the form. [Request.Form] also provides access to the fields as they were submitted: it converts them into text, one line per field, for display;
  • lines 29–36: the view template. For each list, the action calculates which options should be checked or selected: the view will then only need to test a Boolean.

The file [Views/Formulaire/Formulaire.cshtml]:

@model FormulaireModele
<h1 class="h3">Un formulaire complet</h1>
<form method="post" action="/formulaire" style="max-width: 40rem">
  @* champ caché : envoyé avec le formulaire, mais invisible *@
  <input type="hidden" name="jeton" value="@Model.Saisie.Jeton">

  <div class="mb-2">
    <span class="form-label me-3">Titre</span>
    @foreach (var titre in Model.Titres)
    {
      @* boutons radio : même [name], une seule valeur envoyée *@
      <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
        <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="titre" id="titre-@titre.Valeur"
               value="@titre.Valeur" checked="@titre.Choisie">
        <label class="form-check-label" for="titre-@titre.Valeur">@titre.Libelle</label>
      </div>
    }
  </div>

  <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
      <input class="form-control" type="text" id="nom" name="nom" value="@Model.Saisie.Nom">
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="motDePasse">Mot de passe</label>
      @* un mot de passe n'est JAMAIS renvoyé dans la page *@
      <input class="form-control" type="password" id="motDePasse" name="motDePasse">
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
      @* un champ date échange ses valeurs au format aaaa-mm-jj *@
      <input class="form-control" type="date" id="naissance" name="naissance"
             value="@Model.Saisie.Naissance?.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")">
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="mb-2">
    <span class="form-label me-3">Loisirs</span>
    @for (var i = 0; i < Model.Loisirs.Count; i++)
    {
      var loisir = Model.Loisirs[i];
      @* cases à cocher : même [name], plusieurs valeurs possibles *@
      <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
        <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" name="loisirs" id="loisir-@i"
               value="@loisir.Valeur" checked="@loisir.Choisie">
        <label class="form-check-label" for="loisir-@i">@loisir.Libelle</label>
      </div>
    }
  </div>

  <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="pays">Pays</label>
      <select class="form-select" id="pays" name="pays">
        @foreach (var pays in Model.Pays)
        {
          <option value="@pays.Valeur" selected="@pays.Choisie">@pays.Libelle</option>
        }
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="langues">Langues parlées</label>
      @* liste à sélection multiple : plusieurs valeurs possibles *@
      <select class="form-select" id="langues" name="langues" multiple size="4">
        @foreach (var langue in Model.Langues)
        {
          <option value="@langue.Valeur" selected="@langue.Choisie">@langue.Libelle</option>
        }
      </select>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="mb-2">
    <label class="form-label" for="commentaire">Commentaire</label>
    @* une zone de texte : la valeur est ENTRE les balises *@
    <textarea class="form-control" id="commentaire" name="commentaire" rows="2">@Model.Saisie.Commentaire</textarea>
  </div>

  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Envoyer</button>
</form>

@if (Model.Recu is not null)
{
  <h2 class="h5 mt-3">Ce que le serveur a reçu</h2>
  <pre class="bg-light p-2 border">@Model.Recu</pre>
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Line 3: The form is submitted via POST: its fields are included in the request body;
  • Line 5: A hidden field is sent with the form but is not displayed. It is used to pass information from one page to the next (in the case study, for example, it contains the version of a record). Note: The user can modify it;
  • Lines 9–15: Radio buttons share the same [name]; only one can be selected, and only one value is sent. The Boolean attribute [checked="@titre.Choisie"] selects the button (see [selected], Example 17);
  • line 28: a password is never sent back in a page: the field has no [value] attribute;
  • lines 33–34: a date field. The browser displays the date in the user’s format, but always sends and receives [aaaa-mm-jj];
  • lines 40–46: checkboxes with the same [name] attribute: each checked box sends its value; the parameter is therefore repeated;
  • lines 55–60: a drop-down list. The selected option has the attribute [selected];
  • line 65: the [multiple] attribute allows you to select multiple options;
  • line 77: the value of a text field is enclosed within its tags, not in a [value] attribute;
  • Lines 83–86: What the server received, displayed within a [<pre>] tag, which preserves line breaks.

The initial form (http://localhost:5000/formulaire), then after submission:

Note that the text field re-displayed [Bonjour <b>tout</b> le monde] exactly as entered: thanks to the escaping of [@] expressions, the entered tags are not interpreted. The password was received but is not displayed. With [curl], we can see the difference when a checkbox is selected:

curl -d "jeton=A7X2&titre=Mr&nom=Martin&loisirs=sport" http://localhost:5000/form

jeton = [A7X2]
titre = [Mr]
nom = [Martin]
loisirs = [sport]

and two checked boxes:

curl -d "jeton=A7X2&titre=Mr&nom=Martin&loisirs=sport&loisirs=musique" http://localhost:5000/form

jeton = [A7X2]
titre = [Mr]
nom = [Martin]
loisirs = [sport, musique]

(only the content of the [<pre>] tag on the page is reproduced, as displayed by a browser). An unchecked box is not sent at all: [Request.Form] does not contain the field, and the [Loisirs] property of the input retains its initial value—the empty array.

docs.title: 4.7. Example 19: Form Validation
docs.text:
An invalid form must be redisplayed, showing the entered values and a message below each field with an error. Example 19 applies the technique from Example 09 (validation performed by the action, using [ModelState]) to a registration form.

The [Models/InscriptionModele.cs] file:

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

namespace Exemple19.Models;

// form fields and their constraints
public class InscriptionModele
{
     // removes unnecessary spaces from an input (the "setter" is called by the model binding)
    private string? nom;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Le nom est obligatoire.")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.")]
    public string? Nom
    {
        get => nom;
        set => nom = value?.Trim();
    }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "L'adresse électronique est obligatoire.")]
    [EmailAddress(ErrorMessage = "Adresse électronique invalide.")]
    public string? Email { get; set; }

     // anything coming from a form is a string: "42" -> 42
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "L'âge est obligatoire.")]
    [Range(18, 120, ErrorMessage = "L'âge doit être compris entre 18 et 120 ans.")]
    public int? Age { get; set; }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Le mot de passe est obligatoire.")]
    [MinLength(6, ErrorMessage = "Le mot de passe doit comporter au moins 6 caractères.")]
    public string? MotDePasse { get; set; }

     // A rule that applies to DEUX fields: [Compare] compares with MotDePasse
    [Compare(nameof(MotDePasse), ErrorMessage = "La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.")]
    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }
}

// the view template: values to be redisplayed, errors by field
public class FormulaireInscription
{
    public InscriptionModele Valeurs { get; init; } = new();
    public Dictionary<string, string> Erreurs { get; init; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    public bool Html5 { get; init; }
}

// the partial view template _Champ: an input field
public record ChampModele(string Nom, string Libelle, string Type, string? Valeur, string? Erreur, string Attributs);

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 9–16: a property with a private field. Its accessor, [set]—called by the model binding—removes unnecessary spaces from the input: [" Martin "] becomes ["Martin"]. A name consisting solely of spaces is converted to [null] by the model binding itself, and [[Required]] is rejected;
  • line 12: [[MaxLength]] limits the length of a string, just like [[StringLength]];
  • Lines 25–26: The age is converted to an integer and then validated;
  • line 29: at least 6 characters;
  • line 33: the rule “the confirmation matches the password” applies to two fields. The [[Compare]] attribute compares the property it decorates to another property, designated by its name ([nameof(MotDePasse)]: the property name, verified by the compiler);
  • lines 38–42: the view template: the values to be redisplayed, errors sorted by field (a dictionary whose keys are case-insensitive), and a Boolean explained further on;
  • line 46: the partial view template that displays a field.

The file [Controllers/InscriptionController.cs]:

using Exemple19.Models;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple19.Controllers;

[Route("inscription")]
public class InscriptionController : Controller
{
     // ?html5=1: let the browser validate the form before submission
    [HttpGet("")]
