    public IActionResult Afficher(bool html5)
    {
        return View("Inscription", new FormulaireInscription { Html5 = html5 });
    }

    [HttpPost("")]
    public IActionResult Inscrire(InscriptionModele saisie, [FromQuery] bool html5)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
             // Errors by field, to display each message below its corresponding field
            var erreurs = ModelState
                .Where(c => c.Value!.Errors.Count > 0)
                .ToDictionary(c => c.Key, c => c.Value!.Errors[0].ErrorMessage, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
             // RÉAFFICHE the form: entered values (except passwords),
             // and a message below each field with an error
            saisie.MotDePasse = saisie.Confirmation = null;
            ViewData["Erreur"] = "Le formulaire contient des erreurs.";
            return View("Inscription", new FormulaireInscription { Valeurs = saisie, Erreurs = erreurs, Html5 = html5 });
        }
        return View("Bienvenue", saisie);
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 11–13: the empty form. The parameter [html5] will be explained later;
  • Line 17: The template link populates [saisie] using the form fields and validates it. [[FromQuery]] retrieves [html5] from URL;
  • Lines 19–24: If there are errors, they are organized by field. A field may violate multiple constraints: only the first error message ([Errors[0]]) is retained;
  • lines 27–29: The form is redisplayed: the entered values (except passwords), errors by field, and a general message, stored in [ViewData] for the template;
  • line 31: otherwise, the welcome page, with the converted values (age is a number, the name has been cleaned up).

A conversion error (an age [abc]) generates an English message by default: [The value 'abc' is not valid for Age.] (see example 08). The file [Program.cs] replaces it:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(options =>
{
     // error messages from CONVERSION (e.g., age "abc"), in English by default
    var messages = options.ModelBindingMessageProvider;
    messages.SetAttemptedValueIsInvalidAccessor((valeur, champ) => $"La valeur [{valeur}] n'est pas valide.");
    messages.SetValueMustNotBeNullAccessor(champ => "Ce champ est obligatoire.");
});
// Razor writes accented characters as-is (not "é");
// < > & " ' remain escaped
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));

var app = builder.Build();

// 1. Static files in the wwwroot folder: wwwroot/css/styles.css is served at /css/styles.css
app.UseStaticFiles();
// 2. Bootstrap, shared by the examples: the examples/common/bootstrap folder is served at /bootstrap
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "commun", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • Lines 6–11: The messages for template-linking errors are provided by the [ModelBindingMessageProvider] object from the options of MVC. Each method in [Set...Accessor] replaces one of these with a function that generates the message. [SetAttemptedValueIsInvalidAccessor] handles a value that cannot be converted; it receives the value and the field name. The case study thus replaces all of these messages.

The fields are all built using the same model: a partial view factors them out. The file [Views/Shared/_Champ.cshtml]:

@* un champ de saisie ; son modèle : nom, libellé, type, valeur, erreur, et les
   attributs de validation HTML5 (required, maxlength...) *@
@model ChampModele
<div class="mb-2">
  <label class="form-label" for="@Model.Nom">@Model.Libelle</label>
  <input class="form-control @(Model.Erreur is null ? "" : "is-invalid")" id="@Model.Nom" name="@Model.Nom"
         type="@Model.Type" value="@Model.Valeur" @Html.Raw(Model.Attributs)>
  @if (Model.Erreur is not null)
  {
    <div class="invalid-feedback">@Model.Erreur</div>
  }
</div>
  • line 6: the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid] highlights an invalid field in red;
  • line 7: the validation attributes HTML5 are passed as parameters and inserted without escaping ([Html.Raw]): they are written by the developer, not entered by the user;
  • line 10: the error message, below the field (class [Bootstrap] [invalid-feedback]).

The file [Views/Inscription/Inscription.cshtml]:

@model FormulaireInscription
@{
     // an error in a field, or null
    string? Erreur(string champ) => Model.Erreurs.GetValueOrDefault(champ);
}
<h1 class="h3">Inscription</h1>
@if (Model.Html5)
{
  <p>Validation par le navigateur <b>activée</b> - <a href="/inscription">la désactiver</a></p>
}
else
{
  <p>Validation par le navigateur <b>désactivée</b> - <a href="/inscription?html5=true">l'activer</a></p>
}
@* novalidate : le navigateur ignore les attributs required, min... et
   envoie le formulaire tel quel ; seul le serveur valide *@
<form method="post" action="/inscription@(Model.Html5 ? "?html5=true" : "")" novalidate="@(!Model.Html5)">
  <partial name="_Champ" model='new ChampModele("nom", "Nom", "text", Model.Valeurs.Nom, Erreur("nom"), "required maxlength=\"20\"")' />
  <partial name="_Champ" model='new ChampModele("email", "Adresse électronique", "email", Model.Valeurs.Email, Erreur("email"), "required")' />
  <partial name="_Champ" model='new ChampModele("age", "Âge", "number", Model.Valeurs.Age?.ToString(), Erreur("age"), "required min=\"18\" max=\"120\"")' />
  <partial name="_Champ" model='new ChampModele("motDePasse", "Mot de passe", "password", null, Erreur("motDePasse"), "required minlength=\"6\"")' />
  <partial name="_Champ" model='new ChampModele("confirmation", "Confirmation", "password", null, Erreur("confirmation"), "required")' />
  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">S'inscrire</button>
</form>
  • line 4: a local function [C#], declared in the block [@{ }]: it returns the error for a field, or [null];
  • line 17: the Boolean attribute [novalidate] is set when [Html5] is false;
  • Lines 18–22: Each field is an insertion from the partial view, using a template generated on the fly.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inscription</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
    @RenderBody()
    @* l'erreur globale, en bas de page, sur fond rose léger ;
       ViewData["Erreur"] est déposée par l'action *@
    @if (ViewData["Erreur"] is string erreur)
    {
      <div class="zone-erreur" role="alert">@erreur</div>
    }
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • lines 14–16: the global message is displayed at the bottom of the page on a light pink background (class [zone-erreur] derived from [wwwroot/css/styles.css]), as in the case study. [is string erreur] checks the value's type and stores it in a variable.

Let’s submit the form (http://localhost:5000/inscription) with several errors:

docs.title: 4.7.1. Validation by the browser
docs.text:
The attributes [required], [maxlength], [min], [max], [type="email"]... instruct the browser to validate the form before submitting it: the user is immediately notified via a tooltip, without any round-trip communication with the server. This is the behavior achieved by clicking the “Enable” link (http://localhost:5000/inscription?html5=true), which removes the [novalidate] attribute from the form.

This validation is a convenience, not a security measure: you can bypass it simply by removing the [required] attribute using the browser’s developer tools, or by sending the request with [curl]. Server-side validation remains essential. That’s why the example disables browser validation by default: to demonstrate how the server works. The case study, however, retains both: the HTML5 attribute for convenience, and server-side validation for security.

docs.title: 4.8. Example 20: The Post/Redirect/Get Pattern
docs.text:
When a POST form submits successfully, the action can display a page directly. The problem arises if the user then refreshes that page (F5 key): the browser resubmits the form, and the operation is performed a second time (an order placed twice, an appointment made twice...). The Post / Redirect / Get pattern (PRG) prevents this problem: a successful POST action does not generate a page; instead, it redirects to a GET page. Reloading this page simply triggers another GET, with no effect.

One detail remains: the GET page must display a message (“the task has been added”), even though this message was generated by the POST action in a different request. To address this, [ASP.NET Core] provides [TempData]: a dictionary whose contents persist until the next request and disappear as soon as they are read. It is a flash message. By default, [TempData] is stored in a cookie, encrypted by the server.

The file [Services/TachesService.cs]:

namespace Exemple20.Services;

// the task list, in memory, shared by all (singleton)
public class TachesService
{
    private readonly List<string> taches = ["Lire le chapitre 3"];

    public IReadOnlyList<string> Liste() => taches;

    public void Ajouter(string libelle) => taches.Add(libelle);
}

The [Controllers/TachesController.cs] file:

using Exemple20.Services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple20.Controllers;

[Route("taches")]
public class TachesController(TachesService taches) : Controller
{
     // GET /tasks: the list and the form for adding tasks
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Afficher()
    {
        return View("Taches", taches.Liste());
    }

     // POST /tasks: the Post/Redirect/Get pattern
    [HttpPost("")]
    public IActionResult Ajouter(string? libelle)
    {
        var texte = (libelle ?? "").Trim();
        if (texte == "" || texte.Length > 40)
        {
             // Invalid input: the page is reloaded without redirection
            ViewData["Libelle"] = libelle;
            ViewData["Erreur"] = "Le libellé doit comporter de 1 à 40 caractères.";
            return View("Taches", taches.Liste());
        }
        taches.Ajouter(texte);
         // TempData: a message that will persist after the redirect, for the request SUIVANTE
        TempData["Flash"] = $"La tâche [{texte}] a été ajoutée.";
         // No page: a redirect to the page GET
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(Afficher));
    }

     // POST /tasks/no-program: the counterexample (a page in response to POST)
    [HttpPost("sans-prg")]
    public IActionResult AjouterSansPrg(string? libelle)
    {
        taches.Ajouter(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(libelle) ? "(sans titre)" : libelle.Trim());
        ViewData["SansPrg"] = true;
        return View("Taches", taches.Liste());
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 11–13: the list page;
  • lines 21–26: an invalid entry: the page is reloaded (no redirection—the entry and error message must be retained);
  • lines 28–32: a valid input: the operation, the message flashes in [TempData], then a 302 redirect to the [Afficher] action. [RedirectToAction] calculates the URL for the action based on its route (see Example 04). [nameof(Afficher)] is the method name, which is validated by the compiler;
  • lines 36–41: the counterexample, for comparison.

The file [Views/Taches/Taches.cshtml]:

@model IReadOnlyList<string>
<h1 class="h3">Mes tâches</h1>
<ol>
  @foreach (var tache in Model)
  {
    <li>@tache</li>
  }
</ol>
<form method="post" action="/taches" class="d-flex gap-2">
  <input class="form-control" name="libelle" value="@ViewData["Libelle"]" placeholder="Nouvelle tâche">
  <button class="btn btn-primary text-nowrap" type="submit">Ajouter</button>
  @* formaction : ce bouton envoie le MÊME formulaire à une autre adresse *@
  <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary text-nowrap" type="submit" formaction="/taches/sans-prg">Ajouter sans PRG</button>
</form>
@if (ViewData["SansPrg"] is true)
{
  <p class="text-danger mt-2">Page affichée en réponse à un POST : appuyez sur F5 et la tâche sera ajoutée une seconde fois.</p>
}
  • line 13: the [formaction] attribute of a button submits the form to a different address than the one specified by the form’s [action] attribute. The form thus has two buttons, which trigger two different actions. The case study uses this approach on its login page.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Tâches</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
    @* le message flash, en haut de page : le LIRE l'efface de TempData *@
    @if (TempData["Flash"] is string flash)
    {
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">@flash</div>
    }
    @RenderBody()
    @if (ViewData["Erreur"] is string erreur)
    {
      <div class="zone-erreur" role="alert">@erreur</div>
    }
  </div>
</body>
</html>

The flash message is displayed at the top of the page (lines 12–14), and the error message at the bottom (lines 17–19). Reading [TempData["Flash"]] marks the value as consumed: it is cleared at the end of the request.

Here is what [curl] sees when the form is successfully submitted. The [-c fichier] option saves the received cookies, [-b fichier] sends them back; [--data-urlencode] encodes spaces and accents in the field:

curl -i -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt --data-urlencode "libelle=Réviser ASP.NET" http://localhost:5000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Content-Length: 0
Location: /taches
Set-Cookie: .AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider=CfDJ8B0oe7_4_ZJHlxaqeCPfd4UeD0...; path=/; samesite=lax; httponly

The response is a redirect, with the cookie [.AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider], which contains the encrypted flash message (its value, which is very long, has been truncated). The next request sends the cookie; the response deletes it (expiration date in the past):

curl -i -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://localhost:5000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Set-Cookie: .AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; path=/; samesite=lax; httponly

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Tâches</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">La tâche [Réviser ASP.NET] a été ajoutée.</div>
    <h1 class="h3">Mes tâches</h1>
<ol>
    <li>Lire le chapitre 3</li>
    <li>Réviser ASP.NET</li>
</ol>
<form method="post" action="/taches" class="d-flex gap-2">
  <input class="form-control" name="libelle" placeholder="Nouvelle tâche">
  <button class="btn btn-primary text-nowrap" type="submit">Ajouter</button>
  <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary text-nowrap" type="submit" formaction="/taches/sans-prg">Ajouter sans PRG</button>
</form>

  </div>
</body>
</html>

In the browser (http://localhost:5000/taches), after adding a task:

The address bar displays [/taches]: this is the page GET. You can safely reload it; the message disappears. An empty entry:

And the counterexample:

Here, reloading the page triggers a browser warning (“Confirm form submission”), then adds the task a second time. All POST forms in the case study follow the PRG pattern.

docs.title: 4.9. Example 21: Links, Buttons, and Confirmation
docs.text:
A simple rule guides the choice between a link and a button:

  • a link ([<a href>]) generates a GET request. A GET request must not modify anything: browsers, search engines, and antivirus programs may follow links on their own to prepare or analyze a page;
  • an operation that modifies data (add, edit, delete, log out) is a button in a form POST.

Example 21 manages a list of contacts: you can view a contact by clicking a link and delete it by clicking a button, which opens a confirmation window. The files for this example:

21-liens-boutons/
├── Controllers/
│   └── ContactsController.cs
├── Services/
│   └── ContactsService.cs
├── Views/
│   ├── Contacts/
│   │   ├── Fiche.cshtml
│   │   └── Liste.cshtml
│   ├── Shared/
│   │   ├── _Confirmation.cshtml
│   │   └── _Layout.cshtml
│   ├── _ViewImports.cshtml
│   └── _ViewStart.cshtml
├── wwwroot/
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── styles.css
│   └── js/
│       └── app.js
├── appsettings.json
├── Exemple21.csproj
└── Program.cs

The [Services/ContactsService.cs] file:

namespace Exemple21.Services;

// a contact: an ID, a name, a phone number
public record Contact(int Id, string Nom, string Telephone);

// contacts, in memory, shared by all (singleton)
public class ContactsService
{
    private readonly List<Contact> contacts =
    [
        new(1, "Marie Durand", "01 23 45 67 89"),
        new(2, "Paul Martin", "06 12 34 56 78"),
        new(3, "Philippe Jandot", "02 98 76 54 32"),
    ];
    private int dernierId = 3;

    public IReadOnlyList<Contact> Liste() => contacts;

     // null if the contact does not exist
    public Contact? Lire(int id) => contacts.Find(c => c.Id == id);

    public Contact? Modifier(int id, string nom, string telephone)
    {
        var index = contacts.FindIndex(c => c.Id == id);
        if (index < 0) return null;
         // A record is immutable: it is replaced with a modified copy (with)
        contacts[index] = contacts[index] with { Nom = nom, Telephone = telephone };
        return contacts[index];
    }

    public Contact Ajouter(string nom, string telephone)
    {
        var contact = new Contact(++dernierId, nom, telephone);
        contacts.Add(contact);
        return contact;
    }

    public Contact? Supprimer(int id)
    {
        var contact = Lire(id);
        if (contact is not null) contacts.Remove(contact);
        return contact;
    }
}
  • Line 4: a contact;
  • line 20: [Find] returns [null] if no contact has that ID;
  • lines 22–28: a [record] is immutable: its properties are not modified; instead, it is replaced with a modified copy. The expression [with { ... }] creates this copy;
  • lines 31–35: [++dernierId] increments the counter before using it: the identifiers are 4, 5...

The file [Controllers/ContactsController.cs]:

using Exemple21.Services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Exemple21.Controllers;

[Route("contacts")]
public class ContactsController(ContactsService contacts) : Controller
{
     // a LIEN (<a href>): a GET query, which does not modify anything
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Liste()
    {
        return View(contacts.Liste());
    }

    [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
    public IActionResult Fiche(int id)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Lire(id);
        return contact is null ? NotFound() : View(contact);
    }

     // a BOUTON in a POST form: a request that modifies data
    [HttpPost("{id:int}")]
    public IActionResult Enregistrer(int id, string nom, string telephone)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Modifier(id, nom, telephone);
        if (contact is null) return NotFound();
        TempData["Flash"] = $"Le contact [{contact.Nom}] a été modifié.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(Liste));
    }

     // same form, different button (formaction attribute): different action
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/dupliquer")]
    public IActionResult Dupliquer(int id, string nom, string telephone)
    {
        var copie = contacts.Ajouter($"{nom} (copie)", telephone);
        TempData["Flash"] = $"Le contact [{copie.Nom}] a été créé.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(Liste));
    }

    [HttpPost("{id:int}/supprimer")]
    public IActionResult Supprimer(int id)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Supprimer(id);
        if (contact is null) return NotFound();
        TempData["Flash"] = $"Le contact [{contact.Nom}] a été supprimé.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(Liste));
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 11–20: the two pages: the list and the contact detail page. The route constraint [:int] (see Example 02) only accepts an integer identifier; a nonexistent contact results in a 404 error;
  • lines 24–30: saving a record, using PRG;
  • lines 34–39: duplication, triggered by a second button on the same form (attribute [formaction]);
  • lines 42–48: deletion, using POST.

docs.title: 4.9.1. The confirmation window
docs.text:
The browser dialog box ([window.confirm]) cannot be formatted or translated: its buttons remain in the browser’s language. It is replaced by a [Bootstrap] window, embedded in the page and hidden until needed. The [Views/Shared/_Confirmation.cshtml] file:

@* une seule fenêtre pour toute la page, cachée (d-none) au départ *@
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">Non, revenir</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">Oui, confirmer</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 2: the [d-none] class hides the window;
  • line 3: the gray background;
  • line 11: the question’s position;
  • lines 14–15: the two buttons, identified by the [data-action] attribute.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

  • line 18: the window is present on all pages;
  • line 20: the script is loaded at the bottom of the page; when it runs, the elements it looks for already exist. It is served by [UseStaticFiles] from [wwwroot/js/app.js].

A small portion of [JavaScript] links the forms to the window. The file [wwwroot/js/app.js]:

// Confirmation for forms with the data-confirmation="..." attribute
// Without JavaScript, these forms are simply submitted without confirmation.
(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  let enAttente = null; // the form to submit if confirmation is given

   // 1. We intercept the submission of forms requiring confirmation
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault(); // The submission is suspended
      enAttente = formulaire;
      message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
      modale.classList.remove('d-none'); // the window appears
    });
  });

   // 2. The two buttons in the window
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      enAttente.submit(); // Submit, SANS Trigger the 'submit' event again
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      modale.classList.add('d-none');
      enAttente = null;
    }
  });
})();
  • line 3: the code is wrapped in a function that executes immediately, to avoid creating global variables;
  • lines 9–14: the submission of each form bearing the attribute [data-confirmation] is intercepted. [preventDefault()] suspends the submission; the form is stored, the question is placed in the window ([textContent], not [innerHTML]: the question is displayed as text, never interpreted as HTML), and the window is displayed;
  • Lines 19–25: “Yes” submits the cached form. The [submit()] method of a form submits it without triggering the [submit] event: there is no new confirmation prompt. “No” hides the window.

If [JavaScript] is disabled, the forms simply submit without confirmation: the application still works. This is the principle of incremental improvement: [JavaScript] adds convenience, but it is not essential. The case study follows this principle (its script, [wwwroot/js/app.js], adds keyboard handling: the Esc key and focus). The resulting pages, generated from http://localhost:5000/contacts: the list, the confirmation prompt, the list after deletion, and a contact’s profile:

Finally, we verify that deletion cannot be triggered by a query GET:

curl -i http://localhost:5000/contacts/2/delete

HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Content-Length: 0
Allow: POST

The path exists, but not for the GET method: [ASP.NET Core] returns [405 Method Not Allowed], and the [Allow] header indicates the accepted method. With POST:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:5000/contacts/2/delete
